B. Braun Medical Inc., a leader in infusion therapy and pain management, develops, manufactures, and markets innovative medical products and services to the healthcare industry. Other key product areas include nutrition, pharmacy admixture and compounding, ostomy and wound care, and dialysis. The company is committed to eliminating preventable treatment errors and enhancing patient, clinician and environmental safety. B. Braun Medical is headquartered in Bethlehem, Pa., and is part of the B. Braun Group of Companies in the U.S., which includes B. Braun Interventional Systems, Aesculap® and CAPS®.

Globally, the B. Braun Group of Companies employs more than 64,000 employees in 64 countries. Guided by its Sharing Expertise® philosophy, B. Braun continuously exchanges knowledge with customers, partners and clinicians to address the critical issues of improving care and lowering costs. To learn more about B. Braun Medical, visit www.bbraunusa.com

Ready to lead where science, quality, and patient safety come together? Join B. Braun and shape the future of laboratory excellence while driving the strategy, compliance, and innovation behind critical healthcare products.

**Why this role matters:**

The Director, Lab Quality Control serves as the senior site authority for Quality Control Chemistry and Microbiology, providing the scientific and operational leadership needed to protect product quality and maintain regulatory compliance. This role establishes the site’s laboratory strategy, leads critical quality initiatives, and ensures that laboratory operations remain scientifically sound, inspection-ready, and aligned with business and product portfolio requirements.

**How you will make an impact:**

* Develop, maintain, and execute the site Quality Control strategy in alignment with business objectives, product portfolio requirements, and regulatory expectations.
* Provide strategic oversight for QC Chemistry and QC Microbiology operations, including release, stability, raw material, in-process, microbiological, and sterility-related testing activities.
* Establish and govern laboratory standards for testing compliance, data integrity, investigations, sample management, analytical methods, specifications, and laboratory workflows.
* Serve as the primary site subject matter expert during regulatory inspections and customer audits involving laboratory operations and quality systems.
* Partner with Quality Assurance, Manufacturing, Sterility Assurance, Engineering, Validation, Technical Services, Supply Chain, and Regulatory Affairs to support site operations and timely product release.
* Lead laboratory optimization, method modernization, automation, Lean deployment, and quality system improvement initiatives.
* Foster a culture of quality, accountability, scientific rigor, collaboration, safety, and continuous improvement.

**What sets you up for success:**

* Bachelor’s degree in a STEM discipline required; master’s degree or doctorate preferred.
* 10+ years of related experience, including significant leadership responsibility within laboratory quality control or pharmaceutical manufacturing.
* Demonstrated expertise in QC Chemistry and/or QC Microbiology operations within a sterile drug product manufacturing environment.
* Significant experience with laboratory compliance, data integrity, out-of-specification and out-of-trend investigations, analytical methods, and pharmaceutical quality systems.
* Proven experience supporting regulatory inspections, customer audits, and interactions with senior internal and external stakeholders.
* Ability to resolve complex scientific, operational, and compliance issues using sound judgment, technical expertise, and risk-based decision-making.
* Lean Six Sigma certification or demonstrated experience applying Lean and continuous-improvement methodologies preferred.

**What you will enjoy along the way:**

* The opportunity to shape the laboratory quality strategy for a regulated sterile pharmaceutical manufacturing site.
* A highly visible leadership role with influence across Quality, Manufacturing, Technical Operations, Supply Chain, and Regulatory Affairs.
* The ability to modernize analytical capabilities through automation, method lifecycle management, Lean principles, and emerging technologies.
* Responsibility for developing laboratory leaders, building organizational capability, and determining the effective allocation of people and resources.
* Meaningful work that directly supports product quality, regulatory compliance, operational reliability, and patient safety.
* A collaborative environment built on scientific rigor, accountability, diverse perspectives, and continuous improvement.

role.title: Director, United States Operations Quality Audits & Inspections
role.description:
Facility: Quality

Location:
Plainsboro, NJ, US

**About the Department**

 

The Clinical, Medical and Regulatory (CMR) department at Novo Nordisk is one of the most diverse and collaborative groups within the organization. From healthcare provider interactions and developing and implementing regulatory strategies with the FDA to providing medical education and collecting data to support efficacy and new product development, CMR is involved. The one thing that keeps us all marching to the same beat is our patient centered focus. At Novo Nordisk, you will help patients around the world. As their needs evolve, so does our challenge to find better and more innovative ways to improve their quality of life. We’re changing lives for a living. Are you ready to make a difference?

 

**The Position**

Lead independent, risk-based quality audits and inspection readiness across the approved USO Quality (USOQ) domain. Develop and execute the audit and self-inspection strategy to assess compliance, control effectiveness and risks to patient safety, product quality and data integrity across applicable current GxPs [Good Clinical (GCP), Pharmacovigilance (GPV), Distribution (GDP) and Manufacturing (GMP)] practices]. Maintain an objective view of business and Quality activities, including outsourced activities within scope. Lead sustained audit and inspection readiness and act as the designated local health authority inspection point of contact and inspection lead for the USOQ domain, coordinating with Regulatory Affairs, Global Quality, Patient Safety and accountable business leaders. Ensure readiness gaps and regulatory commitments are visible, owned, and escalated. Provide independent assurance over external-party quality controls through risk-based audits & remediation plans.

 

**Relationships**

Position reports to the Head of USO Quality. The sponsor approves the audit charter and risk-based plan, reviews resource adequacy, receives unfiltered findings and has formal input into the Director’s appointment, removal and performance assessment. The Director has direct access to the sponsor to escalate interference, disputed findings, scope restrictions and unresolved material risks. Interface with multiple Novo accountable business leaders, Regulatory Affairs, Legal, Safety, global Quality Audit and Global Clinical Compliance. External relationships include health authorities, clinical trial sites, external auditors and relevant vendors and partners. Coordinate USOQ inspection communications through approved authority channels without displacing global, legal-entity, Regulatory or Safety accountabilities. This role manages the independent audit and inspection department, with multiple experienced quality representatives assigned to diverse quality functions and includes auditor competence, inspection leadership, workload, budget and continuity.

 

**Essential Functions**

* Direct Independent Audits and Self-Inspection Program & Staff
* Maintain the USOQ audit charter, audit universe and risk-based audit and self-inspection strategy. Define scope, frequency, methods, auditor qualifications and escalation criteria across business functions, Quality verticals and relevant external parties. Secure approval of audit plans and material changes, ensure authorized access to personnel, sites, systems and records and align with global audit programs to prevent duplication and coverage gaps
* Lead the annual audit & self-inspection program, including routine, risk-triggered and for-cause reviews. Assign qualified, independent auditors; oversee evidence-based assessments of control design, effectiveness, data integrity and external-party controls. Ensure consistent finding classification, clear communication and timely reporting. Manage budget and staffing, document plan deviations and escalate material coverage or resource gaps
* Inspection Readiness and Health Authority Leadership
* Lead inspection readiness with business and Quality leaders through assessments, mock inspections, playbooks, document-retrieval exercises, SME preparation and trained deputies. Define inspection-team roles, front- and back-room responsibilities, request tracking and escalation. Coordinate USOQ administrative support while leading readiness coordination and independent challenge. Business and process owners retain responsibility for compliant operations, source records and readiness evidence
* Serve as the designated local health authority inspection contact and lead within approved USOQ scope, including FDA and other formally assigned authorities. Coordinate inspection logistics, meetings, interviews, requests and communications with Regulatory Affairs, global functions and accountable SMEs. Lead observation triage, response coordination and commitment tracking. Secure authorized approvals for submissions, commitments and risk acceptance; retain established company signatory, Regulatory and Safety reporting authorities
* Finding Ownership and Remediation Oversight
* Ensure all audit, self-inspection and inspection findings have accountable business or process owners, action owners, deadlines and escalation routes. Business leaders assign ownership and resources; finding owners investigate root causes, develop and implement CAPA and demonstrate effectiveness. Quality owns findings within its processes. Challenge inadequate responses and escalate unassigned, overdue, repeat or high-risk findings to the Head of USOQ and Corporate Quality Audit Sponsor, as appropriate. Honor health authority deadlines
* Independently assess audit and self-inspection responses and verify remediation effectiveness before closing findings under approved procedures. Require additional evidence or action where needed. For inspection observations, coordinate completion and effectiveness checks while preserving authorized response approvals and health authority closure decisions. Reviewers must not assess their own remediation; finding owners retain investigation, CAPA development and implementation
* Report audit themes, inspection readiness, overdue commitments and systemic risks to the Quality Council and relevant global forums. Escalate urgent risks immediately and independence concerns directly to the Corporate Quality Audit Sponsor
* Independence and Performance
* Protect audit objectivity through a documented charter, conflict disclosures, independent assignments and unfiltered reporting. Base conclusions on evidence, free from business or delivery pressures; escalate classification disputes through approved independent channels. Do not operate or approve controls the team audits; arrange independent review of its readiness and inspection-coordination activities. Track risk-based coverage, reporting and regulatory-response timeliness, readiness-gap closure, overdue and repeat findings, CAPA effectiveness and auditor competence. Do not incentivize low finding counts or guarantee inspection outcomes.
 

**Physical Requirements**

10-20% overnight travel required. This position (in-office) is located in Plainsboro, NJ.

 

**Development Of People**

Supervisory. Ensure that reporting personnel have individual development plans (IDP), with annual goals and measurements that are consistent with the priorities of the business and that interim reviews are held so that their work is focused on those priorities and they understand their level of accountability for results and the measurement process. Ensure that the IDP forms include completed learning and aspiration plans and are in place for all reporting personnel to enable the achievement of goals and capability to assume increased levels of responsibility. Manage the application and communication of all Novo Nordisk policies, procedures and Novo Nordisk Way.

 

**Qualifications**

* **Education level:** Bachelor’s degree required. Advanced degree preferred; advanced degree may substitute for 2 years of experience
* **Experience Level:** 10+ years of progressive experience in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or CRO industry, including at least 5 years in GxP Quality Assurance, Compliance, or related functions, and 5 years in people leadership or leading complex cross-functional quality initiatives. Demonstrated experience in commercial/affiliate quality, pharmacovigilance quality, regulatory inspections, and pharmaceutical Quality Management Systems (QMS). Broader GDP/GMP experience preferred.
* **Specific or technical job skills:** Deep expertise in GxP and FDA inspections; working knowledge of GPV/GDP/GMP/GCP and other requirements applicable to commercial & post-marketing operations. role.description:
Job Description
 
 
Position Overview
 
 
Quality Lead, Director– QMS & Digital Quality Governance Analytical
 
Global Quality Management Systems
 
 
The Global Quality Group within our Company Manufacturing Division is seeking an experienced transformation lead in the capacity of Director– Quality Management Systems (QMS) & Digital Quality Governance, to provide strategic and operational leadership for the QMS workstream within a complex, enterprise-level laboratory transformation program.
 
 
This role is accountable for architecting, modernizing, and deploying a modernized, digitized Quality Management System tailored to support next-generation QC testing, end-to-end analytical digitization, instrumentation innovation, and laboratory automation.
 
 
The QMS Quality Lead will oversee the harmonization and evolution of quality processes—including deviation management, investigations, CAPA, change control, risk management (ICH Q9), and computerized systems validation (CSV/CSA)—to ensure seamless integration with modern automated laboratory workflows, LIMS, ELN, and digital data pipelines. In close partnership with the program leadership team, Site Quality heads, Analytical Development, Digital/IT Quality, and Regulatory Compliance, the incumbent will ensure that innovative operational models maintain rigorous compliance with global health authority regulations while driving efficiency, inspection readiness, and continuous improvement.
 
 
Key Responsibilities and Requirements
 
The ideal candidate will combine deep technical expertise in global Quality Management Systems with a forward-thinking innovation mindset, translating digital and automated laboratory advancements into agile, compliant, and sustainable QMS frameworks.
 
 

* Strategic QMS Architecture & Modernization: Define, lead, and execute the QMS integration strategy for the lab transformation initiative, ensuring core quality processes (Change Control, OOS/OOE/OOT investigations, Deviations, CAPA, Method Transfer/Validation, and Batch Release support) are optimized, digitized, and natively integrated with automated laboratory systems
* Coding Experience: Experience and understanding on how coding translates to QMS and analytical functions. Responsible for overseeing the eQMS and ability to be able to review and understand the underlying code and how it is ensures compliance.
* Digital Quality & Data Integrity Governance: Partner with IT/Digital Quality and Automation engineers to embed robust Data Integrity by Design (ALCOA+) and Computer Software Assurance (CSA) principles into digitized laboratory platforms, instrument interfaces, and automated data flows.
* Regulatory Compliance & Inspection Readiness: Ensure all modernized QMS processes, policies, and standard operating procedures (SOPs) comply with global cGMP regulations (FDA 21 CFR Part 11/210/211, EU Annex 11, ICH Q9/Q10, WHO). Drive inspection readiness strategies and author/review corresponding regulatory briefing documents and filing sections.
* Matrixed Program Leadership & Governance: Direct the QMS workstream governance forum, actively tracking milestone execution, interdependencies, risks, and critical paths. Provide regular data-driven progress updates, risk assessments, and escalation pathways to the Overall Quality Lead and executive steering bodies.
* Change Management & Operational Transition: Drive human-centered change management and training initiatives to support site-level and global QC laboratory adoption of digitized quality workflows, fostering a strong culture of quality and transformation agent mindset.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Serve as the central quality authority across laboratory operations, technology development, computerized systems validation, and regulatory affairs, eliminating silos and resolving complex compliance roadblocks.
* People Leadership & Oversight: Supervise and mentor quality specialists, compliance leads, and external consultants supporting QMS transformation, maintaining high standards of technical rigor, accountability, and development.

Required Experience
 
 

* Education: Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Pharmacy, Engineering, Life Sciences, or related discipline required; advanced degree (Master’s, PhD, PharmD, or MBA) strongly preferred.
* Experience: 10+ to 15+ years of progressive experience in pharmaceutical/biopharmaceutical quality operations, quality systems, or compliance within a cGMP manufacturing and QC laboratory environment.
* Quality Systems Expertise: Proven track record in designing, optimizing, and overseeing enterprise-level QMS processes (Deviations, Investigations, CAPA, Change Control, Out of Specification, and Quality Risk Management) in laboratories subject to global health authority inspections (e.g., FDA, EMA, PMDA).
* Digital & Laboratory Systems Acumen: In-depth knowledge of laboratory digital ecosystems, including LIMS, ELN, CDS, SDMS, automated instrumentation, and their integration into enterprise QMS platforms (e.g., TrackWise, Veeva Vault QMS).
* Validation & Compliance Mastery: Strong understanding of Data Integrity expectations, 21 CFR Part 11, EU Annex 11, and modern risk-based validation methodologies (GAMP 5, Computer Software Assurance).
* Governance & Program Execution: Demonstrated success leading large-scale cross-functional workstreams, setting project milestones, proactively managing risk registers, and driving accountable execution.
* Communication & Influencing: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to present technical compliance strategies effectively to executive sponsors, auditors, and technical teams.

Preferred Experience
 
 

* Direct experience leading or supporting QMS transformation initiatives (e.g., transition from paper/hybrid to end-to-end digitized paperless QC environments).
* Working knowledge of automated testing platforms, robotics, or continuous manufacturing/testing control frameworks.
* Experience with global health authority inspections, pre-approval inspections (PAIs), and authoring QMS/Quality sections for regulatory dossiers (NDA, BLA, MAA).
* Practical application of Lean / Six Sigma methodologies to streamline quality workflows and cycle times.
* Programming experience is an asset, and or strong demonstrated ability to quickly learn.
* Experience supporting enterprise workforce strategy, technology evaluation, or transition initiatives.
* Experience managing external third party service providers, software vendors, and implementation partners in regulated environments.

**Required Skills:** 
Analytical Development, Cross-Functional Leadership, Digital Transformation, Enterprise Transformation, Executive Communications, GMP Compliance, Laboratory Quality Control, Project Governance, Quality Management Systems (QMS), Regulatory Strategies
 
 
**Preferred Skills:** 
Analytical Testing, Change Leadership, Program Governance

role.title: Director of Quality
role.description:
**Company Overview**

Red 6 is an innovative Augmented Reality (AR) technology startup leading the way in synthetic air combat training. Our primary technology, supporting our ATARS product, enables pilots to simulate the cognitive challenges of flying while accessing realistic, scalable training in dynamic outdoor environments.

**Director of Quality**

Lead Red 6 into a scalable aerospace product organization.

Red 6 develops advanced augmented reality capabilities for aerospace and defense applications. We seek a hands-on, strategic Director of Quality to lead the next phase of our evolution into disciplined, repeatable product qualification and production. This leader will strengthen existing foundations while guiding the processes, evidence, and behaviors needed to meet customer, regulatory, safety, and aerospace industry expectations.

Success requires more than maintaining certifications. The Director will embed quality planning into product development, improve manufacturing and supplier readiness, and create a culture in which teams jointly solve problems before they become defects, delays, or compliance findings. Key results are building practical, auditable quality processes with Quality as a trusted partner across Engineering, Operations, Programs, and the supplier base.

**WHAT YOU WILL LEAD**

* Own the enterprise Quality strategy and roadmap, scaling the Quality Management System (QMS) to match product maturity, production volume, and customer commitments.
* Maintain and continuously improve AS9100 certification and audit readiness. Lead management reviews, internal audits, corrective action effectiveness, risk based thinking, and process ownership.
* Lead ISO 45001 occupational health and safety management system maturation and certification readiness, in coordination with accountable safety and operations leaders.
* Deploy practical Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP) disciplines aligned to AS9145 where applicable, including quality planning, process flow, PFMEA, control plans, measurement system analysis, first article inspection, and production readiness reviews.
* Integrate Quality into design inputs, reviews, verification and validation, configuration control, design changes, manufacturing transitions, and product release criteria.
* Establish scalable document and record controls, product pedigree, serial level traceability, inspection and test evidence, nonconformance controls, material review, CAPA, and calibration systems.
* Develop supplier qualification, surveillance, performance scorecards, supplier corrective actions, and risk based oversight of contract manufacturers and critical suppliers.
* Partner with Engineering and Operations to strengthen hardware quality, reliability, manufacturability, process validation, FOD/ESD controls, and handling of nonconforming material.
* Improve the connection between Windchill PLM, Epsilon3 MES, Unanet ERP, and existing compliance tools to support controlled, usable, auditable data across design, build, and delivery.
* Lead customer quality engagement, audits, contractual quality deliverables, and coordination with defense and aerospace stakeholders as applicable.

**LEAD A COLLABORATIVE QUALITY CULTURE**

* Build a capable Quality team with clear roles, coaching, succession planning, and cross functional influence.
* Act as a constructive partner to Engineering. Translate standards and contractual obligations into design intent, risk, and measurable acceptance criteria rather than relying on clause citations alone.
* Distinguish nonnegotiable compliance outcomes from implementation choices. Invite Engineering and Operations to co-design efficient solutions.
* Create early quality engagement in program planning and design reviews. Resolve disagreements using evidence, risk, cost, schedule, and accountable decision ownership.
* Establish shared performance measures and a regular Quality–Engineering working cadence to reduce late surprises and unproductive escalation.
* Promote a just, learning oriented culture that encourages timely issue reporting, root cause analysis, and effective preventive action.

**QUALIFICATIONS REQUIRED**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.
* Significant progressive aerospace or defense quality leadership experience, including building or scaling an AS9100 QMS and leading certification or surveillance audits.
* Demonstrated success moving products from prototype or development environments into qualified, controlled, repeatable production.
* Working knowledge of APQP per AS9145, AS9102 first article inspection, supplier quality, configuration management, CAPA, and risk based process control.
* Ability to influence senior technical leaders without defaulting to authority or unnecessary bureaucracy. Strong facilitation, coaching, and conflict resolution skills.
* Experience with customer and supplier quality requirements, quality metrics, and cross functional improvement programs.

* Ability to work on site in Denver and travel periodically to suppliers and other Red 6 locations.
* Must be US Citizen to have the ability to obtain and maintain a DoD Security Clearance.

**PREFERRED EXPERIENCE**

* ISO 45001 implementation or certification leadership; AS9115 awareness for deliverable software where relevant.
* DoD prime contractor interfaces, DCMA, DFARS, and applicable government customer quality requirements.
* Experience with PLM, MES, ERP, and integrated digital quality workflows, especially Windchill, Epsilon3, and Unanet.
* Lean Six Sigma, ASQ quality credentials, GD&T, hardware reliability, and complex electromechanical systems.
* Experience developing small teams into mature, business enabling quality organizations.

**WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE IN THE FIRST 12 MONTHS**

* Publish an agreed risk based Quality maturity roadmap with clear process owners and milestones.
* Sustain AS9100 compliance and close systemic audit or corrective action gaps with evidence of effectiveness.
* Introduce an appropriate APQP and production readiness framework for priority product lines.
* Improve supplier quality visibility, product traceability, and readiness of controlled manufacturing documentation.
* Demonstrate stronger Quality–Engineering collaboration through earlier issue resolution and fewer late stage quality surprises.
* Provide leadership with a concise scorecard covering escapes, rework, supplier performance, CAPA aging, audit findings, and readiness milestones.

Estimated Base Salary range dependent on skills and experience: $175,000 to $195,000

**Full-Time Employee Benefits**

* Healthcare, Dental, and Vision (100% coverage for Employees)
* Paid time off, including vacation, sick, paid holidays, and parental leave
* Short and Long-Term Disability
* Flexible Spending Account (FSA)
* 401(k) Retirement Plan
* Voluntary Worksite Benefits (Accident, Critical Illness, and Hospital Indemnity)
* May be eligible for a discretionary annual bonus based on individual and company performance, subject to plan terms.

**Note**

Red 6 reserves the right to change its current benefits program at any time, in a manner that is consistent with applicable federal and state regulations.

Red 6 has the right to change any and all terms of this job description, including, but not limited to, job responsibilities, qualifications, and benefits. Nothing in this job description constitutes an offer or guarantee of employment.

role.title: Director, Balance of Plant
role.description:
**Company Overview**

Kairos Power is a new nuclear energy technology and engineering company whose mission is to enable the world's transition to clean energy, with the ultimate goal to dramatically improve people's quality of life while protecting the environment. This goal will be accomplished through the commercialization of the fluoride-salt-cooled, high-temperature reactor (FHR) that can be deployed with robust safety, affordable costs, and flexible operation to accommodate the expansion of variable renewables.

**Job Summary**

Kairos Power is seeking an experienced senior engineering leader to serve as Director, Balance of Plant (Power Generation System & Turbine Island), to provide strategic and technical leadership for multidisciplinary engineering teams. This role is responsible for the technical leadership, organizational capability, and execution of the engineering teams responsible for design and deployment for Structures, Systems, and Components that convert thermal energy to electricity and provide auxiliary plant functions necessary to support reliable and efficient plant operation. The ideal candidate combines broad power plant and thermal-fluid systems expertise with demonstrated success building engineering teams, working with external partners, and delivering complex, hardware systems from concept through commissioning and operation.

**Responsibilities**

* Provide strategic and technical leadership for the development and integration of balance-of-plant (BOP) Systems, such as the Heat Transport Systems interfacing with high-temperature steam Rankine cycles, Power Generation System (PGS), and auxiliary systems such as service water, treated water, and compressed air systems.
* Establish department technical direction and decision boundaries consistent with company strategy and designated technical authorities.
* Lead engineering delivery from conceptual sizing through detailed design, vendor package review, and commissioning support, owning design reviews and technical risk.
* Ensures that system and discipline leads satisfy applicable requirements, codes and standards, safety functions,and align to program
* Ensure engineering deliverables—including requirements, calculations, analyses, specifications, drawings, design reports, interface documents, and test plans—are technically sound and meet established quality and schedule requirements.
* Oversee supplier technical execution, including supplier selection, bid evaluations, equipment specifications, design reviews, technical evaluations, qualification programs, factory acceptance testing, and resolution of supplier technical issues, to ensure supplier designs and deliverables meet Kairos Power requirements.
* Oversee evaluation of BOP design and supplier changes for impacts on system interfaces, plant performance, safety, and commissioning readiness, and ensure approved changes are incorporated into the controlled technical baseline.
* Build productive relationships with external organizations while maintaining clear accountability for Kairos Power technical requirements and engineering decisions.
* Translates company strategy into measurable organizational priorities and decision principles.
* Determine and communicate explicit scope, schedule, risk, and resource tradeoffs across the organization.
* Maintain accountability for organizational outcomes and the consequences of scope, schedule, risk, and resource decisions within delegated authority, including decisions delegated to others.
* Ensure execution of strategic priorities, take corrective action when results are off track, and remove systemic barriers teams cannot resolve.
* Establish organizational technical direction and decision boundaries are established, consistent with company strategy and designated technical authorities.
* Ensure material technical and safety risk, their potential consequences, and proposed mitigations are clearly documented and communicated to the appropriate authority, with risk acceptance decisions explicitly recorded.
* Personally engage in mission-critical technical or organizational decisions, crises, external reviews, or critical deliverables when judgment materially changes the outcome.
* Build the organization and leadership pipeline required for current and future strategy, including recruitment, staffing, and leadership development.
* Hold senior leaders and technical leads accountable for team capability, succession, performance, engagement, and retention.
* Ensure systemic operational or compliance weaknesses are corrected and that improvements are sustained across the organization.
* Communicate organizational direction and tradeoffs consistently to leadership, teams, and cross-functional partners.
* Establish alignment across teams, resolve cross-functional conflicts, and escalate tradeoffs that require broader leadership decisions.
* Set the organizational tone for accountability, integrity, psychological safety, and mission stewardship, and reinforce these values through visible decisions, resource choices, recognition, and corrective action.
* Other duties as assigned.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree or higher in Mechanical Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or equivalent
* 15+ years of progressively responsible engineering experience involving power generation, thermal-fluid systems, process systems, nuclear systems, or other complex industrial systems.
* 7+years of progressive engineering leadership experience managing engineering teams with multiple engineering disciplines.
* Experience managing engineering managers or technical leads with accountability for outcomes across multiple teams and work sites.
* Experience working with suppliers, OEMs, engineering contractors, or other external technical organizations.
* Experience leading technical development and qualification of major equipment through external suppliers or OEMs.
* Experience supporting construction, commissioning, startup, or operation of complex power generation or industrial facilities.
* Experience with integrated power plant systems, including modern high-temperature steam Rankine cycles and the interactions between heat transport, power conversion, auxiliary systems, and plant infrastructure.
* Strong systems thinking with the ability to identify and resolve technical issues that cross traditional engineering and organizational boundaries.
* Lead and support recruitment and staffing requirements of group.
* Proactive, organized, adaptable, and able to thrive in fast-paced, multi-tasked environments.

**Knowledge, Skills & Abilities**

* Knowledge of integrated power plant architecture, thermal-fluid systems, power generation systems, auxiliary systems, major plant equipment, and their interfaces, including familiarity with various steam generator technologies such as Heat Recovery Steam Generators and molten salt steam generators.
* Knowledge of equipment procurement, supplier engineering, manufacturing, testing, installation, commissioning, and lifecycle considerations associated with complex industrial systems.
* Skill in leading and developing multidisciplinary engineering organizations and holding teams accountable for technical and execution outcomes.
* Skill in translating program objectives into engineering strategies, priorities, resource plans, and measurable commitments.
* Skill in technical decision-making, trade studies, risk assessment, problem solving, and resolution of complex cross-system issues.
* Ability to establish clear accountability while empowering managers, technical leads, and responsible engineers to make decisions at the appropriate organizational level.
* Ability to operate effectively in a first-of-a-kind environment characterized by technical uncertainty, evolving requirements, and competing priorities.
* Ability to communicate complex technical issues, uncertainties, risks, and tradeoffs to technical and nontechnical stakeholders to support informed decisions.

**Physical Demands**

* Remaining in a stationary position, often standing, or sitting for prolonged periods
* Moving about to accomplish tasks or moving from one worksite to another
* Repetitive assembly operations of manufacturing test fixtures and test setups in collaboration with engineering and manufacturing teams
* Communicating with others to exchange information

**Environmental Conditions**

* General office environment
* Assessing the accuracy, neatness and thoroughness of the work assigned
* High-concentration, demanding and fast-paced
* Prototyping/Test Environments
* Manufacturing/Industrial Environments

**Safety and PPE**

* Reading and interpreting hazardous warning signs
* Reporting issues with equipment or unsafe conditions
* Wearing proper personal protective equipment (PPE), to include face mask, face shields, gloves, safety shoes, and other PPE as required

**Travel**

* Some travel may be required (up to 25%)

**Additional Requirements**

* Occasionally requires working weekends
* Occasionally requires schedule flexibility
* Occasionally requires extended hours to support launch and critical project timelines

#LI-Remote

**About our Benefits**

We know that we have some of the most talented and dedicated employees, and we believe in rewarding them accordingly. If you work here, full-time employees (excludes interns) expect to have access to the benefits below:

* Competitive compensation packages
* Medical, dental and vision benefits for employees and their dependents
* Paid Vacation
* 401(k) and pre-tax health insurance, dependent care, and commuter benefits (FSA)

Kairos Power is committed to building a diverse workforce that reflects the communities where we do business. Kairos Power is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status. We actively welcome people of different experiences, abilities, and perspectives.

Kairos Power participates in E-Verify.

Candidates only, no recruiters or agencies please.

Note: You are applying for a position that is located in a facility that handles information that is subject to export control restrictions by the Department of Energy under 10 CFR Part 810. To work in this facility, you need to be authorized by the Department of Energy to access Part 810-controlled information. Foreign nationals who are citizens of countries that are not on the Department of Energy's general authorization list (link below) are not permitted to work in our facility unless the Department of Energy issues an export control license to the company to permit that individual to have access to Part 810-controlled information. The following questions are intended to determine the licensing requirements that may apply. https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/10/appendix-A\_to\_part\_810

role.title: Plant Manager
role.description:
R10104082 Plant Manager (Open)

Location:

Carnegie, PA

**How will you CONTRIBUTE and GROW?**
-------------------------------------

We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace that embraces the unique perspectives of our employees, our customers, patients, community stakeholders, and cultures across the world. We believe that a variety of backgrounds makes our team stronger and more innovative.

**At Airgas, we RESPECT, HONOR and VALUE diversity.**
=====================================================

 

**Airgas is Hiring for a Plant Manager in Carnegie, PA**
========================================================

 

***We are looking for you !***

 

* **Comprehensive Family Benefits:** Airgas offers a full benefits package designed to support your whole life, including Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, AD&D, and Disability Insurance.
* **Support for Parents:** We offer a 14-week paid child birth benefit to support growing families.
* **Future Security:** 401(k) Retirement Plan with company match, Tuition Assistance, Paid Holidays, Vacation, and Sick time.
* **Early Access:** Your benefits start after just 30 days of employment.

 

The Plant Manager is responsible for leading and empowering the team engaged in producing and repackaging of compressed and liquid gases into cylinders, correcting unsafe acts or conditions without delay, and aligning daily responsibilities with team members according to customer needs, current stock levels and team strengths.

* Ensures the safe operation and maintenance of the plant for pumping or repackaging of gases into cylinders while ensuring compliance with all federal, state, local and company policies, procedures, regulations and laws. Maintains a neat, clean and orderly plant appearance.
* Studies production schedules and estimates team-hour requirements for completion of job assignments. Establishes and/or adjusts work procedures collaboratively to meet production schedules.
* Partners with the team to enhance production methods, equipment performance, and product quality. Adapts workflows and use of equipment to support team productivity and well-being.
* Ensures all safety rules are strictly observed and safety training is regularly scheduled, conducted and documented. Interpret company policies to team members and foster a culture of safety adherence.
* Ensures all injuries and accidents are properly investigated and reported within 24 hours.
* Analyzes and resolves, or partners with team members in solving, work related problems. Supports career growth, internal movement, and constructive performance management. Ensures associate issues, grievances, etc. are effectively handled.
* Mentors and guides operational leaders to cultivate effective leadership. Design collaborative initiatives to inspire and engage the team to achieve goals. Provides coaching and corrective action promptly, to ensure that team members receiving feedback are supported to meet shared performance goals.
* Onboards new team members and supports cross-functional learning to continue production during personnel shortages.
* Maintains time and production records and approves overtime when essential, while keeping overtime at acceptable levels.
* Collaborates with outside sales to ensure order accuracy and properly scheduled customer deliveries by Airgas trucks.
* Monitors SAP reports daily such as open order/delivery reports, billing and delivery block reports and open Purchase Order (PO) reports.
* Oversees employee development in procedural areas such as following all Airgas Standard Operating Procedures (SOPS) and safety regulations.
* Run recurring orders for the next day's deliveries.
* Route all the trucks and PGI tickets.
* Complete Daily Cycle Counts.

**\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_**
----------------------------------------------------

**Are you a MATCH?**
--------------------

**Required Qualifications**

* High School Diploma or GED
* A total of five (5) years of industry experience to include a minimum of two (2) years of demonstrated experience working in a supervisory/leadership role. Prefer prior experience with compressed/packaged gases.

**Prefered Qualifications**

* Bachelor's Degree
* Prior experience utilizing SAP preferred.
* Intermediate knowledge of Google suite applications
* Strong analytical skills and a thorough understanding of how to leverage metrics and related tools to improve production efficiency and effectiveness.
* Excellent oral and written communication skills. Communication skills that ensure a smooth flow of information between self and others through clear speaking and writing, encouragement of open expression of ideas, and effective listening.

* Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to deal effectively with others in both favorable and unfavorable situations regardless of status of position. Accepts cultural diversity and establishes effective working relationships.
* Demonstrated knowledge of addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division in all units of measure using whole numbers, fractions and decimals. Ability to compute rate, ratios, and percent.

* Lives by Airgas safety programs, OSHA, and all related rules, regulations, procedures which are applicable to this position’s responsibilities

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

**Benefits**

We care about and support our Airgas Families. This is evident not only through our competitive compensation but also through a comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, and vision plans, short-term and long-term disability, life and accidental death and dismemberment (AD&D) insurance, Employee Assistance Program (EAP), pre-tax commuter transportation benefit, parental leave, vacation, sick time, floating holidays, jury duty and funeral/bereavement leave, and paid holidays for all eligible full-time employees.

Additionally, we offer our eligible employees a 401k plan with company matching funds, tuition reimbursement, discounted college tuition for eligible employees’ dependents, and an Airgas Scholarship Program for dependent children.

Associates who are members of collective bargaining units should review their bargaining agreement to determine whether they are eligible for some or all of the benefits described here and to see any special terms or conditions for eligibility.

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

**Your DIFFERENCES enhance our PERFORMANCE**

At Airgas, we are committed to building a workplace that embraces the diversity of our employees, our customers, patients, community stakeholders and cultures across the world.

We welcome and consider applications from all qualified applicants, regardless of their race, gender, sexual orientation, religion, disability or any other protected characteristic. We strongly believe a diverse organization opens up opportunities for people to express their talent, both individually and collectively and it helps foster our ability to innovate by living our fundamentals, acting for our success and creating an engaging environment in a changing world.

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

**About Airgas**

Airgas, an Air Liquide company, is a leading U.S. supplier of industrial, medical and specialty gases, as well as hardgoods and related products; one of the largest U.S. suppliers of safety products; and a leading U.S. supplier of ammonia products and process chemicals. Through the passion and diversity of its 18,000 associates, Airgas fosters a culture of safety, customer success, sustainability and innovation. Airgas associates are empowered to share ideas, take initiative and make decisions.

Airgas is a subsidiary of Air Liquide, a world leader in gases, technologies and services for industry and healthcare. Present in 60 countries with approximately 66,500 employees, Air Liquide serves more than 4 million customers and patients.

Join us for a stimulating experience: At Airgas, you matter and so does the work you do. As a member of our team, you play an important role in the success of your team, making sure our products are created sustainably and delivered safely and efficiently. In turn, you’ll find a welcoming workplace where you’re valued for who you are and where you can fill your potential while growing a fulfilling career — whatever path you choose.

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

**Equal Employment Opportunity Information**

We are an equal opportunity employer. We welcome all qualified applicants regardless of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic.

Airgas, an Air Liquide Company is a Government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans’ Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974 and Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973.

Airgas does not discriminate against qualified applicants with disabilities, and is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to the known disabilities of such individuals so as to ensure equal access to benefits and privileges of employment. If you are an individual with a disability and would like to request a reasonable accommodation as part of the employment selection process, please contact us by email at us-accommodationrequest@airgas.com.

Description:

Join Amrize as a Plant Manager - Aggregate and help construct what's next. If you're ready to put your skills to work on projects that matter — and build a career with a company that’s building North America — we want to hear from you!

 

**ABOUT THE ROLE**

The basic function of the Plant Manager is to provide the necessary leadership to plan, direct, organize, coordinate and control the mining of raw materials and the production of shippable product at the assigned Plant in a manner to meet Aggregate Dispatcher requests on a timely and cost efficient basis. The Plant Manager will be tasked with ensuring that an appropriate quality product is made at the Plant.

The Plant Manager will ensure proper staffing and monitoring of the inventory status at the Plant and in addition will coordinate activities with the following departments: Aggregate Operations Department - Dispatch, Maintenance, and Quality Control of the Region in addition Regional Administration/Financial function.

The Plant Manager will analyze and monitor production efficiency / productivity to ensure the Company is fully utilizing on site vehicles and plant equipment at the assigned location. In addition, the Plant Manager will develop mining and production strategies and tactics to ensure an approach to raise productivity levels, maintaining safety as a top propriety, while controlling the costs of the assigned location.

 

**WHAT YOU'LL ACCOMPLISH**

* Consistently identify new operational opportunities and develop strategies for accomplishing the attainment of improved efficiency and productivity.
* Address the needs of the customer while at the same time promoting and protecting the long-term interests of the Company.
* Initiate and implement production and scheduling related programs, strategies and techniques that result in increased productivity, and maintain safe operations of the assigned Plant, while containing the budgeted expenses of the assigned plants.
* Manage the performances of subordinate personnel, work independently, meet deadlines and manage the assigned Plant with fiscal integrity.
* Delegate responsibilities; must be able to objectively evaluate the performance of subordinates; and must be able to hold others accountable in a constructive manner.
* Participate in Company safety inspections.
* Communicate with site crew which includes plant operator, loader operators and laborers
* Supervise team to maintain production and efficiency. Schedule production and execute preventative maintenance routines
* Maintain sufficient inventory levels at site to service customers’ needs
* Coordinate safety issues and investigate incidents with safety department. Ensure environmental compliance, rehabilitation and meeting permit obligations
* Demonstrate a commitment to communicating, improving and adhering to health, safety and environmental policies in all work environments and areas. Promote a culture of safety and exhibit these behaviors.
 

**WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR**

**Education:** Bachelor's degree

**Field of Study Preferred:** Mining Engineering, Management
 
**Required Work Experience**: 5-7 years Aggregate Mining and related Raw Materials Plant Production experience

**Required Technical Skills:** Computer proficiency required. SAP experience would be a plus

 

**Additional Requirements:**

* Successful candidates must adhere to all safety protocols and proper use of Amrize approved Personal Protection Equipment ("PPE"), including but not limited to respirators. Subject to applicable law, employees that are required to wear respirators must be clean shaven where the respirator seal meets the face in order to pass the qualitative and quantitative fit tests.

* Paid time off & paid holidays
* Paid Parental Leave (maternity & paternity)

role.title: Plant Manager/ CDL Mixer Operator - Ready Mix Concrete
role.description:
About the Opportunity:

We are seeking a hands-on Plant Manager / CDL Mixer Operator to oversee the daily operations of our ready mix concrete plant while also operating a concrete mixer truck as business demands require. This is a working management position ideal for someone who enjoys leading a team, maintaining efficient plant operations, and providing excellent customer service in the field.

The successful candidate will ensure safe, efficient production and delivery of quality concrete while maintaining high standards for customer service, equipment maintenance, and regulatory compliance.

Your Mission & Key Responsibilities:

* ### **Plant Operations**

 + Oversee daily batching and production of ready mix concrete.
 + Schedule production and deliveries to meet customer needs.
 + Supervise plant employees and coordinate daily work assignments.
 + Monitor inventory of cement, aggregates, admixtures, and other materials.
 + Ensure quality control standards are maintained.
 + Coordinate equipment maintenance and repairs to minimize downtime.
 + Maintain a clean, organized, and safe plant environment.
 + Ensure compliance with OSHA, DOT, environmental, and company safety policies.
 + Complete production reports and maintain accurate operational records.

 ### **CDL Mixer Operations**

 + Operate a ready mix concrete mixer truck (Class A or Class B CDL) when needed.
 + Safely transport and deliver concrete to commercial and residential job sites.
 + Perform pre-trip and post-trip vehicle inspections.
 + Maintain delivery documentation and DOT compliance.
 + Communicate effectively with dispatch, customers, and job site personnel.
 + Assist with plant and yard duties during downtime.

What Sets You Apart:

* Valid Class A or Class B CDL with current DOT Medical Card required.
* Previous ready mix concrete plant management or supervisory experience preferred.
* Experience operating a concrete mixer truck.
* Knowledge of batching systems and concrete production.
* Strong leadership and organizational skills.
* Excellent customer service and communication abilities.
* Commitment to safety and regulatory compliance.
* Mechanical aptitude with the ability to identify and troubleshoot equipment issues.
* Ability to work outdoors in varying weather conditions.
* Ability to climb ladders, lift up to 100 pounds, and perform physical job duties as needed.

About SRM:

SRM Concrete (Smyrna Ready Mix) is a family-owned, values-driven leader in the ready mix concrete industry. Founded in 1999 with a single plant in Smyrna, Tennessee, we’ve grown to over 600 locations nationwide by focusing on quality, integrity, and service. Our mission is to serve our customers, our communities, and our team members with excellence—every load, every day.Why Join SRM Concrete?

**Why Join SRM Concrete?**

* **Growth & Advancement:** Be part of a rapidly expanding company with real opportunities to grow your career.
* **Impact:** Lead a team that plays a pivotal role in building America’s future.
* **Competitive Pay & Exceptional Benefits:** Low-cost medical, dental, vision, STD, LTD, and life insurance; paid holidays; PTO/vacation; 401k with $100 weekly match; family days; and more!
* **Team Culture:** We value hard work, respect, and teamwork. We support each other, recognize a job well done, and believe in doing what’s right—on the job and in the community. You’ll find a straightforward, dependable environment where every team member matters.

At SRM Concrete, you’re more than a manager—you’re a valued team member helping to build America’s future. If you’re ready to say “YES” to new opportunities and deliver service that sets the standard in our industry, apply today and join the SRM family!

role.title: Plant Manager
role.description:
**Lead Operations. Build Teams. Drive Growth.**

Are you a hands-on operations leader who thrives on building high-performing teams, improving processes, and delivering results? UFP Factory Built is looking for a Plant Manager to lead one of our manufacturing facilities and play a key role in the success of our growing business.

 

As a Plant Manager, you'll have the opportunity to run the operation like it's your own, leading production, safety, quality, inventory, maintenance, and team development while making a direct impact on profitability and customer satisfaction. This is an ideal role for a leader who enjoys solving problems, developing people, and creating a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.

**About UFP Factory Built**

UFP Factory Built, a division of UFP Industries, supplies structural components and engineered solutions for manufactured housing, modular construction, RV, and cargo trailer manufacturers throughout North America. We are part of a stable, growth-oriented organization with a strong reputation for investing in our people and promoting from within.

 

### **What You'll Do**

* Lead all day-to-day plant operations, ensuring safety, quality, productivity, and profitability goals are achieved.
* Build, mentor, and develop a high-performing team of supervisors and production employees.
* Drive operational excellence through process improvements, waste reduction, and efficiency initiatives.
* Manage production scheduling, inventory levels, shipping activities, and resource planning.
* Monitor key performance metrics and take action to improve throughput, quality, and financial results.
* Partner with leadership on capital investments, facility improvements, and business growth initiatives.
* Foster a culture centered around safety, employee engagement, accountability, and continuous improvement.
* Ensure compliance with company policies, OSHA standards, and all applicable regulations.
Oversee maintenance programs to maximize equipment reliability and minimize downtime. 

 

### **What We're Looking For**

* Experience leading manufacturing, production, operations, or industrial teams.
* Proven ability to motivate employees, develop talent, and drive results.
* Strong business acumen with experience managing budgets, costs, and operational metrics.
* Ability to identify opportunities, solve problems, and implement effective solutions.
* Experience with inventory management, production scheduling, and process improvement.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office, including Excel, Word, and Outlook.
Forklift certification or willingness to obtain certification. 

 

### **Why Join UFP?**

* Opportunity to lead and influence all aspects of a manufacturing operation.
* High visibility and direct impact on business performance.
* Stable and growing company with a strong national footprint.
* Collaborative culture that values leadership, innovation, and accountability.
* Career advancement opportunities within UFP Industries.
Competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits package. 

 

### **What Success Looks Like**

In this role, you'll build a safe, efficient, and engaged operation, develop future leaders, improve plant performance, and help position the facility for continued growth. You'll have the autonomy to make decisions, the support of an experienced leadership team, and the opportunity to leave a lasting impact on the business.

 

**If you're a driven operations leader looking to take ownership of a facility, develop teams, and grow your career with an industry leader, we'd love to hear from you.**

**Benefits** **currently offered to our employees:**

* Medical Insurance
* Health Savings Account with Company Contribution
* Dental Insurance
* Vision Insurance
* Basic and Voluntary Life Insurance
* Disability Insurance
* 401(k) plan with Company Match
* Paid Vacation and Holidays
* Stock Purchase Program with Employee Discount
* Education Reimbursement
* Wellness Programs and Challenges
Other Supplemental Benefits 

*The Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer.*

Ensures the highest standards of environmental safety and operational excellence by effectively managing the day-to-day operations of the assigned MRF and maintains cost management within the MRF. 
 
**II. Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

* Ensures smooth operation of site, including: gatehouse, sorting, loading.

* Continually works to reduce turnaround time for trucks in and out of site.

Leadership experience in a manufacturing or similar environment

role.title: Plant Manager - Ready Mix Concrete - Bowling Green KY
role.description:
About the Opportunity:

Are you a proven leader who thrives on building strong teams and delivering exceptional service? At SRM Concrete, our Plant Managers are the driving force behind our commitment to operational excellence and customer satisfaction. As a Plant Manager, you’ll lead by example—empowering your team, optimizing daily operations, and ensuring every load meets the highest standards of safety, quality, and service.

If you’re passionate about leadership, logistics, and making a positive impact in your community, this is your opportunity to join a company that values integrity, teamwork, and growth.

Your Mission & Key Responsibilities:

* Lead with purpose: Inspire, coach, and develop your plant team to achieve operational excellence and deliver outstanding service to every customer.
* Oversee daily plant operations: Manage staff scheduling, load planning, and route optimization to ensure efficient and timely concrete deliveries.
* Champion customer service: Collaborate with drivers, dispatch, and sales teams to exceed customer expectations and resolve any issues with urgency and care.
* Drive performance: Implement and monitor key metrics to assess plant efficiency, productivity, and service quality.
* Foster a culture of safety: Ensure full compliance with safety regulations and company policies, creating a safe and positive work environment for all.
* Promote teamwork: Conduct regular meetings to review performance, address challenges, and celebrate successes.
* Build relationships: Develop strong connections with customers, suppliers, and SRM team members to support seamless operations.
* Contribute to growth: Participate in strategic planning and budgeting, sharing insights to enhance plant efficiency and profitability.

What Sets You Apart:

* Inspirational leadership style with a passion for developing high-performing teams.
* Commitment to delivering exceptional customer service and building lasting relationships.
* Strong organizational and problem-solving skills; able to prioritize and adapt in a fast-paced environment.
* Deep understanding of logistics, supply chain management, or plant operations—experience in the concrete or construction industry is highly valued.
* Proficiency with dispatch software, Microsoft Office Suite, and a willingness to learn new systems.
* Knowledge of DOT regulations and safety standards for transportation and delivery.
* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills; you build trust with team members, customers, and partners.
* Dedication to safety, quality, and continuous improvement.
* Willingness to undergo SRM’s pre-employment screenings.

About SRM:

SRM Concrete (Smyrna Ready Mix) is a family-owned, values-driven leader in the ready mix concrete industry. Founded in 1999 with a single plant in Smyrna, Tennessee, we’ve grown to over 600 locations nationwide by focusing on quality, integrity, and service. Our mission is to serve our customers, our communities, and our team members with excellence—every load, every day.Why Join SRM Concrete?

**Why Join SRM Concrete?**

* **Growth & Advancement:** Be part of a rapidly expanding company with real opportunities to grow your career.
* **Impact:** Lead a team that plays a pivotal role in building America’s future.
* **Competitive Pay & Exceptional Benefits:** Low-cost medical, dental, vision, STD, LTD, and life insurance; paid holidays; PTO/vacation; 401k with $100 weekly match; family days; and more!
* **Team Culture:** We value hard work, respect, and teamwork. We support each other, recognize a job well done, and believe in doing what’s right—on the job and in the community. You’ll find a straightforward, dependable environment where every team member matters.

At SRM Concrete, you’re more than a manager—you’re a valued team member helping to build America’s future. If you’re ready to say “YES” to new opportunities and deliver service that sets the standard in our industry, apply today and join the SRM family!

role.title: Plant Manager
role.description:
**PURPOSE:**

* Supervise the production of donated and new goods, assuring all personnel are properly trained in all areas of the production process.
* Maintain production standards and quotas for supplying all agency stores with saleable merchandise.
* Maintain inventory production records.

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

Coordinates the following:

* Trains production associates to develop proficiency in providing proper classification of donated material and new goods.
* Evaluates the performance of workers and makes recommendations for changes if necessary.
* Monitor quality of processed clothing, wares, shoes, purses, books, etc. by spot checking racks and totes being distributed to stores. Monitor processed clothing for damage due to improper tagging.
* Monitor processed clothing and housewares for Consumer Product Safety Commission recalls.
* Monitor Falls Creek processing for safety issues.
* Maintain Kaizen implementation by conducting monthly Falls Creek Kaizen audits.
* Promptly report all instances of safety, and recall issues to responsible individual. Retrain individual on proper quality standards, safety policies, and CPSC guidelines.
* Sort’s incoming material into predetermined category, sends sorted materials to storage or proper activity or processing.
* Follows style trends to determine classifications of articles.
* Prepares and maintains records as directed.
* Takes note of any unusual or valuable items received.
* Assists in establishing performance standards for associates.
* Develops and trains to meet standards.
* Assures that all machines and equipment are used properly.
* Responsible for all safety and accident functions.
* Assures housekeeping and grounds keeping is attended.
* Orders supplies directly related to production.
* Keeps President and CEO informed on supply of unprocessed material.
* Assists in all production and transportation aspects.
* Must be able to stand for long periods of time, use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms; push or pull.
* Must be able to occasionally sit, kneel, and climb.
* Must be able to regularly stoop, bend, squat, reach tum and twist body and lift up to 25 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds.

**RELATIONS:**

* Works under the general supervision of the President and CEO with authority to make minor decisions within established policies and procedures.
* Refers major decisions to the President and CEO.
* Works closely with Director of Mission Services and Program Specialist to ensure full integration of referrals into the workforce.
* Works closely with Warehouse Manager to ensure efficient flow of product to retail stores and required inventory of product is readily available for processing.

**STANDARDS FOR MEASURING PERFORMANCE:**

* The ability to meet or exceed cost and performance standards.
* The manner in which all material is processed.
* Effectiveness and detecting and safeguarding valuable or unusual items.
* Adequacy and accuracy of records.
* Degree to which respect and confidence of co-workers is established.
* Quality, quantity, and timeliness in the performance of assigned tasks.
* The manner in which one conduct reflects the high standards of morals and integrity expected of all Goodwill associates.
* Ability to meet deadlines and respond to special requests and the desires of management.

Benefits after 90 days include: agency paid life insurance and vision insurance, vacation, sick, holidays, and eligible to participate in group health and dental programs with biweekly co-pay. EOE

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

* High school graduate or equivalent with prior management and supervisory experience.
* Must have good work habits and respond appropriately to supervision.
* Must possess adequate physical endurance to work at industrial standards.
* Must have a valid PA Driver's License and clean MVR, and clean Criminal History, Child Abuse, and Fingerprint Clearances.

role.description:
**Job Overview**

Manages plants and directs and supervises the activities of personnel engaged in Advanced Water Reclamation, Potable Water supply distribution systems and solids management to ensure proper utility service to County residents and property owners.

**Annual Salary Range- $93,600.00- $125,257.60**

***Internal rates may vary based on the selected candidate's current grade.***

***Ideal Candidate***

The ideal candidate is an experienced Class “A” Florida Wastewater Treatment Plant Manager or Supervisor with exceptional leadership skills. The candidate would possess extensive knowledge of wastewater process control strategies and would have exceptional analytical and troubleshooting skills, with an ability to make sound and logical corrective actions. The candidate would possess maintenance experience which would allow them to make minor repairs or modifications as needed. The candidate would be well organized, utilizing calendars and reminders to aid themselves and subordinates in completing tasks. The candidate would possess the ability to plan and direct operational duties for his team or shift; cleaning duties, special projects, overtime, and maintenance. The successful candidate would be a highly motivated, self-starter possessing extensive motivational skills and exceptional teaching skills. The ideal candidate would utilize delegation as a tool to teach their subordinates and prepare them for succession. The candidate would have the ability to set up and facilitate staff meetings, safety meetings, and tailgate meetings before work. A good listener while also being a great communicator both orally and written as well as maintain detailed records and logs of duties and logistical data. The candidate would follow up on work performed in the plant, always communicating changes and status updates to the chain of command. Candidates should be able to safely and comfortably work with various industrial and laboratory chemicals. Candidates must be able and willing to respond to emergency situations to provide for public health and safety. Though the work consists of a team atmosphere, candidates at times will be required to work independently, occasionally work rotating shifts, including nights, weekends and holidays as well as cover overtime as needed. Candidates should have extensive computer skills with standard software such as Microsoft Excel, Word, Outlook, Teams, etc.

**Core Competencies**

* ***Customer Commitment*** - Proactively seeks to understand the needs of the customers and provide the highest standards of service.

role.description:
Join a growing, stable company offering consistent hours, and strong benefits. Gas and Supply is the region’s largest independent distributor of welding, safety, and industrial supplies, as well as a top national distributor of industrial, medical, and cryogenic gases. With over fifty locations across seven states, we are seeking a motivated individual to become a part of our team as a Fill Plant Manager.

**What’s in it for you:**

* Competitive wages commensurate with experience
* Regular overtime
* Monday – Friday work week (some Saturdays as needed)
* Bonus opportunities
* Career advancement opportunities
* Employer-paid life insurance
* Employer-paid disability insurance
* Health, dental, and vision insurance available
* 401K with employer match
* Educational reimbursement program
* Generous personal leave policy

**Job Description**:

Our Fill Plant Manager is responsible for supervising activities and workers engaged in the repackaging of compressed gas and liquid gases into cylinders. They will also be responsible for assigning job tasks to workers according to customer needs, stocking levels and other branch needs. Additional tasks may be assigned depending on the workload.

**Job Duties:**

* Operate and safely maintain equipment for pumping or repackaging gases into cylinders.
* Perform all pre-fill and post-fill inspections and tests before cylinders are released.
* Ensure cylinders are adequately maintained - cylinders requiring maintenance or repair are removed from service until corrected.
* Regularly inspect and maintain pumping apparatus and associated pressure gauges and monitoring devices.
* Fill cylinders or containers to proper pressure or weight, whichever is appropriate.
* Ensure cylinder filling records are accurately maintained and that all required procedures are followed in order to comply with local, state and federal regulations.
* Conduct periodic checks of plant for safe and efficient operation.
* Operate a forklift, pallet jack and other warehouse equipment.
* Assist with loading and unloading trucks and/or trailers when required.
* Assist with inventory, general housekeeping and help customers when necessary.
* Position requires working at industrial sites with equipment and tools.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Must pass drug test.
* Must pass background check.
* A high school diploma or equivalent preferred.
* Ability to read and comprehend material safety data sheets.
* Knowledge of the area and ability to lift 60 lbs. required.
* Ability to work independently and under some pressure to meet deadlines.
* Must be able to work occasional overtime if necessary.
* Must be able to work with a wide variety of people with different personalities and backgrounds.
* Must be able to operate in a drug-free workplace.
