role.title: Sr. Director Operational Excellence
role.description:
**Company Description**

At **Link Snacks**, we show up hungry, roll up our sleeves, plaid or otherwise, and dive straight into the hard work. We don’t hide from challenges; we hunt them down. We push harder, move faster, and take the kinds of big swings that built this business in the North Woods of Wisconsin four decades ago.

We’re everyday people who deliver extraordinary results. Innovation, creativity, and urgency aren’t buzzwords, they’re expectations. And just like the real protein snacks we make across our global house of brands—Jack Link’s®*,* Lorissa’s Kitchen®*,* Golden Island®*,* BiFi®*, and* Peperami® *and* KOOEE!® to name a few—there’s nothing artificial about us. What you see is exactly what you get: humble, gritty, passionate people who show up every day ready to not just be a participate in the meat snack industry that the Link Family created, but to move faster, innovate harder and keep raising the bar so high, the rest of the world needs a ladder just to see it.

Dominating this space across the world takes a team. A team that runs together, succeeds together, and celebrates together. A team that’s full of relentless energy and spirit that can only be fueled by one thing: a fist full of our delicious meat snacks.

Real Meat Protein. Real People. Real Results. THAT is Link Snacks.

 **Job Description**

**JOB SUMMARY**

The Sr Director of Operational Excellence leads the company's continuous improvement strategy across all manufacturing sites. This role will build the process, capabilities, tools, and governance necessary to create a consistent and sustainable approach to continuous improvement across all factories. The Sr Director will establish a standardized manufacturing excellence framework grounded in lean principles, structured problem solving, loss elimination, standard work, and performance management.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Lead the CI change effort. Develop and lead the company’s Continuous Improvement strategy and roadmap across all factories.
* Establish a common CI methodology, tools, governance, terminology, and expectations across the manufacturing network.
* Establish common standards for Lean practices, structured problem solving, daily management, standard work, and performance improvement.
* Establish and advance Lean manufacturing practices including standard work, Kaizen, 5S, value-stream mapping, visual management, root-cause analysis, waste elimination, centerlining, and structured problem solving.
* Develop CI training, tools, playbooks and learning programs.
* Develop a network of plant-level Continuous Improvement champions to accelerate adoption and share knowledge.
* Manage performance. Work with the Plant Leadership Team to track plant targets and KPIs regularly and set action plans and follow-up meetings to close gaps.
* Own KPI visibility. Manage the daily, weekly, and monthly KPI charting and posting process to keep teams accountable.
* Simplify data. Use Power BI and SAP to turn complex operational data into clear, usable information for plant and operations leaders.
* Apply analytics. Use statistics and other analytical methods to identify improvement opportunities and support decisions.
* Track savings. Implement and manage a cost savings tracking process aligned with corporate standards and deliver against savings targets.
* Partner on safety. Partner with the Safety Director to embed safety into improvement work, including incident investigation, hazard reduction, and safety considerations in kaizen events.
* Perform other duties as assigned

 
**Qualifications**

**Required**

* Bachelor’s degree in operations, manufacturing, supply chain, business, engineering, food science, or related field, or equivalent experience in continuous improvement.
* 7 to 10 years experience in a manufacturing environment, including a leadership role.
* 5+ years in influencing roles, such as CI, Lean, or support functions.
* Experience or education in statistical process control, root cause analysis, or other analytical methods.
* Training and hands-on experience with value stream mapping, kaizen methods, 5S, leader standard work, and other Lean tools.
* Project management experience leading cross-functional teams to deliver on timelines, budgets, and goals.
* Experience developing or implementing a playbook for a management operating system (MOS) and a continuous improvement program, including how the playbook was rolled out across sites.

**Preferred**

* Experience with SAP and Power BI for operational reporting.
* Experience in food or consumer packaged goods manufacturing.
* Experience with Total Productive Maintenance (TPM), with at least working exposure to its Autonomous Maintenance (AM) and Planned Maintenance (PM) pillars.

**Skill and Competencies**

* Strong written and verbal communication and presentation skills, with the ability to influence leaders at every level.
* Diplomacy in communicating needs and recommendations, with credibility that earns trust across functions.
* A proactive style that drives projects to completion despite obstacles.
* A collaborative team approach in all situations.
* Ability to manage multiple priorities and workstreams at once.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office.

 **Additional Information**

*The salary range for this role is $195,000 - 225,000 annually*

Link Snacks provides a variety of benefits to eligible Team Members, including medical, dental and vision benefits, life and disability insurance, 401k participation, paid holidays, and paid time off.

**Equal Employment Opportunity Employer** 
We are an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation and gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

-------------------

============

Maintain frequent and open communications with executive and corporate leaders that focus on timely resolution of issues that may potentially affect the safety, quality, identity, purity, and/or potency of collected plasma. Review and monitor Quality metrics and reports for trends and opportunities for improvement.

 

**Reports To**: Sr. Director, Quality Assurance
 
**Direct Reports:** Assistant Manager of Quality (Approximately 6-7)

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

 
 

* Manage staff, including selecting, training, developing, coaching and terminating, as applicable with guidance from Human Resources. Appraise employee performance and provide feedback and counseling to staff, as applicable.

 Ensure regular management review of quality performance that delivers stable, high levels of compliance performance in assigned QA areas. Provide leadership and coordination to established automated systems for control.
* Manage Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) performance to ensure meeting regulatory and departmental requirements, and to drive continual improvement in department processes. Works with CSL applicable systems to analyze and identify significant quality issues/trends and reports those to appropriate Sr. Management. Provides routine reports on the quality KPIs as requested by the applicable business units.

* Establish, implement and ensure timely delivery of strategic Quality Assurance performance. Provide direction and guidance on quality topics including resolutions and corrective actions. * Develop & maintain process to disseminate quality interpretation & strategies to operationalize relevant regulations, guidance & standards in collaboration with stakeholders. Maintain & update Quality training materials and provide consistent technical guidance to the operations team. Develop, deploy and occasionally deliver Quality information/publications to appropriate Corporate or Center staff.
* Mentor others on data analysis, technical problem prevention and resolution, design control procedures, investigation processes, and methods to arrive at true root causes as it relates to quality systems.
* Maintain high level of regulatory, compliance and communications skills with department staff, ensuring competence to make decisions and judgments in the course of business, including times of uncertainty.

Lead teams without the benefit of a direct reporting relationship

role.title: Senior Manager, Performance and Quality
role.description:
We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.

As the Senior Manager, Performance and Quality, you'll lead proposal development and formal client responses for the account, and coordinate the team's responses to client, external, and government audits. You'll turn complex contract, pricing, performance guarantee, and operational requirements into accurate, persuasive, on-time submissions. Every commitment and audit response you produce is supported, traceable, and clear to the client. In Finance and Contract Compliance, you'll link what proposals promise to how performance and quality are checked through audits and corrective action. You will also project-manage implementations and changes on the account.

**Primary responsibilities**
----------------------------

* Develop proposal strategies and response plans for renewals, RFPs, RFIs, client-requested program and benefit-change proposals, and contract amendments that align with account objectives and client requirements.
* Manage the end-to-end development and submission of proposals and formal client responses, from requirement intake through final review and delivery.
* Partner with account, executive, Finance, Legal, Clinical, and Operations leadership to define key messages and value propositions, and confirm that pricing, performance guarantee, and contract commitments are accurate and approved before submission.
* Write clear, persuasive, client-ready narratives and executive communications about capabilities, program results, and positions, and represent the team in client meetings on proposals and deliverables.
* Lead project management for implementations and account changes, such as new programs, vendor transitions, and benefit or system changes. Build and manage project plans for these and for RFPs, renewals, contract amendments, client deliverables, and audit responses, with timelines, milestones, owners, and dependencies. Plan for compressed client turnaround times and escalate at-risk items early.
* Research client needs, program developments, and market and competitive trends to inform proposal strategy and client recommendations.
* Implement standardized templates, content libraries, style guides, and quality checklists for proposals and audit responses, and train contributors to use them.
* Support contract negotiations during RFPs and amendments by coordinating redlines and negotiating items with Legal and leadership, and documenting each decision to keep, trade, or drop an item, with its approver, so the rationale stays on record.
* Own the audit request log and coordinate intake, scoping, ownership, and evidence production for client, external, and government audits of the account, including third-party audits triggered by performance guarantee escalation provisions.
* Perform quality reviews of audit responses and evidence packages to confirm every part of the request is addressed, amounts reconcile, and the response is clear to an independent reviewer; coordinate secure submission and retain final versions.
* Maintain internal corrective action plans (CAPs) for known contract breaches, so completed fixes are documented before the client asks, and lead the response when the client invokes the contract's formal CAP process. Track audit findings, management responses, fixes, and closeout against contract timelines, and report recurring performance and quality themes to leadership.

**Key deliverables**
--------------------

* Proposal and client-response calendar, plus a project plan for each RFP, renewal, contract amendment, implementation, and major account change.
* Proposal strategies and response plans for renewals, RFPs, RFIs, and client-requested proposals.
* Standard content library, templates, style guide, and quality checklist.
* Commitment and negotiating-items log tying each commitment and redline decision to its approver and source.
* Audit request log, scope and ownership matrix, and evidence-package standards.
* Internal CAP register for known contract breaches, plus a findings, management-response, and corrective-action tracker and audit closeout packages.
* Leadership summaries of open proposals, implementation and change status, at-risk deliverables, and audit status.

***\*\*\*This is a remote role, but the ideal candidate will live in the Eastern Time Zone\*\*\****

**Minimum qualifications**

* 7+ years of work experience.
* Experience managing end-to-end proposal or RFP responses for complex healthcare or PBM clients.
* Experience planning, executing, and delivering across concurrent deadlines and owners.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint, SharePoint, and proposal content-management tools.

**Preferred qualifications**

* PBM, health plan, or government program experience, including implementations or vendor transitions.
* Experience coordinating audits, regulatory requests, or evidence-based client reviews.
* Experience validating pricing, performance guarantee, or contract commitments in proposals.
* Proposal management or project management certification.

**Education**

* Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.

**Pay Range**

The typical pay range for this role is:

$67,900.00 - $182,549.00

This pay range represents the base hourly rate or base annual full-time salary for all positions in the job grade within which this position falls. The actual base salary offer will depend on a variety of factors including experience, education, geography and other relevant factors. This position is eligible for a CVS Health bonus, commission or short-term incentive program in addition to the base pay range listed above. This position also includes an award target in the company’s equity award program.

Our people fuel our future. Our teams reflect the customers, patients, members and communities we serve and we are committed to fostering a workplace where every colleague feels valued and that they belong.

**Great benefits for great people**

We take pride in offering a comprehensive and competitive mix of pay and benefits that reflects our commitment to our colleagues and their families.

 
This full‑time position is eligible for a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the physical, emotional, and financial well‑being of colleagues and their families. The benefits for this position include medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid time off, retirement savings options, wellness programs, and other resources, based on eligibility.

Additional details about available benefits are provided during the application process and on Benefits Moments.

 
We anticipate the application window for this opening will close on: 11/14/2026

Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with all federal, state and local laws.

role.description:
**Who We Are**
--------------

**ABOUT ENOVIS™**

Enovis Corporation (NYSE: ENOV) is an innovation-driven medical technology growth company dedicated to developing clinically differentiated solutions that generate measurably better patient outcomes and transform workflows. Powered by a culture of continuous improvement, global talent and innovation, the Company’s extensive range of products, services and integrated technologies fuels active lifestyles in orthopedics and beyond. For more information about Enovis, please visit www.enovis.com.

**What You'll Do**

At Enovis™ we pay attention to the details. We embrace collaboration with our partners and patients, and take pride in the pursuit of scientific excellence — with the goal of transforming medical technology as we know it.

Because that’s how we change the lives of patients for the better. And that’s how we create better together. Why work at Enovis? See for yourself.

As a key member of the Quality Assurance team, you will play an integral part in helping Enovis drive the medical technology industry forward through transforming patient care and creating better patient outcomes.

**Job Title**:

Sr Manager, Quality Assurance

**Reports To**:

Director, Quality Assurance

**Location:**

Fort Worth, TX

**Business Unit Description**:

QA

**Job Title/High-Level Position Summary:**

The Sr. Quality Assurance Manager is responsible for leading a team of quality engineers and Quality technicians in driving product and process excellence across the Recovery Sciences /Bracing and Support device portfolio. This role ensures compliance with regulatory standards, support manufacturing as well as new product introduction and fosters a culture of continuous improvement. The Sr. Quality Assurance Manager will collaborate cross-functionally to implement quality strategies that enhance product reliability, reduce risk, and improve operational efficiency across multiple locations.

**Key Responsibilities**:

 

* Lead and mentor a team of quality engineers and technicians, providing technical guidance and performance management.
* Develop and implement quality strategies that align with business objectives and regulatory requirements.
* Lead quality engineering support for manufacturing operations, ensuring robust process controls, effective risk management, and validation of production methods.
* Ensure compliance with FDA QSR (21 CFR Part 820), ISO 13485, and ISO 14971 standards.
* Drive root cause analysis and corrective/preventive actions (CAPA) for product and process issues.
* Collaborate with Manufacturing, R&D, Regulatory Affairs, and Supply Chain to resolve quality challenges and improve processes.
* Support internal and external audits, acting as a subject matter expert for quality engineering practices.

* Maintain and improve quality system documentation, including procedures, work instructions, and validation protocols.
* Be qualified as a Laser safety officer for the DFW location.
* Represent the LiteCure, TJM, and TJD Quality Management System as Management Representative.

**Travel requirements:**

* 50% to Tijuana sites

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Mechanical, Biomedical, Industrial, or related field); Master’s degree preferred.
* 8+ years of experience in quality engineering within medical devices or other regulated industries, including 3+ years in a leadership role.
* Strong knowledge of ISO 13485, FDA QSR, ISO 14971.
* Proven ability to lead cross-functional teams and manage complex projects.
* Excellent communication, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

**Desired Characteristics:**

* ASQ Certified Quality Engineer (CQE) or Certified Quality Manager (CQM), Certified Quality Auditor (CQA), or Six Sigma Black Belt.
* Familiarity with eQMS systems, statistical software, and metrology tools.
* Demonstrated success in driving quality improvements and regulatory compliance.

*Currently, Enovis does not provide sponsorship for employment visas (e.g., H-1B) and will not offer such sponsorship in the future. Applicants must already have full-time work authorization in the United States, both now and in the future, without requiring sponsorship.*

**“Creating better together”. It’s the Enovis purpose, and it’s what drives us and empowers us every day on a global scale.** We know that the power to create better – for our customers, our team members, and our shareholders – begins with having the best team, pursuing common goals, operating at the highest levels, and delivering extraordinary outcomes.

**What does creating better together mean to us at Enovis? Discover the “why” behind our purpose, values and behaviors:**

Our Enovis Purpose, Values and Behaviors on Vimeo

We offer a comprehensive benefits package that includes:

* Medical Insurance
* Dental Insurance
* Vision Insurance
* Spending and Savings Accounts
* 401(k) Plan
* Vacation, Sick Leave, and Holidays
* Income Protection Plans
* Discounted Insurance Rates
* Legal Services

Join us in creating better together.

**EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY** 
Enovis provides equal employment opportunities based on merit, experience, and other work-related criteria without regard to race, color, ethnicity, religion, national origin, sex, age, pregnancy, disability, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable law. We also strive to provide reasonable accommodation to employees’ beliefs and practices that do not conflict with Enovis policies and applicable law. We value the unique contributions that every employee brings to their role with Enovis.

The Director of Cyber Operational Excellence leads the design, deployment, and continuous improvement of a modern, digitally enabled Operational Technology (OT) cybersecurity operating model.

This critical role will lead the improvement and governance of HBS’s OT cybersecurity capability and standards across the globe to ensure HBS has the ability to provide market-ready and competition leading solutions for customers.

You will report directly to our Chief Operating Officer and you'll work out of the Atlanta, GA location on a hybrid schedule.

 

**You Must Have**

* Minimum 8 years demonstrated experience in cybersecurity architecture or solution architecture for OT and IT systems.
* Competent with security frameworks and standards such as: ISO 27001, NIST Guidelines, IEC/ISA 62443, CIS.
* Strong understanding of service contracts, entitlement models, field operations, and planning systems.
* Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders in a complex, matrixed environment.
Experience leading a high‑impact team 

**Success Measures**

* Understands industry cybersecurity standards and has insights into in country cybersecurity regulations.
* Provides strategic input and guidance for global Buildings OT focused cybersecurity solutions.
* Provides cybersecurity technical knowledge and experience to help close high-level sales.
Orders and margin above set quota in support of Annual Operating Plan (AOP). 

*Honeywell is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will be considered without regard to age, race, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, marital status, affectional or sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, disability, nationality, sex, religion, or veteran status.* Learn more

 

**Key Responsibilities**

* Own and operationalize the end‑to‑end cybersecurity value chain, integrating cybersecurity offerings across new projects, service contract bundles, entitlement structures, digital capabilities, and customer use cases into a cohesive and scalable operating model.
* Lead the evolution of standardized, value‑optimized cybersecurity offerings, moving away from highly customized, labor‑biased delivery models.
* Partner cross‑functionally with Commercial, Digital, IT, Finance, and Operations leaders to align strategy, execution, and investment priorities.
* Establish closed‑loop Voice of the Customer (VOC) and Voice of the Employee (VOE) feedback mechanisms to continuously improve cybersecurity design and execution.
* Lead transformation initiatives across short‑, medium‑, and long‑term horizons, ensuring adoption of new operating models and ways of working.
* Directly manage and develop a high‑performing team focused on cybersecurity offering definition, management, analytics, and continuous improvement, including improving deployment policies.
* Monitor and analyze market trends including ability to differentiate against competitors’ services and products.
* Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, and customer focus within the team.

role.description:
**Job Details:**

Job Summary:
 
As a pivotal leader in the organization, this role assumes comprehensive responsibility for all facets of operations across multiple plant locations. From overseeing the efficient functioning of production, maintenance, safety, shipping & receiving, sanitation, scheduling, quality, to driving continuous process improvement, this position plays a crucial role in ensuring the holistic success of our facilities.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

In addition to these core responsibilities, the incumbent will have ownership and/or responsibility for critical business metrics, including P&L, Return on Sales, Operations, and People Metrics. This underscores the significance of the role in not only operational efficiency but also in contributing to the financial health and workforce dynamics of our organization.
 
 
The position involves motivating and guiding managers to enhance the skill levels of their teams, adeptly addressing issues related to the quality of incoming and outgoing goods and leveraging a keen eye for reviewing cost and performance data to identify areas in need of improvement. The execution of all capital improvements for designated facilities falls under the purview of this role, emphasizing a commitment to driving excellence and ensuring a positive impact on key financial and operational indicators.
 
 
Within the broader context, the position's scope extends to providing guidance, leadership, and coaching to Plant Managers, and support groups across the division. With decision-making authority in the absence of the business unit Vice President, the role involves leading problem resolution, holding underperforming plants accountable, and motivating the leadership team to achieve both short and long-term goals. The responsibilities further encompass onboarding and training new plant managers, and senior production managers, identifying and delivering development opportunities for plant management, and overseeing special projects for the Business Unit.
 
This role is pivotal in fostering a culture of excellence, proactively addressing challenges, and contributing to our organization's overall success and growth through a multi-year strategy, directly impacting key financial and operational metrics.
 
 
Requirements:

Education: Bachelor's degree or equivalent.

Work Experience: 12-plus years of progressive experience in manufacturing; relevant food manufacturing experience a plus.

 
 

Special Job Competencies:

* Strong and effective leadership characteristics, collaborating and influencing multiple functions and teams.
* Demonstrates formal and informal authority and influence, leading by example while embodying the RIGHT Behaviors.
* Passion for continuous improvement and ethical decision-making.
* Proficient in problem-solving, analysis, and project management.
* Communication proficiency with excellent written and verbal skills.
* Ability to influence a variety of audiences with differing viewpoints and objectives.
* Business and financial acumen, with a track record of proven cross-functional work.
* Ability to multi-task effectively in a high-pressure environment.
* High level of manufacturing and technical competencies.
* Strong cultural fit, embodying and modeling the ONE Team methodology.

Supervisory: This role oversees 4-6 plant managers

Travel: Extensive travel and temporary relocation may be required.

People Leaders should demonstrate the ability to drive responsible AI adoption, enable effective use of approved solutions, identify opportunities to improve team performance through AI, and ensure accountability for the quality and accuracy of AI-supported outcomes.

**Be a Tar Heel!**

A global higher education leader in innovative teaching, research and public service, the **University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill** consistently ranks as **one of the nation’s top public universities**. Known for its beautiful campus, world-class medical care, commitment to the arts and top athletic programs, Carolina is an ideal place to teach, work and learn.

One of the best college towns and best places to live in the United States, Chapel Hill has diverse social, cultural, recreation and professional opportunities that span the campus and community.

University employees can choose from a wide range of **professional training opportunities** for career growth, skill development and lifelong learning and enjoy **exclusive perks** for numerous retail, restaurant and performing arts discounts, savings on local child care centers and special rates on select campus events. UNC-Chapel Hill offers full-time employees a **comprehensive benefits package**, paid leave, and a variety of health, life and retirement plans and additional programs that support a healthy work/life balance.

 

**Primary Purpose of Organizational Unit**

The UNC Adams School of Dentistry Dean’s Office provides oversight for the Adams School of Dentistry and serves as the liaison to the University, citizens, alumni and friends.

 

**Position Summary**

The Director of Continuous Improvement & Transformation provides strategic project leadership and organizational improvement expertise to strengthen the operations and services that support the Adams School of Dentistry’s education of future oral health professionals, advancement of research and discovery, and delivery of exceptional patient care. The position leads complex, high-priority initiatives designed to transform and improve ASOD operations, organizational effectiveness, service delivery, and the experience of faculty, staff, students, patients, and other stakeholders.
 
 
Working collaboratively with ASOD leadership and stakeholders across the School and University, the Director of Continuous Improvement & Transformation identifies organizational and operational challenges and opportunities for improvement; defines, scopes, and prioritizes projects; analyzes current-state processes and organizational needs; and facilitates the development of solutions aligned with ASOD priorities. The position serves as a strategic thought partner to leadership and applies project management, change management, analytical, and continuous improvement approaches to complex issues that may cross multiple departments, programs, and functional areas.
 
 
The Director of Continuous Improvement & Transformation leads initiatives through the full project lifecycle, including project definition and planning, analysis and solution design, implementation, change management, evaluation, and continuous improvement. Responsibilities include establishing project goals, deliverables, measures of success, and implementation strategies; coordinating work among subject matter experts and stakeholders; monitoring progress and outcomes; identifying and resolving barriers; and supporting the adoption and sustainability of improvements.
 
 
Projects vary in size, complexity, duration, and organizational impact. Depending on the scope and complexity of assigned initiatives, the position may lead a single large-scale project or manage multiple concurrent projects. The role works across organizational boundaries and relies on collaboration, facilitation, strategic influence, and effective stakeholder engagement to advance initiatives and achieve measurable improvements in support of ASOD priorities.

 

**Minimum Education and Experience Requirements**

Master’s or Bachelor’s and 0-2 years’ experience; or will accept a combination of related education and experience in substitution.

 

**Required Qualifications, Competencies, and Experience**

Demonstrated knowledge of project management, change management, organizational improvement, and problem-solving principles, with the ability to apply these concepts to complex, cross-functional initiatives.
 
 
Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills, including the ability to assess organizational and operational challenges, evaluate potential solutions, develop actionable recommendations, and use qualitative and quantitative information to support decision-making and continuous improvement.
 
 
Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with leaders and stakeholders across multiple functional areas and organizational levels and to facilitate change and influence outcomes without direct supervisory authority.
 
Excellent interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills, including the ability to facilitate meetings and discussions, present information and recommendations, and communicate complex concepts clearly to diverse audiences.
 
 
Strong organizational and project coordination skills, with the ability to independently manage multiple priorities, exercise sound judgment, navigate ambiguity, monitor progress and outcomes, and adapt to changing organizational needs.

 

**Preferred Qualifications, Competencies, and Experience**

Experience leading complex, cross-functional or organization-wide projects, strategic initiatives, operational reviews, or organizational improvement efforts.
 
 
Demonstrated experience applying project management and change management methodologies to the planning and implementation of complex initiatives.
 
 
Project Management Professional (PMP) certification preferred. Formal training or certification in organizational change management methodologies, such as Prosci Change Management Certification or an equivalent program, is highly desirable.
 
 
Experience facilitating collaborative problem-solving and solution-design activities with senior leaders, subject matter experts, and stakeholders across multiple functional areas.
 
 
Experience developing performance measures, analyzing outcomes, and using data and metrics to evaluate effectiveness and support continuous improvement.
 
 
Demonstrated ability to synthesize complex information and develop clear recommendations, presentations, and other communications for senior leadership and diverse stakeholder groups.
 
 
Experience working within a complex organization, preferably in higher education, academic health care, or a similarly decentralized environment.
 
 
Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint and experience using project management, collaboration, data visualization, or related business tools.

 

**Special Physical/Mental Requirements**

 

**Campus Security Authority Responsibilities**

This position is designated as a Campus Security Authority in accordance with the Clery Act. This position will be required to report Clery crimes to the Clery Compliance Manager and complete annual training about reporting responsibilities.

role.title: Director, Merchandising Operations
role.description:
Parachute Health is transforming post-acute care as the leading digital ordering platform for medical equipment and supplies. We connect major health systems, health plans, and suppliers to help patients get the life-saving products they need at home. Since launching, we've connected 300,000+ clinicians and 3,000+ supplier locations across all 50 states and helped 15M+ patients. What started as a DME ePrescribing tool has become the order management platform of choice for home medical equipment.

Join our team and make a difference in patient care.

### **About the Role**

Parachute Health is building the definitive platform for ordering home medical equipment and supplies, helping clinicians and suppliers ensure that millions of patients each year receive the critical equipment and supplies they need. Our Merchandising Operations team (AKA "Merch") comprises Category Managers and Category Analysts who have three primary jobs: 1) build and maintain our catalog, 2) build and maintain our coverage criteria rules engine, and 3) partner with R&D to improve the tools and workflows behind both. Merch sits at the intersection of e-commerce, compliance, operations, and R&D, and its work is central to Parachute's core functionality. Clinicians use our catalog to find and order the right equipment for their patients, and suppliers rely on it to fulfill those orders. Our coverage criteria help users determine whether an item should be covered by the patient's insurance.

The Merch team's work is nuanced and detail-dense: we maintain information on tens of thousands of products so our software, and the people who use it, can rely on it. The 18-person team splits its time between project work, like building and redesigning product categories and turning payer rules into qualification questions, and ticket-based work, resolving complex requests escalated by our support and partner teams. Our work requires efficient operational processes and excellent documentation.

As Director of Merchandising Operations, you will own the team's operating framework: how work is planned, prioritized, and delivered, and how the team partners with other teams across Parachute. You'll coach and develop a mix of managers and individual contributors, lead the team's largest cross-functional projects, and serve as a close thought partner to the SVP of Merchandising.

The role is primarily internal (roughly 90%), with occasional customer communication, especially on escalations, that calls for a steady, polished hand.

### **What You'll Do**

* Be the operational leader for a highly motivated, highly capable team of managers and individual contributors: keep work running smoothly, protect morale, and learn and add to a team culture that is already strong.
* Drive key projects: stay close to the work and personally drive the team's largest, most complex projects, including timelines, dependencies, and cross-team communication.
* Know every team process end to end. Lead the creation, maintenance, and centralization of SOPs and shared resources; drive consistent practices, training, quality assurance, and continuous improvement across category teams.
* Collaborate with partner teams (e.g., Supplier Implementation, Product, Customer Success) so handoffs and shared processes run smoothly.
* Be a Merch advocate: make the team's work understandable and visible across the company.
* Run bandwidth and capacity planning; flag risks early and rebalance coverage.
* Define and report on team metrics (ticket throughput, SLAs, SKU work, rollout milestones).
* Own escalations as needed, partnering effectively with people at all levels across the organization.
* Support recruiting as needed, own onboarding for new merchants, and maintain continuity coverage for every category.

### **Requirements**

* 7+ years in operations, program delivery, or management or technology consulting (e.g., a Big Four or top-tier firm), with 3+ years managing and growing managers.
* Track record of delivering complex, cross-functional projects using a clear, repeatable methodology.
* Data-driven: comfortable with capacity models, dashboards and prioritization trade-offs.
* Willingness to travel roughly once a quarter.

### **More About You**

* Passionate about improving patient outcomes in the healthcare space.
* Gets things done: drives work to completion and builds processes that stick.
* Thrives in complex, nuanced domains; quickly learns intricate systems (e.g., insurance coverage rules, product data) well enough to make sound calls.
* Clear, concise communicator who pushes back constructively and drives decisions.
* Sound compliance judgment: in a highly regulated industry, you know which issues to resolve and which to escalate.
* Track record of growing into increasing scope and responsibility.
* Nice to have: catalog, product data or e-commerce experience; healthcare, DME/HME or payer experience.

### **Benefits**

* Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage: Comprehensive plans with options for low-to-no-cost premiums
* Employer HSA Contribution: Company-funded contributions to your Health Savings Account
* 401(k) Retirement Plan
* Equity Incentive Plan
* Annual Company-Wide Bonus: Opportunity for up to 15% bonus based on company performance
* Remote-First Culture: We are remote-first with a dedicated NYC office and reimbursement options for co-working spaces
* Flexible Vacation Policy
* Summer Fridays: 5 additional Fridays off during the summer (separate from PTO)
* Home Office and Wellness Stipend
* Monthly Internet Stipend
* Annual Learning and Development Stipend

### **Base Salary Range (based on level and experience)**

$145,000-$180,000

role.title: Regional Operations Director
role.description:
### **Your Impact as a Regional Operations Director**

As a Regional Operations Director, you are a key leader responsible for the success and health of a diverse portfolio of veterinary hospitals. You will serve as the crucial link between local hospital teams and the broader Mission Pet Health network, empowering your teams to achieve excellence in both business performance and patient care.

* **Champion a Thriving Culture:** You'll partner with your Regional Medical Director to foster a positive, engaged, and high-performing culture across all hospitals in your region.
* **Develop Future Leaders:** You'll guide the growth of Hospital Managers and their teams, ensuring a strong pipeline of talent through effective coaching, training, and career development.
* **Drive Business Performance:** You'll have full ownership of the financial health of your region, managing P&Ls to drive revenue growth and optimize operational efficiency.
* **Build Winning Teams:** You'll lead the strategy for non-DVM recruiting and staffing, ensuring your hospitals have the talent they need to succeed.
* **Elevate the Client Experience:** You'll set the standard for exceptional client service, ensuring operational processes support a seamless and positive experience for every pet owner.

### **What You'll Bring to the Team**

* A proven track record of successful multi-site P&L management, with a keen ability to drive financial results.
* Demonstrated success in recruiting, developing, and retaining high-performing teams, especially in a leadership capacity.
* Exceptional leadership skills with a talent for building a positive, accountable, and solutions-focused culture.
* Excellent communication and conflict management skills, with the ability to tailor messages to diverse audiences.
* Significant experience leading in a multi-site veterinary, healthcare, or customer-centric retail environment.

### **How You're Supported**

*As part of the Mission Pet Health family, you get the stability of a local practice backed by the comprehensive benefits and resources of a larger network. The focus is on investing in you, so you can focus on what you love.* 
 
*Note: Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to support you at every stage. Eligibility for specific benefits varies based on your role and hours worked.*

##### **Competitive Compensation**

A competitive hourly rate or salary based on your experience and role.

##### **Health & Wellbeing**

We offer comprehensive coverage options including Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance, along with access to our Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for all teammates.

##### **Financial Security**

Plan for your future with our 401k retirement options and additional financial protection benefits like Life Insurance and Disability coverage.

##### **Commitment to Growth**

We support your career goals with opportunities for professional development, including educational assistance for qualified teammates to enroll in AVMA-accredited veterinary technician programs.

##### **The Power of a Network**

Join a nationwide community of over 20,000 veterinary professionals who share a passion for collaboration, career growth, and sharing best practices.

##### **Valuable Perks**

Enjoy discounted veterinary care for your own pets, access to an online discount platform, and free 24/7 access to doctors through Teladoc.

### **About Mission Pet Health**

Mission Pet Health was founded by veterinarians on the belief that local practices thrive with clinical autonomy, collaboration, and medical excellence. The organization provides world-class support to its 850+ hospital teams on a hyper-local basis so they can focus on what matters most: the medicine, their patients, and their team culture. Learn more at **missionpethealth.com**.

Driving the award-winning culture are the WAG values – **Work Together, Amaze, and Grow**. Mission Pet Health is veterinarian-led, people-focused, and on a mission to be the best place to work in veterinary medicine. We are proud to be recognized as a 2025 "Most Loved Workplace," ranked #2 in America's Top 100 and #1 in veterinary care.

**Reasonable Accommodations:** Applicants with disabilities may be entitled to reasonable accommodation. Please contact benefits@mvetpartners.com with your request and contact information.

**EEO Statement:** Mission Pet Health is an equal opportunity employer. We embrace diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

role.title: VP Manufacturing Engineering
role.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE JOB

 The Vice President, Manufacturing Engineering holds executive accountability for defining, scaling, and optimizing all aspects of manufacturing engineering across the entire Anduril enterprise. This role encompasses strategic development, execution of multi-year operational roadmaps, technological and process advancement, and organizational leadership across all product lines, production sites, and divisions. The VP will ensure consistent, rapid, and high-standard execution, driving efficiency, scale, and performance that directly contribute to Anduril's mission and market leadership. This role sits centrally and is responsible for ensuring that every division builds against a common standard. 

 WHAT YOU’LL DO

 
 Own the overarching manufacturing engineering strategy, operational roadmap, and resource budget for Anduril's centralized manufacturing engineering organization.

 Develop and champion a multi-year scaling strategy to meet exponential growth targets, changing operational constraints, and evolving customer demands.

 Strategically allocate resources (talent, capital, systems, facilities) across competing priorities, balancing urgent tactical needs with long-term capability building.

 Establish and enforce the enterprise standard for how Anduril builds production line operation, manufacturing systems usage, process design, and engineering practice, and hold division production leadership accountable to it.

 Own the roadmap for centralized capabilities, ensuring they are built to scale across product lines.

 Partner with and influence the VPs and Heads of Production across all divisions, setting technical direction for organizations that do not report to you.

 Drive consistency in how manufacturing engineering roles are defined, leveled, and expected to perform at every Anduril site, and deploy leadership and IC talent across the enterprise accordingly.

 
 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 
 15+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing engineering, production operations, or industrial engineering within a hardware/physical-product environment, with 5–7+ years at the executive level (VP or Senior Director) leading multi-team or multi-site organizations.

 Exceptional presentation, interpersonal, and stakeholder management skills; capable of aligning C-suite leaders and motivating frontline operators alike.

 Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Industrial, Manufacturing, Electrical, or Aerospace Engineering (or a related engineering/technical discipline). Master's degree or MBA preferred.

 Eligible to obtain and maintain a DoD Security Clearance.

 
 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 
 Experience navigating high-mix/low-volume transitions into high-volume/mass delivery.

 Background in fast-paced, high-accountability sectors (e.g., aerospace, defense, deep-tech, autonomous systems, high-growth industrial tech).

 US Salary Range
 $252,000 — $382,000 USD 


 The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:   

  

 Benefits 

 At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next.  For more information, Explore Our Benefits . 

  

 
 Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams 

 Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.



 
 To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

 
 
 No Financial Requests:  Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.



 Please always verify communications: 
 
 Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.

 Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com . 

 


 
 Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach:  If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.



 
 What to Do If You Suspect Fraud:  Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to  contact@anduril.com . Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.



 


  

 Data Privacy 

 To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/ .   

  

 By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

role.title: Director, Analytical Development & Quality Control
role.description:
Position Summary 

 The Director of Analytical Development & Quality Control will provide strategic and operational leadership for analytical development, characterization, method validation, transfer, and quality control activities supporting a growing pipeline of small molecule Oral Solid Dose (OSD) and parenteral Drug Product programs.  The incumbent will have deep experience in analytical activities required to support early-stage to late-stage oral solid dose and parenteral drug products. Additional experience in antibody/ADC manufacturing-focused analytical activities is desirable. This individual will be responsible for operating in a 100% outsourced environment to establish and manage phase-appropriate analytical strategies from preclinical through commercialization, overseeing external analytical operations, and ensuring compliance with global regulatory expectations and GMP requirements for assigned programs.

 As a key member of the Technical Operations team, the Director will collaborate cross-functionally with Medicinal Chemistry, Toxicology, Clinical Pharmacology, Drug Substance, Drug Product, ADC production, Regulatory Affairs, Quality Assurance, and external CDMOs/CRO/consultants to advance programs efficiently through development milestones while building scalable analytical and quality control capabilities for a rapidly growing organization.

  

 Key Responsibilities 

 Analytical Development Leadership 

 
 Lead, develop and execute phase-appropriate analytical method development and testing strategies and activities supporting Drug Product development, with an emphasis on small-molecule OSD and large-molecule parenteral Drug Product analytical method development and testing for assigned programs, including:

 
 Phase-appropriate small molecule oral solid dose drug product method development and testing (tablets, capsules, gelcaps)

 Phase-appropriate method development supporting antibody manufacture, ADC conjugation, and parenteral drug product manufacture.

 
 Provide technical oversight for development, qualification, validation, and lifecycle management of analytical methods.

 Ensure analytical methods support process development, formulation development, manufacturing, release testing, and regulatory submissions.

 Depending on experience, incumbent may serve as the company's analytical subject matter expert for ADC development.

 
 Support characterization of monoclonal antibodies, cytotoxic payloads, linkers, conjugates, and related impurities.

 Guide implementation and interpretation of advanced analytical techniques such as:  HPLC, UPLC, LC-MS, HRMS, SEC, CE-SDS, icIEF, HIC, ELISA, and bioassays.

 Collaborate with external CDMOs and internal process development teams to define CQAs and control strategies for ADC products.

 
 
 Quality Control Oversight 

 
 Establish and lead QC strategies across clinical manufacturing operations for assigned programs.

 Oversee external GMP testing activities including raw materials, IPCs, release testing and stability programs.

 Ensure timely release and disposition support for clinical materials.

 Manage investigations involving OOS, OOT, deviations, and laboratory events.

 
 Regulatory and Quality Support 

 
 Author and review analytical sections of regulatory submissions including: INDs, IMPDs, BLAs, NDAs, and CTAs for assigned programs.

 Ensure analytical approaches align with ICH, FDA, EMA, and other global regulatory expectations.

 Support establishment of specifications and analytical control strategies throughout the product lifecycle.

 May participate in regulatory agency interactions and inspections.

 Ensure compliance with cGMP, GLP, GCP, and data integrity requirements.

 Partner closely with Quality Assurance to maintain inspection readiness.

 Support audits of contract testing laboratories and manufacturing partners.

 
 External Partner Management 

 
 Manage relationships with contract laboratories and CDMOs.

 Oversee method transfers, validation activities, and technical governance of external laboratories.

 Establish performance metrics and ensure delivery against development and manufacturing timelines.

 Evaluate/implement new technologies/outsourced capabilities as needed.

 
  

 Required Qualifications 

 Education 

 
 Ph.D./MS in Analytical Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Biochemistry, Biotechnology, Chemical Engineering, or related scientific discipline preferred.

 
 Experience 

 
 12+ years (Ph.D.)15+ years (MS) of progressive pharmaceutical or biotechnology analytical development experience.

  Demonstrated deep experience in analytical development activities supporting Drug Product development and manufacturing with emphases on oral solid dose, parenteral, and pediatric formulations.

 Proven track record advancing products from early development through late-stage clinical development and/or commercialization.

 Demonstrated success working with CDMOs and global development partners.

 Additional experience in development and implementation of analytical methods to support antibody/ADC manufacturing is preferred.

 
 Technical Expertise 

 Strong working knowledge of:

 
 Analytical method development and validation

 Stability programs and specification setting

 Quality control laboratory operations

 GMP analytical testing

 Oral solid dose characterization and phase-appropriate method development, including discriminatory dissolution method development

 ADC analytical characterization

 Experience with Biologics testing methodologies preferred

 ICH Q1, Q2, Q3, Q6, Q7, Q8, Q9, Q10, and Q14 guidance

 Regulatory submissions and health authority interactions

 
 Leadership Competencies 

 
 Strategic thinker with strong business and scientific acumen.

 Excellent project management and organizational skills.

 Strong communication and influence skills across scientific, quality, regulatory, and program teams

 Ability to travel (20%) to CDMO domestic and international sites.

 Fluency with standard computer software packages (MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Project), iStability, and JMP (or similar statistical tools).

 High level of personal integrity, commitment to excellence and to our patients.

 Experience in developing and commercializing drugs for oncology is preferred.

 
 This position is classified as exempt. The anticipated annual base salary range for candidates who will work in Watertown is $193,877 to $232,875. The final base salary offered to the successful candidate will be dependent upon several factors that may include but are not limited to the type and length of experience within the job, and other factors. Treeline Biosciences is a multi-state employer, and this salary range may not reflect positions that work in other cities or states. 

   

 Recruitment fraud statement 

 Please be aware of recruitment fraud and related job scams, where scammers present themselves as recruiters but are seeking to steal money or personal information. Keep the following in mind to protect yourself: 

 
 Treeline Biosciences will never ask for money from you as part of our recruitment process. Do not provide bank details or pay somebody for the promise of a job at Treeline. 

 We do not conduct interviews through RingCentral, Skype or Telegram. 

 Our job openings are first posted to treeline.bio/careers. If you locate a listing for a Treeline job on another site, please ensure it is also posted on our careers website. 

 You can find more information about job scams at consumer.ftc.gov/articles/job-scams. 

 To report job scams, head to ReportFraud.ftc.gov. 

 Notice to Search Firms/Third-Party Recruitment Agencies (Recruiters)

 The Human Resources team manages the recruitment and employment process for Treeline Biosciences. To protect the interests of all parties involved, Treeline Biosciences will only accept resumes from a recruiter if an executed search agreement directed to the particular position or positions is in place at the start of the recruitment effort. Unsolicited resumes sent to Treeline Biosciences from recruiters do not constitute any type of relationship between the recruiter and Treeline Biosciences and do not obligate Treeline Biosciences in any way to pay fees should we hire from those resumes. Recruiters are requested not to contact or present candidates directly to our hiring manager or employees.

 In direct collaboration with Manufacturing Operation units and other functions (Quality, Engineering, IT, etc.) the Director, TSMS provides clear direction and the necessary expertise to:

 Ensures adherence to cGMP requirements, guidelines, SOPs, as well as compliance to local laws, the Elanco Red Book, company policies and Health Safety & Environment (HSE) requirements. Particular attention is given to the protection of employees, patients, company assets and the environment.
 Ensure that mAb products and processes are in control and capable, with appropriate control strategies in place to meet Elanco Global Quality and Manufacturing standards and maintain continuity of supply.
 Develop and lead continuous improvement initiatives which positively impact cycle time, productivity, process robustness, gross margin, and production capacity.
 Partner with Commercialization, R&D, Manufacturing, Engineering, Supply Chain and Quality to successfully in-transfer new mAb products.  Ensure that transfers are accomplished on-time, with appropriate process / product control strategies in place.
 Leads cross functional teams for root cause investigations.
 Committed to knowledge sharing/transfer inside site manufacturing groups as well as to Technical R&D (TRD).
 Drives the product control strategy including development and application of KPIs to enable meaningful CPP/CQA trending and reporting of key process data as well as to quickly identify changing quality trends and issues.
 Develop the expense and capital planning budgets for the TSMS function in collaboration with the Sr. Director, Commercialization and site leadership team.  Ensure TSMS delivery meets or exceeds financial commitments.
 Responsible for the design and delivery of TSMS owned technical training programs as well as appropriate technical on-boarding to ensure competency of TSMS associates.
 Stays abreast of technological, regulatory and industry developments, e.g., via internal and external benchmarking.
 Build and grow the TSMS function, recruiting and developing talent in alignment with the site’s strategic needs.
 Maintain a safe work environment and establish a strong safety culture in compliance with Elanco standards and all applicable government requirements.
 Ensure TSMS staff operate in accordance with all applicable Quality and cGMP requirements.  Accountable for quality performance of the function and delivery against site quality targets.
 Develop and review operational objectives with direct reports, establish appropriate talent development plans, and conduct staff performance management reviews as required.
 Other duties as required.

 Bachelor’s degree in a biomanufacturing related discipline (e.g. biology, Chemistry, engineering, etc.).
 10 years of related working experience
 5+ years’ experience in technical management position.
 5+ years’ experience in (bio)pharmaceutical formulation, process development, or manufacturing technology.
 Ability to lead and develop a team.
 Fundamental understanding of (bio)pharmaceutical analytical testing.
 Demonstrated understanding of Q culture, cGMP standards, and regulatory regulations.
 
 Additional Preferences :
 MSc in Science, Pharmacy, Mechanical or Chemical Engineering, Pharmaceutical Technology.
 Proficiency in applied statistics/Lean Six Sigma methodologies.
 Understanding of USDA, FDA, and EU GMP regulatory standards for veterinary biologics.

 Ability to network and build strong, collaborative relationships across functions / geographies.
 Excellent verbal and written communication skills (English).

role.title: Director of Operations
role.description:
**Director of Operations**

**Job Summary:** The Director of Operations reports directly to VP Operations and is responsible for managing all activities related to operations management at Prescott, WI; implements policies and procedures to align with corporate long and short-term goals; manages strategic planning and headcount objectives by performing the following duties personally or through subordinate supervisors.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**

* Provide direct leadership to the functions of Manufacturing, Engineering, SHE, Materials Management, and Facility/Maintenance.
* Manage and maintain operating functions that follow TCLAD philosophy. Establish and implement policies and procedures necessary for orderly and effective operations and ensure compliance to all applicable TCLAD policies and procedures.
* Ensure compliance with TCLAD standards for human resource management, safety and loss prevention, cost control, waste reduction, quality, and on-time delivery.
* Ensure compliance with all Federal, State and Local legal and regulatory requirements.
* Manages resources to effectively balance strategic objectives with financial return (profit) and efficient use of financial assets, including working capital. Manage all capital planning and expenditures.
* Develop innovative and cost-effective methods of manufacturing, labor management, material procurement and utilization, and business processes to position Thermal Substrates for continued growth.
* Plan, implement and manage outsourcing and offshore production and supplier initiatives & projects.
* Support TCLAD quality initiatives, and leads the Thermal Substrates facility commitment at all levels of direct and indirect personnel to follow the ISO 9001, ISO 14001 & IATF 16949 Quality Management Systems
* Audit facility operations continuously by reviewing performance, major item variances, and other critical business elements, and reports as required by the VP Operations, or other management.
* Establish and maintain customer and other business relationships necessary for the successful operation of Thermal Substrates. Participate in key customer visits when required.
* Represent the operation at various meetings as required.
* Perform other duties as may be assigned.

**Minimum Qualifications:**

* Experience with ERP/MRP software, Internet software; Project Management software; Spreadsheet software and Word Processing software.
* Proven analytical, project management and systems background.
* P&L responsibility in general management or plant management in a manufacturing organization.
* Exceptional leadership skills that are demonstrated by achieving desired results through others and building an effective management team through coaching and mentoring.
* An in-depth technical understanding and knowledge of Thermal Substrates product lines.
* PCB Manufacturing Experience
* Proven strategic and tactical skills. Demonstrated problem analysis and resolution.
* Excellent interpersonal, written, verbal and presentation communication skills.
* Comprehensive business process and systems knowledge, such as ERP, and the ability to identify and implement best practices.
* An entrepreneurial spirit coupled with a strong ethic and a commitment to high personal standards that link to exceptional business values and ethics.

**Education and/or Experience:** B.S. or B.A. degree in Engineering, Operations or related technical field. Desired: Master’s Degree (MBA). Prefer 15+ years of experience in manufacturing and engineering, including 10 years of senior leadership through plant/general management experience in manufacturing.

**Safety Roles and Responsibilities**
-------------------------------------

All TCLAD employees are empowered to stop production if someone is in danger and notify their supervisor if an unsafe act or product quality concern is occurring. Also, each member of the TCLAD team is responsible for identifying continuous improvement and pollution prevention opportunities and participating in problem solving teams as necessary.

* Provide leadership for the implementation and execution of the TCLAD SHE program
* Clearly communicate and ensure that SHE rules, and procedures are in place to prevent injuries, minimize occupational health exposures and prevent SHE incidents
* Ensure that you are adequately trained in all SHE-related aspects of your job
* Hold accountable employees who fail to follow SHE rules, procedures or accepted safe work practices
* Consistently and frequently audit work practices and behavior; and not tolerate any deviations from accepted standards and requirements
* Correct any known SHE deficiency, either facility or people related, as a priority
* Participate or lead investigations of all injuries, suspected injuries and SHE incidents, and ensure that recommendations to prevent recurrence are completed
* Lead by example by following all SHE rules and procedures, using accepted safe work practices and setting high SHE standards
* Position SHE as a top priority in communications, actions and decisions

role.title: Director, Supplier Industrialization Engineering
role.description:
Are you ready to build America’s energy future? Form Energy is an American manufacturing and energy technology company. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form!

In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by *TIME* as a “Best Invention”, *MIT Technology Review* as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and *Fast Company* as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia.

Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing - might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.

**Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.**

**Role Description**
--------------------

Form Energy is hiring a Director of Supplier Industrialization Engineering and Quality to build and lead the team responsible for the technical relationship with our supplier base, from first sketch through high-volume production, and for the quality systems that ensure everything that arrives at our factories meets spec. This role reports into our VP, Global Supply Chain and brings together two functions that have to move as one: the engineers who industrialize our components and equipment, and the quality systems and team that hold our suppliers accountable once they are producing.

Form's 85% domestically sourced supply chain was built for a battery chemistry with no existing supplier base, which means the industrialization playbook and the quality systems we need are still being written. You will set that standard: rigorous enough to protect a product with a 100-hour duration promise, and practical enough to work with suppliers who are learning our process alongside us. You will fly high enough to set the strategy and the org, and go deep enough to sit in a root cause review when it matters. 
 
*Relocation assistance is available.*

### **What you'll do:**

* Lead Form's Supplier Industrialization Engineering and Supplier Quality organization, growing a team of engineers embedded across battery materials, components, and equipment categories.
* Own the end-to-end industrialization journey for direct materials and made-to-spec components, from design-for-manufacturability review and supplier selection through tooling qualification and sustaining production support.
* Build and own Form's supplier quality management system, including PPAP, APQP, PFMEA, control plans, and SCAR/8D corrective action processes, calibrated for a novel battery chemistry with no legacy supply base to borrow from.
* Set the technical bar for supplier selection and qualification, partnering with Global Supply Managers to ensure our sourcing strategy is backed by suppliers who can deliver on cost, quality, and schedule.
* Own supplier process capability and yield performance, coordinating with Design Engineering, Manufacturing, and Reliability teams to drive root cause analysis and corrective action when issues surface.
* Develop the roadmap and staffing plan for quality systems aligned to relevant standards (e.g., ISO 9001, IATF 16949) at a scale and stage appropriate to where Form is today and where we are headed.
* Represent supplier technical and quality readiness within the Product Development Process, ensuring every component and supplier is qualified ahead of commercial scale.
* Partner with Supply Chain leadership and cross-functional stakeholders to align supplier roadmaps with Form's build plan and deployment targets.

### **What you'll bring:**

* Bachelor's degree (or higher) in Mechanical, Manufacturing, Materials Engineering, or a related technical field.
* 12+ years of experience in supplier industrialization, quality, or manufacturing engineering, including at least 5 years in a people leadership role building and scaling a team.
* Demonstrated expertise across DFM/DFA, PPAP, APQP, FMEA, SPC, and structured root cause methodologies (8D, 5 Whys).
* Experience building quality and industrialization systems from the ground up, ideally in a hardware, energy, or battery environment without an established supplier base to lean on.
* Strong technical fluency to go deep with engineers and suppliers, paired with the executive presence to represent risk, tradeoffs, and strategy to senior leadership.
* Comfort operating across the full arc from early design concept through high-volume production and sustaining support, with the judgment to know which problems need a system and which need a phone call.

*#LI-Onsite*

*Humanity is a cornerstone of Form Energy’s culture, and we make sure our compensation and benefits reflect that. Form Energy offers competitive salaries, stock options, and a holistic benefits package to ensure all employees have what they need to thrive while working here.*

*When it comes to you and your family’s health, we cover 100% of medical, dental, and vision premiums for full-time employees - and 80% of healthcare premiums for dependents. This starts from day one. We also offer at least 12 weeks of paid leave for new parents (up to 20 weeks for birthing parents), and generous vacation policies to give employees time to recharge when needed.*

*To build America’s energy future, we need everyone at the table. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply to our open jobs.*

*If you may require reasonable accommodations to participate in our interview process, please contact accommodations@formenergy.com. Requests for accommodations will be treated with discretion.* 
 
*Form Energy is committed to maintaining the privacy of our applicants. Please be aware that we will* ***never*** *solicit sensitive personal information such as Social Security numbers or bank account details during the recruiting or hiring process.*
