role.title: Director, Issue Validation Quality Control (QC)
role.description:
The Director, Issue Validation Quality Control (QC), will lead a team of audit professionals responsible for executing risk-based quality control reviews and providing independent challenge of IAG’s issue validation activities. The role will oversee and perform the independent assessment of IAG validation procedures, supporting evidence, and testing effectiveness to confirm well-supported issue closure conclusions in accordance with IAG’s Charter, Policies & Procedures (P&P), Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA) Standards, and applicable regulatory expectations. Through targeted reviews, identification of emerging trends, and continuous improvement initiatives, the role will strengthen IAG validation practices. This role is key to advancing IAG’s aspiration to be a world-class audit function.

 

* 7+ years of experience in internal audit, issue management, issue validation, risk management, assurance advisory, or public accounting; financial services, banking, or capital markets experience preferred.

* Bachelors degree or advanced degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

* Internal Audit, Assurance, Risk, or Accounting professional certification (CIA, CPA, CISA, CRCM, or equivalent)

* Direct experience evaluating and validating corrective action implementation, issue remediation evidence, validation testing, and the quality of issue closure conclusions.

* Strong knowledge of IIA standards and regulatory and financial industry guidance relevant to Internal Audit, issue management, and remediation validation.

* Excellent written and oral communication skills, including the ability to articulate constructive challenge and present findings in a compelling manner to senior stakeholders; strong project management skills.

* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including assessing evidence sufficiency, identifying root causes and trends, and translating QC results into practical recommendations for improvement.

* Demonstrated people leadership experience and ability to coach, develop, and lead teams while maintaining independent, risk-based judgment.

Employment eligibility to work with American Express in the United States is required as the company will not pursue visa sponsorship for these positions.

 

At American Express, our culture is built on a 175-year history of innovation, shared values and Leadership Behaviors, and an unwavering commitment to back our customers, communities, and colleagues. From delivering differentiated products to providing world-class customer service, we operate with a strong risk mindset, ensuring we continue to uphold our brand promise of trust, security, and service.

As part of Team Amex, you’ll experience our powerful backing with comprehensive support for your holistic well-being and many opportunities to learn new skills, develop as a leader, and grow your career. Here, your voice and ideas matter, your work makes an impact, and together, you will help us define the future of American Express.

 

We back you with benefits that support your holistic well-being so you can be and deliver your best. This means caring for you and your loved ones' physical, financial, and mental health, as well as providing the flexibility you need to thrive personally and professionally:

* Competitive base salaries
* Bonus incentives
* 6% Company Match on retirement savings plan
* Free financial coaching and financial well-being support
* Comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life insurance, and disability benefits
* Flexible working model with hybrid, onsite or virtual arrangements depending on role and business need
* 20+ weeks paid parental leave for all parents, regardless of gender, offered for pregnancy, adoption or surrogacy
* Free access to global on-site wellness centers staffed with nurses and doctors (depending on location)

For a full list of Team Amex benefits, visit our Colleague Benefits Site .

For positions covered by federal and/or state banking regulations, American Express will comply with such regulations as it relates to the consideration of applicants with criminal convictions.

role.title: Director, Quality Assurance - Xenotransplantation (DPF)
role.description:
California, US residents .

**The job details are as follows:**

Who We Are

We are the first publicly-traded biotech or pharmaceutical company to take the form of a public benefit corporation. Our public benefit purpose is to provide a brighter future for patients through the development of novel pharmaceutical therapies; and technologies that expand the availability of transplantable organs.

United Therapeutics (Nasdaq: UTHR) seeks to travel down the corridors of indifference to develop treatments for rare, deadly diseases. We were founded in 1996 by a family seeking a cure for their daughter’s pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Today, we have six FDA-approved therapies that treat PAH, pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease (PH-ILD) and neuroblastoma, a rare pediatric cancer. Our near-term pipeline seeks to develop additional therapies for PAH and pulmonary fibrosis (PF).

The cure for end-stage life-threatening diseases like PAH, PH-ILD, PF, and many others is an organ transplant, but only a small percentage of donated organs are available to address the vast need. For this reason, we are working to create manufactured organs to address the shortage of kidneys, hearts, lungs, and livers available for transplant. We believe an unlimited supply of tolerable, transplantable organs will eliminate the transplant waiting list and cure end-stage organ diseases for which transplant is not currently an option. 
 
Who You Are

You’ll help define what “right first time” means in one of the most ambitious frontiers of modern medicine. In this role, you’ll provide both strategic leadership and hands‑on quality oversight for the manufacture and release of designated pathogen‑free animal organs intended for human transplantation—operating at the intersection of FDA, USDA, and global GxP expectations in a truly novel environment. This is a role for a quality leader who thrives on complexity, builds systems that people actually follow, and wants their expertise to directly shape the future of organ transplantation.

The Director, Quality Assurance – Xenotransplantation provides strategic and operational leadership for Quality Assurance systems supporting the manufacture, assessment, and release of designated pathogen‑free (DPF) animal organs intended for human transplantation. This role ensures sustained compliance with FDA, USDA, and global GxP requirements while enabling operational execution across DPF site operations, animal care, laboratories, and manufacturing functions. This position serves as a senior Quality leader for DPF operations, partnering closely with Site Operations, Animal Care, Facilities, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, and R&D to drive inspection readiness, right‑first‑time execution, and continuous improvement in a highly regulated and novel manufacturing environment.

 

* Responsible for strategic planning, direction, and goal setting for the Quality Assurance function of Xenotransplantation
* Provide strategic direction and governance for the DPF Quality Management System (QMS), ensuring compliance with cGMP, cGLP, cGCP (as applicable), FDA, USDA, and internal quality standards
* Establish, maintain, and continuously improve QA policies, procedures, and programs supporting xenotransplantation and organ manufacturing activities
* Own Quality oversight for deviations, investigations, CAPAs, change control, complaints, and product quality reviews
* Ensure robust document control, data integrity, and record retention practices across animal care, laboratories, and manufacturing operations
* Lead Quality Assurance to support regulatory and clinical efforts to reach FDA approval of animal organs for human transplant
* Review documentation (including, but not limited to: animal care records, analytical/medical records, clinical case records, protocols, reports, environmental monitoring data, and laboratory data) for accuracy, completeness, and compliance with United Therapeutics policies and procedures, and GxP/FDA/Clinical Trial/USDA requirements
* Provide Quality oversight of material receipt, inspection, release, and supplier qualification activities
* Manage and lead controlled document collaboration, review, and approval
* Provide prompt review of clinical case data
* Perform Quality Assurance oversight activities to ensure compliance with current regulatory standards (e.g. deviation/failure investigations, change control documentation management, complaints, standard operating procedures, and product quality review)
* Review and write/update SOPs and reports to support these systems
* Perform internal and vendor audits; track corrections to audit observations and manage internal and external audit files; summarize data to support annual product reports
* Assist Operations, Quality, and R&D in the preparation of validation protocols and reports; coordinate validation plans and tasks to ensure timely completion of validation projects as assigned by Quality management
* Develop and provide guidance and direction regarding new initiatives and quality improvements; assess internal processes and procedures to ensure the most efficient utilization of resources; provide strategic advice and support to senior management and staff
* Establish Quality Assurance policies, practices, and programs to support Xenotransplantation function
* Initiate and lead departmental and/or interdepartmental strategic objectives; translates strategy into operational and tactical plans
* Lead FDA/USDA or other regulatory agency inspections; interpret direction from the inspection and react accordingly and quickly to mitigate potential problems; support the timely and accurate transfer of data, documents, and information to inspectors; act with discretion
* Responsible for overall planning, staffing, budgeting, and managing expenses
* Manage, coach, provide feedback, and review team's work, providing mentorship and professional development
* Drive a culture of quality, accountability, ethical conduct, and continuous improvement

Minimum Requirements

 

* Bachelor’s Degree in science, engineering, or related field or Master’s Degree in science, engineering, or related field
* 15+ years of experience in a GxP/FDA/USDA regulated environment
* Extensive managerial experience with demonstrated people leadership, including conflict resolution, change management, coaching, and professional development
* Experience managing FDA inspections
* In‑depth Quality Assurance knowledge with applied expertise in GxPs/Quality Systems, FDA/USDA guidelines, and relevant industry standards
* Ability to interpret data and apply GxP principles to company‑specific procedures, processes, and products, including those related to organ assessment and preservation
* Strong analytical judgment with exceptional problem‑solving and risk assessment capabilities
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, including professional documentation and the ability to independently produce high‑volume, complex written materials
* Ability to interact effectively across departments, including leading meetings and delivering presentations
* Ability to review work performed by others, identify issues or deficiencies, enforce company policies and procedures, and drive corrective actions
* Ability to handle confidential company data, projects, and information with discretion
* Exceptional skills in problem and risk analysis/assessments
* Ability to interpret data in relation to a vast number of company procedures as well as current GxP/Quality Systems/USDA/etc. requirements
* Advanced analytical thought, judgment, and in-depth Quality Assurance knowledge
* Competency in conflict resolution, change management, coaching, and professional development
* Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and Outlook
* This position requires working in-person from our facilities five days per week, when not on business travel
* Must not have interaction with pigs outside of the company

Preferred Qualifications

 

* 12+ years of experience in animal husbandry/tissue bank and/or cell processing environment
* Experience with TrackWise and MasterControl (eDMS) systems
* Working knowledge of Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS)
* Experience with SAP S/4HANA

Job Location

This position will be based 100% onsite at our facility in Stewartville, MN and will require up to 25% travel.

The salary range for this position is $167,500 - $230,000 per year and reflects our good-faith estimate of the compensation for this role at the time of posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on factors such as education, qualifications, experience, skills, geographic location, and business needs, as well as other factors permitted by law at the time of posting. This range may be modified in the future based on company and market factors.

At United Therapeutics, our mission and vision are one. We use our enthusiasm, creativity, and persistence to innovate for the unmet medical needs of our patients and to benefit our other stakeholders. We are bold and unconventional. We have fun, we do good.

role.description:
**Revised:** October 22, 2026 
**Job Title:** Director of Quality Management Systems and Compliance 
**Department:** Quality and Compliance 
**Reports To:** Chief Operating Officer 
**FLSA Status**: Exempt 
**Location**: TBD; responsibilities across company locations 
 
**Who is Dielectric Manufacturing?** 
Dielectric is a plastics and metals contract manufacturer specializing in thermosets and thermoplastics, delivering world class service using our family values. Our company values guide all that we do. 
*Open to Change | Passion | Get ‘r Done| Respect | Responsible & Accountable | Accept the Challenge*

**Job Summary:** 
The Director of Quality and Compliance establishes companywide quality and compliance strategy and leads its execution across manufacturing locations. Reporting to the COO, this role prioritizes customer and applicable regulatory CMMC, ITAR, RoHS, PFAS requirements, ISO 9001 Quality Management System effectiveness and Eco Vadis Sustainability requirements while developing the quality organization. The role supports customer needs through cross-site leadership, team development and hands-on resolution of critical issues.

**Essential Functions:** 

* Develop ISO quality and CMMC compliance strategy, annual objectives and resource plans with the COO; integrate requirements into new programs and facility transfers.
* Own the EcoVadis assessment and improvement program, coordinate policies and evidence with functional owners, and track actions through completion.
* Lead REACH, RoHS, PFAS and PPWR responses, packaging technical files and declarations; manage BOMcheck, Assent, and IMDS submissions where applicable.
* Oversee FAI, PPAP, PSW and SRPQP packages, material certifications, customer change requests and deviations; govern traceability, holds, calibration and competence records.
* Own quality-system governance across locations, including policies, document control, audit programs, certification readiness and management review.
* Establish ownership of applicable customer, contractual and regulatory obligations; maintain visibility of requirements, evidence, deadlines and unresolved risks.
* Lead customer-quality relationships, audit responses, portal governance, flowdown review and required change approvals with Sales, Engineering and Operations.
* Direct supplier-quality qualification, risk assessment, performance improvement and corrective actions; partner with Purchasing on technically approved alternative sources.
* Lead corrective-action effectiveness reviews, escalate significant risks and initiate containment or hold actions through established procedures.
* Develop and provide guidance to the Site level quality staff, recommend staffing and training needs.
* Set quality and compliance metrics, report performance and risks to executive leadership, and prioritize improvements using customer impact and cost of poor quality.
* Perform other duties as assigned.

**Qualifications:** 

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, quality, manufacturing or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.
* Ten or more years of progressive manufacturing quality experience, including at least five years leading quality systems, teams or cross-site programs. Experience in medical and/or aerospace and defense preferred.
* Demonstrated success by establishing quality strategy, developing leaders and implementing improvements in a regulated manufacturing supply chain.
* Experience with EcoVadis and material reporting platforms such as BOMcheck or IMDS preferred. Strong ISO 9001 quality-system experience and ability to interpret customer-specific requirements; relevant aerospace/defense or medical supply-chain experience preferred.
* Hands-on experience leading audits, resolving findings, managing customer escalations and verifying corrective-action effectiveness.
* Experience with supplier quality, material declarations, traceability and qualification documentation such as FAI, PPAP, PSW or customer-specific equivalents.
* Ability to assess applicability of requirements, communicate limitations and obtain qualified technical or legal advice as appropriate.
* Strong analytical, communication and project-management skills, with the ability to influence across functions and hold owners accountable.
* Experience defining metrics, budgets and resource priorities; familiarity with ERP systems, customer portals and controlled documentation.
* Lead auditor training or relevant ASQ certification preferred; Epicor Kinetic experience helpful.

Work Environment: 

* Office and manufacturing-floor environment with onsite leadership presence and travel among company locations and to customers or suppliers as needed.
* Follow site safety requirements and wear required PPE on the manufacturing floor.

**Authority and Cross Functional Accountability:** 
The Director leads quality-system governance, compliance and EcoVadis coordination. Site and functional leaders own implementation and supporting evidence.

role.title: Managing Director - Quality Control (Chief Inspector)
role.description:
Achieving our goals starts with supporting yours. Grow your career, access top-tier health and wellness benefits, build lasting connections with your team and our customers, and travel the world using our extensive route network. 
 
Come join us to create what’s next. Let’s define tomorrow, together. 

**Description**
---------------

At United, we have some of the best aircraft in the world. Our Technical Operations team is full of aircraft maintenance technicians, engineers, planners, ground equipment and facilities professionals, and supply chain teams that help make sure they’re well taken care of and ready to get our customers to their desired destinations. If you’re ready to work on our planes, join our Tech Ops experts and help keep our fleet in tip-top shape.

**Job Overview and Responsibilities**

The Chief Inspector provides executive-level leadership and oversight for aircraft inspection, quality control, and nondestructive testing programs to ensure the continued airworthiness, safety, reliability, and regulatory compliance of aircraft maintenance operations. This role serves as the designated FAR Part 119 Chief Inspector and is responsible for maintaining effective inspection systems, ensuring compliance with applicable FAA regulations and company standards, and promoting a strong safety and quality culture across the organization.

* Lead the Quality Control inspection and nondestructive testing (NDT) programs to ensure aircraft, engines, and components are inspected, maintained, and returned to service in an airworthy condition in accordance with all applicable regulatory, company, and industry requirements
* Coordinate with Maintenance, Engineering, Safety, Compliance, and other operational teams to resolve quality, airworthiness, and regulatory issues
* Serve as the FAA-designated Chief Inspector in accordance with 14 CFR Part 119 and assume final authority on all matters concerning aircraft, engine, and component airworthiness
* Partner with Director of Maintenance and Director of Safety and interface with FAA Certificate Management Office
* Establish and continuously improve inspection policies, procedures, authorizations, and oversight processes to ensure compliance with FAA regulations, Operations Specifications, the General Maintenance Manual, and accepted industry standards
* Provide inspection program support to the Continuous Airworthiness Maintenance Program (CAMP), participate in Continuing Analysis and Surveillance System (CASS) activities as a board member, and utilize inspection program findings to monitor performance, identify risks, and drive systemic corrective actions
* Determine qualification, training, certification, and competency requirements for Quality Control, inspection, and NDT personnel and ensure personnel maintain the knowledge, skills, and authorizations necessary to perform assigned functions
* Promote a culture of accountability, technical excellence, safety, and regulatory discipline within the inspection organization
* Operate the organization efficiently and effectively by ensuring that inspectors with the right qualifications are available to support Maintenance at the right time
* Provide oversight and on-site surveillance of essential maintenance providers and other external suppliers to verify compliance with regulatory requirements, company procedures, and airworthiness standards
* Develop and maintain the Required Inspection Item (RII) program to ensure maintenance activities affecting airworthiness receive appropriate independent inspection and oversight

**Qualifications**
------------------

#### **What’s needed to succeed (Minimum Qualifications):**

* B.S. degree in Engineering, Aviation Management or related field, or comparable experience
* Hold a mechanic certificate with both airframe and powerplant ratings, and have held these ratings for at least three years
* 10+ years of aircraft maintenance/inspection experience, including at least five years in a senior management role
* Extensive knowledge of FARs, aircraft equipment design and operational characteristics, aircraft maintenance materials and processes, including NDT processes
* Proven leadership experience managing technical personnel, cross-functional teams, and regulatory compliance activities
* Ability to interpret technical documentation, maintenance manuals, regulatory guidance, and company policies
* Must be legally authorized to work in the United States for any employer without sponsorship
* Successful completion of interview required to meet job qualification
* Reliable, punctual attendance is an essential function of the position

#### 

#### **What will help you propel from the pack (Preferred Qualifications):**

* Advanced degree

* Chicago, IL

Our Company's Animal Health Division offers veterinarians, farmers, pet owners and governments the widest range of veterinary pharmaceuticals, vaccines and health management solutions and services.
 
 
Our company's Animal Health Division is committed to operating its business in a way that is best suited to meet the unprecedented demands faced today. Its strategic goal is to achieve sustained growth through the continued provision of integrated solutions with innovative animal health products and services that meet the evolving needs of our customers.
 
 
**Purpose of the role:** 
As Director ATS (Analytical Technical Solutions) US lead your role is integral to shape our manufacturing & testing organization in line with the company strategy. You will be key member of the global ATS leadership team and collaborate with partners across other involved organizations.
 
 
In this role, you will be responsible for managing and developing the team, strategic planning and execution of the ATS project portfolio across multiple sites and platforms. You will provide valuable guidance and leadership for your team and be part of the overall governance to assure progress and deliverables against company priorities and programs.
 
 
Your expertise and direction will be crucial in guaranteeing smooth and reliable project deliverables & team performance. To excel in this position, end to end holistic understanding of pharmaceutical manufacturing involving operations, process, analytical, supply, financial, and other dependencies will be essential.
 
 
Comprehensive communication skills, ability to collaborate, big picture perspective and looking beyond own area of influence will complete the expected profile.
 
 
You will be part of an integrated team responsible for developing, planning, executing the regional company strategy. You will own, oversee and report out all related analytical activities being undertaken by your team.

role.title: Director of ITAD Operations
role.description:
**Director of ITAD Operations**

 

**A Candid Look at Our Culture**

Dynamic is a high-accountability, low-ego workplace. We take our work and commitments seriously, but we don't take ourselves too seriously.

At **Dynamic Lifecycle Innovations**, we give electronics their next best life while protecting our planet and our customers' interests. As a Certified Great Place to Work® since 2017, we've built a team culture that's rewarding, engaging, and FUN! But don't just take our word for it—see what our Team Members have to say.

**How We Hire: The Head, Heart, and Briefcase**

We believe great performance comes from alignment across three areas:

* **Head** – your natural behavioral drives and cognitive agility (measured by our Predictive Index assessment)
* ❤️**Heart** – your values, passions, and what drives you to make a meaningful impact
* **Briefcase** – your experiences, skills, and results from past roles

Every step of our process is designed to understand you in all three areas. It's how we ensure the best mutual fit, not just for what you can do, but for how you'll thrive here long-term.

**\*\*Required Step** **- You'll start with the Predictive Index (PI) assessment** (takes <20 minutes total), then move through structured interviews, work samples, and culture-focused interviews. We respect your time and promise clear, timely communication throughout.

**Location:** Onsite within our Onalaska, WI, or Hendersonville, TN facilities.

**Total Cash Compensation (Base + Bi-Annual Incentive):** $170,000 - $250,000

**Benefits Include:**

* Comprehensive health benefits starting the first of the month following hire
* 401(k) with company match
* Quarterly incentive opportunity
* Generous paid time off and paid holidays

**Your Purpose**

As the Director of ITAD Operations, you'll lead the people and operations that give technology its next best life. Our IT asset disposition (ITAD) facilities operate much like manufacturing environments, where production flow, labor planning, equipment, inventory, quality, and safety all contribute to performance. If you've led manufacturing operations and enjoy developing people while improving how work gets done, your experience could make a significant impact here.

Reporting to the Executive Vice President of ITAD, you'll turn strategy into results across Dynamic's primary and satellite facilities. You'll develop leaders, strengthen operational consistency, and use data and technology to improve efficiency, profitability, and customer satisfaction.

This is an opportunity to shape how our operations grow. From improving processes on the floor to building the capabilities needed across multiple locations, your leadership will help Dynamic process IT assets securely, efficiently, and profitably while advancing our mission.

**What You'll Do**

* **Lead operations across multiple facilities.** Turn business priorities into clear operating plans, align leaders around shared goals, and drive consistent execution across primary and satellite locations.
* **Develop leaders who develop their teams.** Coach, mentor, and empower your leaders to build team capability, own results, and prepare future leaders through training and succession planning.
* **Improve production flow and performance.** Apply Lean manufacturing practices, Gemba walks, and root cause analysis to remove bottlenecks, reduce waste, and improve productivity and quality.
* **Make performance visible and actionable.** Build dashboards and scorecards that help teams understand results, recognize issues early, and take ownership of improvement.
* **Connect operational decisions to profitability.** Manage labor, costs, and budgets while aligning production schedules and capacity with business demand and customer commitments.
* **Use technology to improve how work gets done.** Partner across teams to strengthen ERP use, inventory management, and process automation as operations grow.
* **Protect our people and our customers' trust.** Hold high standards for safety, quality, environmental compliance, and data security while ensuring customer assets are handled securely, and service commitments are met.

**What You Bring (Briefcase)**

* Bachelor's degree in operations management, business administration, engineering, supply chain management, or a related field. Additional relevant experience will be considered in lieu of formal education.
* Eight or more years of progressive operations leadership experience, including significant experience managing teams and operational performance. Demonstrated success leading complex, high-volume processing, manufacturing, reverse logistics, refurbishment, or ITAD operations.
* Experience leading operational teams across multiple facilities and developing leaders who deliver consistent results.
* Demonstrated success improving operational performance through continuous improvement, financial discipline, and data-informed decisions.
* Preferred: MBA
* Preferred: Knowledge of IT asset disposition, secondary markets for IT equipment and components, and the processing requirements of servers, networking equipment, storage systems, and GPUs.
* Preferred: Familiarity with R2, e-Stewards, NAID AAA, and ISO standards, along with ITAD data security and environmental compliance requirements.
* Preferred: Knowledge of Lean Six Sigma, Total Quality Management, or the Toyota Production System.

**Skills & Abilities (Head)**

* Strong knowledge of Lean manufacturing and continuous improvement practices, including Kaizen, 5S, Gemba walks, and root cause analysis.
* Financial acumen connecting operational decisions to gross margin, operating expenses, and overall profitability.
* Understanding of forecasting, labor and capacity planning, and Sales & Operations Planning.
* Ability to use ERP systems, inventory management technology, production planning, and automation to improve operations.
* Analytical skills to build actionable dashboards and scorecards that make performance visible in real time.
* Clear communication, active listening, and project management skills that help teams align and execute.
* Leadership skills in coaching, mentoring, training, delegation, and succession planning.

**❤️** **Who You Are (Heart)**

You're a leader who connects strategy with what happens on the floor. You set clear expectations, listen closely, and help people understand how their work contributes to the bigger picture. You're comfortable digging into the data, asking thoughtful questions, and working alongside your teams to solve problems.

You hold high standards for results and how they're achieved. You build accountability through trust, develop leaders who can own their decisions, and look for better ways to work without losing sight of safety, quality, or the customer. You bring the judgment to balance today's operational demands with the capabilities Dynamic needs for its next stage of growth.

**Why You'll Love Working Here**

**Purpose with Impact:** Help give electronics their "next best life" while protecting the planet 
 **Award-Winning Culture:** We put people first as a Certified Great Place to Work® since 2017 
**Executive Influence:** Shape long-term enterprise strategy with your executive peers

**Transform at Scale:** Lead the modernization of technology, data, and AI through growth
 **Build Something Lasting:** Dynamic is privately owned without PE – our focus is long-term, sustainable growth, and you'll help us build a foundation to enable decades of success

* **️** **Equal Employment Opportunity**

Dynamic Lifecycle Innovations is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to providing fair employment opportunities for all based on merit. For positions subject to state contract requirements, we adhere to state affirmative action obligations and take proactive steps to ensure equal opportunity in our hiring practices. We do not discriminate or make any employment decisions on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

You will lead day-to-day operations while fostering a positive, inclusive, and safety-first culture aligned with Enbridge’s values and expectations.

 

In this role, you will work collaboratively with internal teams, contractors, service providers, and community stakeholders to deliver strong operational and financial results. You will provide hands-on leadership across operations, maintenance, asset integrity, and compliance, while maintaining financial discipline and transparency. If you are an experienced leader who thrives in a dynamic operational environment, values continuous improvement, and takes pride in enabling reliable renewable energy production, apply today. #joinourteam

 

**What You Will Do**

* Lead safe and reliable operations by managing all operational and maintenance activities for wind turbines and Balance of Plant (BOP) assets, ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements (e.g., NERC, CIP, FAA) and Enbridge safety standards.

* Champion a strong safety culture by ensuring adherence to safety policies and procedures, overseeing contractor and partner performance, and ensuring timely and accurate reporting and investigation of safety incidents and metrics.

* Manage people and contractors on site, including daily supervision, site orientations, performance oversight, and effective engagement with service providers, landowners, and internal stakeholders.

* Execute asset maintenance and integrity plans, ensuring all preventive, corrective, and major maintenance activities are planned, scheduled, tracked, and completed to Enbridge standards using systems such as MAXIMO.

* Oversee compliance and operational excellence, conducting audits, monitoring performance, managing lost production, and proactively addressing operational issues in collaboration with operations, engineering, and asset management teams.

* Drive financial performance and accountability by developing and managing the facility’s budget, forecasts, P&L reporting, explaining variances, managing procurement and work orders, and identifying opportunities for cost optimization and efficiency.

Provide clear reporting and leadership visibility, delivering accurate facility performance, safety, environmental, and financial reporting, and representing Enbridge as a trusted, responsible partner in the operation of the facility. 

 

**What you bring:**

* Related university degree and seven-plus years’ experience OR nine ‐ plus years of previous field operations experience, OR equivalent mix of formal education and experience.

* Valid Driver’s License and ability to obtain a Passport.

* Minimum of 8 years of relevant experience including 3 years in a supervisory or management role.

* Strong electrical systems knowledge preferred, with ability to troubleshoot SCADA, substations, collection systems, and met towers; wind generation plant experience considered an asset.

* Demonstrated commitment to safety, ability to perform calmly under pressure, and strong problem‑solving and decision‑making capability.

* Proven people leadership, contract administration experience, and ability to build effective relationships with employees, contractors, landowners, municipalities, and community stakeholders.

Strong communication and integrity, customer-focused mindset, willingness to learn Enbridge systems and processes, and digital proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel) and Oracle. 

 

**Working Conditions:**

* This role will require being on-call (24/7) to respond to emergencies and/or maintenance needs of the site (on a pre-determined, scheduled basis).

* Plant Manager must reside within 75 miles of the site due to on-call requirements.

Travel may be required from time to time both within the United States and Canada (approximately 10-20%) 

 

The successful candidate will undergo various background screening that includes but is not limited to a 5-year driving record, criminal check, a company sponsored medical and drug testing.

 

**Physical Requirements:**

Must meet requirements of fit for work which includes, but is not limited to, demonstrating hand, arm, back and leg coordination needed to ascend and descend a wind tower and comply with a weight restriction of 132 kg (or 290lb) total climbing weight. Comfort with completing physically demanding tasks in all weather conditions and comfort working in enclosed spaces and at heights of 300 ft. Employee understands that these requirements may be modified at the Company's discretion.

Grasping, kneeling, light – moderate lifting (objects up to 45 pounds), reaching above shoulder, repetitive motion, sitting, standing, visual requirement (able to see screens, detect color coding, read fine print), hearing requirement.

 

**Mental Requirements:**

Ability to: understand, remember and apply oral and/or written instructions or other information, understand sophisticated problems and collaborate/explore alternative solutions, organize thoughts and ideas into understandable terminology, coordinate and prioritize work schedule on a short-term basis, make decisions which have moderate impact on the immediate work unit and monitor impact outside this area, understand and follow basic instructions and guidelines, complete routine forms, compose letters, outlines, memoranda and basic reports and connect with individuals via telephone.

Applicable compensation policies and guidelines apply to internal candidates.

* A flexible benefits program that allows each employee to select the level of coverage needed for their family in the areas of health, dental, insurance, and disability.

role.title: Slag Plant Manager
role.description:
Line of Business: Cement & White

### **About Us**

Heidelberg Materials is one of the world's largest suppliers of building materials. Heidelberg Materials North America operates over 450 locations across the U.S. and Canada with approximately 9,000 employees.

 

The Plant Manager role is based at our slag grinding facility in Cape Canaveral, FL and reports directly to the Vice President of Cement Operations.

 

### **What You’ll Be Doing**

 

* Leads plant safety program to ensure a safe working environment. Ensures all company safety policies are implemented and followed.

* Actively participate in the development of the plant’s objectives and oversee all aspects of daily plant production and maintenance activities to optimize plant performance.

* Provide input into plant capital plan and operation plan and effectively manage budget costs.

* Plans, coordinates and directs all production activities to ensure that Plant Operations goals and targets are realized.

* Analyzes plant activities on a daily basis to assess and recommend areas for improvements in production, quality or efficiency.

* Synchronizes production activities with quarry, maintenance, process and quality control activities to make certain that the plant is performing to highest standards.

* Manages the team to ensure production requirements are met.

* Oversee plant maintenance.

* Ensure that the maintenance and operation of equipment is at optimal levels.

* Guides and directs maintenance managers to minimize equipment downtime.

* Plans, organizes and oversees the annual plant shut down.

* Ensures HTC Maintenance initiatives are implemented.

* Leads and fosters the collaborative efforts of the plant staff to address operating methods, procedures, and problems toward continuous improvement of production quality and efficiency. Identifies training needs of plant staff and ensures that appropriate training is implemented.

* Fully support the company’s purchasing initiative and ensure that purchasing policies and contract management policies and procedures are adhered to in the plant.

* Work in partnership with Plant Purchasing personnel regarding the purchase of major equipment.

* In collaboration with Sales and Marketing stay abreast of customer requirements and concerns.

* Determine and oversee the timely resolution to issues stemming from production, quality, etc.

* Participate in community activities to continually promote plant/community relations.

* Works with the plant Quality Control Department to meet product specifications and production goals

* Ensure compliance with plant policies & procedures, safety, environmental, state and federal process regulations.

* Ensure implementation of company policies and procedures.

* Responsible for the flawless execution of the Plant on call schedule, participating as needed.

* Leads and fosters the collaborative efforts of the plant staff to address operating methods, procedures, and problems toward continuous improvement of production quality and efficiency.

### **What Are We Looking For**

* A College Degree in Engineering or related field.

* 5 or more years progressive experience managing operations in a slag grinding facility

* Synchronize production activities with quarry, maintenance, process and quality control activities to make certain that the plant is performing to highest standards.

* Manage the team to ensure production requirements are met.

* Oversee plant maintenance.

* Ensure that the maintenance and operation of equipment is at optimal levels.

* Guide and direct maintenance manager to minimize equipment downtime.

* In coordination with Plant Management, plan, organizes and oversee the annual plant shut down.

* Ensure HTC Maintenance initiatives are implemented.

* A high level of technical knowledge related to all aspects of cement manufacturing

* Familiar with Central Control operations, including the process control system in a preheater plant with a pre-calciner and alternate fuels experience an asset.

* Managerial and leadership competencies acquired in progressively more responsible positions in a non-unionized plant with the ability to perform in roles of both plant manager and direct reports on a relief basis.

* Ability to make timely, critical decisions, often under conditions of uncertainty and stress.

* Detailed knowledge about process equipment interlocking; Knowledge in mill liner installation and ball charge design.

* Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written.

* Proficient with windows-based PC software programs including MS Office, SAP and other applicable software programs.

* Ability to read and understand financial statements and cost reports, prepare budget and forecasts and to focus on and manage costs.

* Strong interpersonal, leadership and motivational skills.

* Ability to communicate effectively and interact as a team member in a Total Quality environment

### **What We Offer**

 

* Competitive base salary, $139,100 to $185,460 annually and participation in our annual incentive plan.
* 401(k) retirement savings plan with an automatic company contribution as well as matching contributions.
* Highly competitive benefits programs, including:

* + Medical, Dental, and Vision along with Prescription Drug Benefits
 + Health Savings Account (HSA), Health Reimbursement Account (HRA) and Flexible Spending Account (FSA)
 + AD&D, Short- and Long-Term Disability Coverage as well as Basic Life Insurance
 + Paid Bonding Leave, 15 days of Paid Vacation, 40 hours of Paid Sick Leave and 10 Paid Holidays

Equal Opportunity Employer - Minority / Female / Veteran / Disabled.

role.title: Manufacturing Execution Systems Senior Manager
role.description:
Ready to join a global leader in air movement and ventilation? At Greenheck Group, joining our team means more than just starting a job, it’s joining an award-winning culture prioritizing your growth and development. Our unwavering commitment in supporting our team members both personally and professionally has earned us national recognition time and time again. As an innovative, environmentally responsible manufacturer of commercial HVAC systems, Greenheck Group designs and manufactures industry-leading air movement and ventilation solutions through our family of trusted brands. Our products are found in commercial, institutional, and industrial facilities worldwide, from schools and hospitals to factories and stadiums. Since 1947, we’ve proudly invested in our people and our communities, fostering innovation, leadership, and opportunity at every level. We are more than products, we are a team of inspired people doing extraordinary things.

As a Manufacturing Execution Systems Senior Manager for Greenheck Group you will own product strategy and delivery across Greenheck Group’s full manufacturing-systems portfolio — Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), maintenance management, machine integration, machine/production monitoring (MDC), and automation. You will serve as the senior product leader for Manufacturing Execution Systems, directly leading the MES functional lead team, owning the roadmap for the Critical Manufacturing platform consolidation, and establishing enterprise standards and consistency for manufacturing technology across Greenheck Group’s plants. You will operate as the critical connective link between enterprise manufacturing systems and the business, IT, Divisional Systems teams, and the broader Operational Systems/CoE community.

**WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING**

* Program Leadership: Own the product roadmap and delivery across the full manufacturing-systems portfolio — MES, maintenance management, machine integration, machine/production monitoring (MDC), and automation — across all Greenheck production sites. Lead the end-to-end roadmap for the Critical Manufacturing platform consolidation, replacing legacy custom integrations and MII applications across Greenheck's production sites. Coordinate cross-functional teams, allocate resources, and co-manage project timelines with Program Management. Drive accountability throughout execution and establish aggressive, results-oriented goals for the team.
* Divisional & CoE Alignment: Serve as the critical point of alignment between enterprise MES capabilities and divisional/plant-level execution — partnering closely with the business, IT, Divisional Systems teams, and the other Operational Systems/CoE groups (e.g., Operational Excellence, Machine Automation/MDC) to ensure enterprise standards translate into plant-level adoption and results.
* Team Leadership: Build and lead the MES functional lead team across the MES, maintenance, machine integration, monitoring, and automation domains.
* Change Leadership: Facilitate organizational change related to MES and manufacturing-systems adoption; communicate to create buy-in and promote system acceptance across plant floors.
* Standards and Consistency: Drive manufacturing-systems standards and consistency across Greenheck production sites through an MES steering committee and governance framework spanning MES, maintenance, machine integration, monitoring, and automation.
* Communication: Provide status updates on timeline, cost, and risk to the Operational Systems and OT Executive Steering Committees; communicate with team, stakeholders, and senior/executive leaders.
* Strategic Planning: Set the vision and develop and execute a comprehensive manufacturing-systems strategy aligned with organizational goals; identify opportunities for process improvement, efficiency gains, and cost reduction across MES, maintenance, machine integration, monitoring, and automation.
* Collaboration: Work closely with the Sr Manager, ERP and Program/Project Management on shared roadmap, resourcing, and delivery dependencies; partner with external resources to ensure manufacturing systems align with business objectives.
* Best Practices: Stay current on MES, automation, and manufacturing-technology trends and bring forward platform recommendations.

**WHAT YOU SHOULD HAVE AS A MANUFACTURING EXECUTION SYSTEMS SENIOR MANAGER**

* 4 Year / bachelor’s degree in engineering, information systems, business, or a related field required
* Graduate Degree in engineering, information systems, or related field preferred
* 4-6 years of relevant work experience in MES implementation, project management or related fields required
* Strong understanding of manufacturing processes and production environments required
* Certification in project management preferred
* Experience with MES systems and their integration with ERP preferred
* 80/20 thinking
* Manufacturing experience and credibility
* Strong team building and leadership
* Systems and technology savvy
* Strategic thinking and leadership
* Action-oriented

**SOME THINGS WE THINK YOU SHOULD KNOW**

* Travel of 10 to 25% will be required for this role.
* This is an on-site role at our Schofield, WI location.

**COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

Greenheck Group takes pride in providing competitive total compensation along with a comprehensive benefits package as part of our total rewards program. The compensation for this role includes base salary along with the opportunity to earn additional variable compensation based on achieving specific performance metrics. The starting base pay range for this position is $160,353 - $198,083 and may vary based on factors such as job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and performance.

 

With best-in-class benefits, you can be the best you, and together, we can be the best in the industry. Visit our **Perks & Benefits page** for more information on these offerings:

 

* Health & Family Support
* Financial Security
* Learning & Development
* Rewards & Recognition
* Wellbeing & Mental Health
* Work-Life Balance
* Fun Perks

**SPECIAL NOTATION**

The preceding statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by people in this position. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills. The Employer retains the right to change or assign other duties to this position.

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS**

Work is performed in an office environment and requires the ability to operate standard office equipment, such as a computer and phone. Sedentary work. Exerting up to 10 pounds of force occasionally and/or negligible amount of force frequently or constantly to lift, carry, push, pull or otherwise move objects. Repetitive motion. Substantial motions of the wrists, hands, and/or fingers. The person is required to have close visual acuity to perform an activity such as: preparing and analyzing data, and figures; transcribing; viewing a computer terminal; extensive reading. Occasional mobility required to attend in-person meetings and complete various office tasks.

**EEO STATEMENT**

We are an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or veteran status.

**ACCOMMODATIONS REQUEST**

Greenheck Group complies with federal and state disability laws and makes reasonable accommodations for applicants and candidates with disabilities. To request an accommodation for the application or interview process, please email HR@greenheck.com with your name, job title, posting number, and requested accommodation.

**RECRUITING FRAUD ALERT**

At Greenheck Group, your personal information and online safety are our top priorities. Our recruiters will only direct candidates to apply through our official career page at https://greenheckgroup.com/careers/. We will never request payments, financial account details, or sensitive information such as Social Security numbers. If you’re unsure about the legitimacy of a message, please contact HR@greenheck.com for verification.

If you're looking for a place to grow while working with happy, enthusiastic, values-based people, you'll enjoy your career with us!

role.title: Senior Manager Operations
role.description:
Since 2018, Elevate Aircraft Seating has been enhancing the passenger experience through innovative aircraft seat design and manufacturing. With locations in California, Washington, and Germany we are guided by creativity, collaboration, and a shared commitment to quality.

We are looking for a skilled Senior Manager Operations to join our team in Santa Maria, CA. This is an on-site position based in Santa Maria, CA. We value teamwork, inclusivity, and continuous professional development, and we offer competitive benefits along with opportunities for growth.

**Export Control Requirements:**

**This position must meet U.S. export control compliance requirements. To meet U.S. export control compliance requirements, a “U.S. Person” as defined by 22 C.F.R. §120.62 is required. “U.S. Person” includes U.S. Citizen, U.S. National, lawful permanent resident, refugee, or asylee.**

**JOB SUMMARY**

The Senior Manager, Operations is responsible for leading and overseeing manufacturing operations and maintenance activities to ensure the achievement of safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and cost objectives. This role drives operational performance through effective resource planning, workforce development, and process optimization while supporting continuous improvement initiatives. Partnering cross-functionally, the Senior Manager implements operational strategies, promotes accountability, and ensures efficient manufacturing execution aligned with organizational and customer objectives.

**SUMMARY OF JOB DUTIES** - **Essential Functions****(Other duties and projects may be assigned or requested.)**

*Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions*

**Operational Leadership & Performance**

* Lead and oversee daily manufacturing operations and maintenance activities to achieve safety, quality, on-time delivery, productivity, labor efficiency, scrap reduction, and work-in-process (WIP) inventory objectives.
* Establish, monitor, and drive accountability for key operational performance indicators (KPIs), implementing corrective actions to address performance gaps.
* Support continuous improvement initiatives by identifying operational inefficiencies, collaborating with relevant stakeholders, and implementing improvements within manufacturing operations.

**Production Planning & Execution**

* Oversee all phases of manufacturing operations to ensure production activities comply with established procedures, quality standards, and approved manufacturing processes.
* Plan, coordinate, and optimize departmental activities, production schedules, and resource allocation to meet customer requirements and business objectives.
* Evaluate production capacity, workforce requirements, and operational constraints to ensure effective utilization of labor, equipment, and manufacturing resources.

**People Leadership & Workforce Development**

* Lead, develop, and manage production and associated functional teams, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and operational excellence.
* Oversee workforce planning, recruitment, onboarding, training, and employee development to maintain operational readiness.
* Establish performance expectations, evaluate employee performance, and partner with Human Resources on coaching, employee relations, corrective actions, and performance management.

**Quality, Safety & Regulatory Compliance**

* Ensure manufacturing operations adhere to established Quality Management System (QMS) requirements, AS9100 standards, applicable aerospace regulations, and internal policies and procedures.
* Promote a culture of safety, quality, and compliance by ensuring employees are appropriately trained and consistently follow established manufacturing procedures.

**Financial Management & Cross-Functional Collaboration**

* Manage departmental budgets, monitor operational expenditures, and implement cost-control measures to support financial objectives.
* Partner with Supply Chain, Planning, Quality, Engineering, Program Management, and other stakeholders to resolve operational challenges, align production priorities, and meet customer delivery commitments.

**Other**

* Maintain a safe, secure and legal work environment, adhering to all Company policies and procedures.
* Protect the confidentiality of the Company’s information and products.
* Contribute to team efforts by performing other job-related duties and projects as assigned or requested.

**GENERAL QUALIFICATIONS – Education, Knowledge, and Experience**

**Education**:

* High School Diploma or GED equivalent required.
* Associate degree, technical/trade certification, or bachelor’s degree in Manufacturing, Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field preferred.

**Experience**:

* 10+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing operations, including 5+ years in a leadership role overseeing production teams, operational performance, and manufacturing processes.
* Demonstrated success managing manufacturing operations in a complex, quality-driven production environment, with a focus on improving safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and cost performance.
* Proven ability to lead supervisors or managers, develop high-performing teams, and drive operational improvements across multiple manufacturing functions.

**Skills**:

* Strong leadership and people management skills, with the ability to develop teams, establish accountability, and manage employee performance.
* Proficiency in manufacturing operations, production planning, workforce allocation, and capacity management.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to interpret operational KPIs and implement effective corrective actions.
* Knowledge of budget management, cost control, and resource optimization within a manufacturing environment.
* Effective communication, organizational, and cross-functional collaboration skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and support business objectives.

**Preferred Skills/Experience:**

* Experience in aerospace manufacturing, aircraft interiors, or other highly regulated manufacturing environments, with knowledge of AS9100 and Quality Management Systems (QMS).
* Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or other continuous improvement methodologies.
* Experience utilizing Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems and manufacturing performance reporting tools.

**Other**:

* Extended or irregular hours may be required.
* Must be authorized to work in the United States.
* Elevate Aircraft Seating is an “at-will” employer; employment is at the mutual consent of both the employee and the employer, and may be terminated at will for any reason, with or without cause, at any time during employment with the Company.
* As business conditions warrant a change in the operating necessities of the Company, all employees are expected to react productively, handle other essential tasks assigned now or in the future.
* Tasks may vary slightly based on products produced at a division.

role.title: Sr. Director, Operational Excellence
role.description:
Sr. Director, Operational Excellence

**Position Summary**
====================

The Senior Director of Operational Excellence serves as a key strategic and operational partner to the Vice President of Operations, responsible for driving enterprise-wide operational initiatives, workforce optimization, project execution, and organizational effectiveness across CRH Healthcare.

This leader provides direct oversight of the centralized Provider Scheduling team, ensuring effective scheduling operations, proactive coverage planning, workforce utilization, and continuous process improvement. Additionally, the Sr. Director partners with regional and cross-functional leaders to translate strategic priorities into actionable plans, establish accountability, identify operational improvement opportunities, and ensure consistent execution across the organization. The position requires a balance of strategic thinking, hands-on leadership, financial acumen, and the ability to independently drive results in a complex, multi-site healthcare environment.

**Essential Responsibilities**
==============================

**Operational Excellence & Executive Support**
----------------------------------------------

* Serve as a strategic operational partner to the VP of Operations, translating enterprise priorities into actionable execution plans, establishing accountability across functional teams, and ensuring initiatives are delivered on time with measurable operational and financial outcomes.
* Develop and maintain standardized operational performance through reporting that identifies trends, variances, and opportunities across regions. Partner with operational leadership to develop corrective action plans, monitor progress, and ensure sustained improvement.
* Ensure operational excellence with vendors and processes that support the business, including procurement, surveys, and regulatory requirements.
* Support the VP of Operations in evaluating competing priorities, organizational capacity, and resource allocation to ensure alignment with enterprise objectives.
* Develop operational process workflow structure, and communication and training plans to implement, along with feedback loop and tracking to measure success and/or challenge.
* Other duties as assigned by the VP of Operations.

**Workforce Optimization**
--------------------------

* Direct and oversee the centralized Provider Scheduling team, including performance, workload, service expectations and escalation practices.
* Oversee provider scheduling processes, capacity visibility, coverage planning and coordination with regional operational leaders. Identify recurring coverage risks, utilization opportunities and avoidable scheduling disruptions.
* Coordinate with Operational Leadership, Talent Acquisition and Finance on workforce demand, hiring priorities, and labor cost trends.

**Project Management**
----------------------

* Lead full project lifecycle, from planning to closeout for operational initiatives.
* Establish project governance, prioritization, milestones, risks and executive reporting.
* Develop stakeholder engagement, communication, training and adoption plans to sustain operational change.
* Manage project scope, schedules, budgets, and deliverables effectively.

**Qualifications**
==================

* Bachelor’s degree in healthcare administration, business, operations or related field.
* 7+ years of progressive experience in healthcare operations, workforce management, project delivery or operational excellence.
* 5+ years of people leadership experience, including demonstrated success leading managers or functional teams multi-stie environment with a distributed field force.
* Experience supporting multi-site healthcare operations; urgent care or ambulatory care experience preferred.
* Proven ability to lead teams, drive change, influence business partners, and deliver operational results through data-driven decision making, stakeholder collaboration, and organizational influence.
* Strong project portfolio governance, change management, workforce analytics, financial acumen and stakeholder influence.
* Ability to lead through partnerships and remote workforce.
* Office based position with approximately 25% travel to company clinics.

*CRH Healthcare is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws. All offers are contingent upon successful completion of applicable credentialing, licensure verification, background review, and employment requirements.*

role.title: Senior Director, Franchise Operations
role.description:
**Job Description Summary:**

**Job Description**

 

The Senior Director Franchise Operations leads the Operations function across the South Region and is responsible for execution of the full portfolio across Coca-Cola United and all South Region Mainstream bottlers, translating aligned business strategies into integrated operating plans, disciplined marketplace execution, and sustainable performance. The role shapes regional operating priorities, recommends resource allocation, and aligns bottler regional operations teams and cross-functional partners to deliver volume, revenue, transactions, share, and profitable growth objectives. The role connects strategic planning with frontline execution, leads the regional performance agenda, and resolves cross-market execution barriers within delegated authority. As the direct people leader of the Franchise Operations team, the Senior Director sets clear accountabilities and develops Directors’ commercial judgment, financial acumen, and general management capabilities. The role partners with commercial, strategy, and transformation leaders to incorporate aligned initiatives into core operating plans without duplicating their functional mandates.

 

**What You’ll Do for Us**

 

* Lead the South Region Franchise Operations performance agenda for the full portfolio across Coca-Cola United and all South Region Mainstream bottlers, driving profitable volume, revenue, transactions, and share growth through clear priorities, integrated operating plans, and accountable execution with bottler partners.

* Expand market potential through Share of Visual Inventory (SOVI), Cold Drink Equipment (CDE), day one minute one innovation execution, and best-in-class conversion of category and commercial plans into outlet-level growth.

* Strengthen bottler operating partnerships by aligning regional, division, and sales-center teams on growth corridors across customers, channels, brands, and packages, securing shared execution commitments through influence rather than direct authority over bottler operations.

* Lead the Franchise Operations contribution to annual and long-range business planning, translating aligned South Region growth priorities into geography-specific operating plans, capability requirements, execution milestones, and measurable business outcomes.

* Assess differences in market potential and performance across bottlers and geographies; recommend operating priorities, resource deployment, and short- and long-term interventions to the VP, and lead implementation of agreed choices.

* Directly lead the Franchise Operations team, setting individual objectives and decision rights, managing performance, and holding Directors accountable for business commitments, bottler partnership, and execution follow-through across their assigned geographies.

* Develop the next generation of franchise leaders through regular coaching, actionable feedback, individual development and succession plans, and cross-functional assignments that build commercial judgment, financial acumen, strategic problem-solving, and general management capabilities while delivering current-role results.

* Lead weekly and monthly regional performance routines, integrating revenue, volume, share, transactions, and execution indicators into clear diagnoses, decisions, named owners, and time-bound actions—not reporting alone.

* Hold Directors accountable for identifying root causes of performance gaps and agreeing corrective actions with bottler regional operations teams; track recovery, adjust plans, and escalate unresolved risks and material trade-offs to the VP with clear recommendations.

* Manage discretionary budgets and deploy resources within approved authority, balancing growth potential, regional business needs, expected returns, and bottler execution capacity; recommend investment trade-offs and additional resource needs

* Lead regional deployment of aligned commercial strategies and growth initiatives, partnering with commercial, strategy, and transformation leaders to establish operational readiness, clear sequencing, ownership, and adoption within core business plans.

* Lead development and activation of contingency plans with bottler and cross-functional partners to protect annual business plan delivery across revenue, volume, share, net outlets, SOVI, and pricing execution; define recovery milestones and monitor results.

* Build execution capability with bottler regional operations teams through targeted training, effective scorecards, and disciplined business routines; identify successful market practices and lead adoption across relevant South Region geographies.

* Partner with franchise commercial leaders to lead the bi-monthly planning process, integrating customer, channel, marketing, finance, and supply-chain inputs into a coherent regional execution agenda with clear priorities and bottler commitments.

Maintain a regular in-market cadence with Directors and bottler regional operations teams to validate outlet execution, learn from frontline teams and customers, and understand execution barriers; bring the voice of the market into regional decisions, capability priorities, and future business plans. 

 

**Qualifications & Requirements**

 

* Bachelor’s degree with a Master’s degree is preferred.

* 10 or more years in a CPG organization across sales, key account, franchise management, or operations, including P&L responsibility, direct people management, and leadership of business execution across multiple geographies.

* Demonstrated success translating annual and long-range strategies into integrated operating plans, forecasting business performance, managing customer and distributor relationships, and leading corrective actions that deliver sustained growth.

* Strong commercial and financial judgment, including experience with revenue and operating P&Ls, investment trade-offs, resource prioritization, selling, and negotiation in a complex franchise or entrepreneurial environment.

* Strong understanding of channel marketing, customer and outlet execution, syndicated research, and competitive analysis, with the ability to combine data and frontline insights to identify growth opportunities and execution priorities.

* Proven ability to lead and develop experienced individual contributors through clear expectations, performance management, coaching, individual development plans, and succession planning.

* The ability to influence outcomes and be persuasive.

The Coca-Cola Company will not offer sponsorship for employment status (including, but not limited to, H1-B visa status and other employment-based nonimmigrant visas) for this position. Accordingly, all applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis and must not require The Coca-Cola Company's sponsorship to continue to work legally in the United States.

**Skills:**

Business Integrations, Business Planning, Channel Management, Execution Excellence, High Impact Communication, Market Dynamics, Negotiation, Revenue Growth Management, Value Chain Economics

**Pay Range:**

United States: 198,000 - 230,000 USD


*Base pay offered may vary depending on geography, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. A full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits, dependent on the position, is offered.*

**Annual Incentive Reference Value Percentage:**

50

**Long-term Incentive Reference Value Percentage:**

20

United States of America

Atlanta

26% - 50%

Yes

November 13, 2026

We are taking deliberate action to nurture an inclusive culture that is grounded in our company purpose, to refresh the world and make a difference. We act with a growth mindset, take an expansive approach to what’s possible and believe in continuous learning to improve our business and ourselves. We focus on four key behaviors – curious, empowered, inclusive and agile – and value how we work as much as what we achieve. We believe that our culture is one of the reasons our company continues to thrive after 130+ years. Visit Our Purpose and Vision to learn more about these behaviors and how you can bring them to life in your next role at Coca-Cola.

role.title: Director of Quality Assessment and Compliance
role.description:
Description:

Looking for a rewarding career that makes a difference in children’s lives? Look no further and join the team at Meeting Street! Meeting Street is a special place of learning, where children of all abilities have the opportunities to reach their fullest potential.

Full-time employees receive:

* Competitive Pay
* Generous PTO
* 13 paid holidays
* Medical, dental, vision and MORE

Meeting Street is currently looking for a Director of Quality Assessment and Compliance for 40 hours per week.

Duties:

* Oversees compliance of all client and student records, including electronic records, professional licensing, HIPAA, FERPA, Department of Education and Department of Health requirements and any other applicable state and/or federal requirements.
* Works with all programs and services to direct and monitor compliance issues and ensures timely investigation and resolution.
* Ensures that management and employees are in compliance with the rules and regulations of regulatory agencies and that policies and procedures are being followed.
* Keeps abreast of new compliance and regulatory issues and related policies and procedures.
* Works with Human Resources and others as appropriate to develop an effective compliance training program, including appropriate introductory training for new employees as well as ongoing training for all employees and managers.
* Designs and develops standardized operational, management, and ad hoc reports. Works with user community to understand reporting needs; identifies sources.
* Manages Learning Management System (LMS) enrolling new hires and working with managers on proper training for employees.

Meeting Street believes the dignity of each person is paramount. We recognize that our community’s future strength rests firmly on our commitment to our values of respect, *compassion, integrity, inclusivity, and excellence.* To uphold these commitments, we expect all employees to recognize and properly respond to racism and other forms of injustice.

*It is our policy to recruit, hire, train, transfer and promote employees, and to ensure that all other employment practices (i.e. salary and benefits administration, education and training programs, and social and recreational programs) are administered without regard to race, color, religion, marital status, gender, sexual preference or orientation, gender expression or identity, age, national origin or ancestry, legally recognized disability, citizenship status, genetic information, veteran status, military status, socioeconomic background, homelessness or any other characteristic or category protected by law. It is also our policy to protect employees and applicants from any coercion, retaliation or discrimination for filing a complaint or assisting in any investigation pursuant to the equal opportunity laws.*

L*earn more about us at* *https://www.meetingstreet.org*

Requirements:

* Bachelor’s Degree preferred.
* Experience in a business role working in compliance, privacy, quality assurance, non-financial audits and/or assessments; history of non-profit management a plus.
* LMS experience preferred
* Staff and Management experience and interaction – with an emphasis on sharing information, creating dialogue and explaining policies and procedures in a manner that is clearly understood by a diverse group of stakeholders.
