role.title: Director of Quality & Food Safety - St. Louis, MO
role.description:
**CoffeeBeverage Manufacturing | St. Louis, MO** **Know quality. Know food safety. Know coffee? Let's talk.** Ronnoco Beverage Solutions is looking for an experienced Director of QualityFood Safety to lead quality, food safety, regulatory compliance, and continuous improvement across our manufacturing and warehousing operations.This is an opportunity to take your quality experience beyond a single production floor. You'll help set the standards that protect our products, our customers, and the consistency consumers expect from every cup. **What You'll Lead** **CoffeeBeverage Quality**Oversee quality standards across coffee, tea, and beverage products, from specifications and testing to packaging, labeling, warehousing, and customer requirements. The role works with product evaluation that includes the taste and aroma of coffee, tea, and beverage products.**Food SafetyRegulatory Compliance**Lead programs and audits involving SQF, HACCP, GMP, FDA, Kosher, Organic, and applicable health department requirements, while strengthening consistent food safety and sanitation standards across operations.**Quality SystemsContinuous Improvement**Use quality data, performance trends, operating practices, and controls to identify opportunities for improvement and build stronger, more consistent quality systems across company locations.**CustomerProduct Quality**Own product specifications, quality alerts, customer complaints, corrective actions, and quality issues involving packaging, labeling, order picking, and hand-packing.**Product HoldsRework**Partner with the Green Bean buyer on product holds and rework while directing the disposition of overage and damaged product.**Quality LeadershipTraining**Work alongside operations and cross-functional teams to develop clear, practical quality processes. You'll also oversee employees performing laboratory and quality testing and help identify and deliver quality-related training. **What We're Looking For** **You may be a great fit if you bring:**

* Bachelor's degree in a related field
* 3–5 years of quality and regulatory experience in food manufacturing
* Experience supporting quality programs across multiple locations
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
* The ability to spot trends in data and turn findings into action
* Experience with Microsoft Dynamics/Great Plains or a similar ERP
* Strong attention to detail and the ability to work independently
* A proactive, solutions-oriented approach

**Not a Desk-Only Quality Role** **You'll be where the product is.**The position blends office-based leadership with hands-on time in production, warehouses, laboratories, and receiving areas, including environments associated with roasting and processing. Travel of up to 25% to company facilities, co-manufacturers, suppliers, and customer sites is expected. **Ready to Make Your Mark on Every Cup?**If you're a quality professional who understands the discipline behind great food and beverage manufacturing and you're ready to influence quality across multiple operations, we'd like to hear from you. **Bring your expertise. Raise the standard. Help us protect the quality behind every cup.**Apply today to join Ronnoco Beverage Solutions in St. Louis.

role.title: Plant Manager
role.description:
**Employee Type:**

Full time

**Location:**

MD Cambridge

**Job Type:**

Production Operations

**Job Posting Title:**

Plant Manager

**About Us:**

TreeHouse Foods is a leading manufacturer of private label packaged foods and beverages, operating a network of over 20 production facilities and several corporate offices across the United States and Canada. At TreeHouse Foods, our commitment to excellence extends beyond our products and revolves around our people. We are investing in talent and creating a performance-based culture where employees can do their best work and develop their careers, directly impacting our mission to make high quality, affordable food for our customers, communities, and families. We hope you will consider joining the team and being part of our future.

Named one of America’s Best Large Employers by Forbes Magazine, we are proud to live by a strong set of values and strive to "Engage and Delight – One Customer at a Time." Guided by our values— **Own It, Commit to Excellence, Be Agile, Speak Up, and Better Together.** We are a diverse team driven by integrity, accountability, and a commitment to exceptional results. We embrace change, prioritize continuous learning, and foster collaboration, transparency, and healthy debate. Together, we set each other up for success to achieve enterprise-wide goals.

**What You Gain:**

* Competitive compensation and benefits program with no waiting period – you’re eligible from your first day!
* 401(k) program with 5% employer match and 100% vesting as soon as you enroll.
* Comprehensive paid time off opportunities, including immediate access to four weeks of vacation, five sick days, parental leave and 11 company holidays (including two floating holidays).
* Leaders who are invested in supporting your accelerated career growth, plus paid training, tuition reimbursement and a robust educational platform – DevelopU – with more than 10,000 free courses to support you along the way.
* An inclusive working environment where you can build meaningful work relationships with a diverse group of professionals. Take advantage of opportunities to build on our team-oriented culture, such as joining one of our Employee Resource Groups.
* Access to our wellness and employee assistance programs.

**Job Description:**

***About the Role:***

 

We are seeking a Plant Manager for our Cambridge, MD, facility, a leading manufacturer of quality aseptic products. This role is responsible for providing overall leadership and accountability for plant operations with a strong focus on delivering results. In partnership with the site leadership team, the Plant Manager will drive employee engagement, safety, quality, customer service, continuous improvement, cost management, and production performance to meet or exceed business objectives. The successful candidate will identify and implement strategic opportunities to improve operational efficiency, safety, throughput, productivity, schedule attainment, cost reduction, and product quality while fostering a positive and high-performing work environment.

 

***You will add value to this role by performing various functions including, but not limited to:***

* Providing coaching and leadership to team members in the areas of employee engagement, safety, quality, customer service, continuous improvement, cost, and equipment reliability to elevate the team’s performance.
* Promoting a safety culture and ensuring adherence to all health and safety policies/protocols.
* Leading the development, execution, and monitoring of the operations strategy in line with the overall operational objectives to achieve safety, quality and performance improvement and ensure achievement of manufacturing goals.
* Leading the continuous improvement program to deliver opportunities in cost, quality, food safety and service.
* Utilizing available data including OEE, line speed target, and efficiency and process data to continuously improve productivity, uptime, and reliability.
* Coordinating manufacturing activities with all other functions of the organization and suppliers to obtain optimum production and utilization of human resources, machines, and equipment.
Contribute to the development and execution of strategic plant-wide initiatives. 

 

***Important Details:***

* This is a full-time, on-site role on first shift. Occasional flexibility is required to support alternate shifts.
The anticipated compensation for this position ranges from $154,700.00 - 232,100.00 USD annually. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, shift, travel requirements, sales or revenue-based metrics and business or organizational needs. For certain roles, the successful candidate may be eligible for annual discretionary merit compensation award, bonus and equity pay. 

 

***You’ll fit right in if you have:***

* High school diploma or equivalent is required; Bachelor's degree in manufacturing, industrial technology, or related field is preferred.
* Minimum of five years of leadership experience in a production or food manufacturing environment.
* Strong leadership and team management skills.
* Experience leading in a union environment is preferred.
* Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing Principles.
* Knowledge of safety regulations, quality control procedures, and inventory management.
* Excellent problem-solving, troubleshooting, and decision-making skills.
Proficient in Microsoft Office. 

**Your TreeHouse Foods Career is Just a Click Away!**

Click on the “Apply” button or go directly to www.treehousefoods.com/careers to let us know you’re ready to join our team!

*At TreeHouse Foods, we embrace diversity and inclusion for innovation and growth. We are committed to building inclusive teams and an equitable workplace for our employees to bring their true selves to work to help us “Engage and Delight – One Customer at a Time”.* *TreeHouse Foods is an Equal Opportunity Employer that prohibits discrimination or harassment of any type. All qualified applicants are considered for employment without regard to race, color, national origin, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Applicants who require an accommodation to participate in the job application or hiring process should contact* *disability-accommodations@treehousefoods.com*

role.title: Plant Manager - Alaska Naturals Bellingham
role.description:
Overview:

Trident Seafoods is North America’s largest vertically integrated seafood company—partnering with fishermen, employees, and communities to responsibly harvest, process, and share wild Alaska seafood with the world. With deep roots in Alaska and operating across the globe, Trident is a privately held company headquartered in Seattle, committed to nourishing the world while upholding the highest standards for safety, sustainability, and excellence.

At Trident Seafoods, we work together for something bigger than ourselves. From nourishing the world with the best protein on earth to protecting our oceans, serving our fishermen, and supporting communities in Alaska and beyond, here, you’ll find a values-driven culture where your growth matters, your work has purpose and your contributions are recognized and appreciated—because at Trident, we believe meaningful work connects us all.

Responsibilities:

**Summary:**

The Plant Manager leads all operations for Trident Seafoods’ Alaska Naturals facility in Bellingham, Washington, which produces fish oil and related nutritional products. This role has overall accountability for safe, reliable, compliant, and cost-effective plant performance, including production, quality, maintenance, technical processes, people leadership, and financial results.

The Plant Manager provides hands-on leadership in a specialized manufacturing environment and works closely with a small, experienced technical team to maintain process control, resolve complex production issues, improve yield and throughput, and ensure products consistently meet customer and regulatory requirements. role.title: Director of Operations
role.description:
The Director of Operations owns every operational outcome at Bold Reuse: sanitation, logistics, inventory, quality, safety, and operating cost, in every market we serve. You will build and run the wash hubs that wash, sort, inspect, and recirculate millions of reusable items, and you will stand up new facilities fast without sacrificing quality or unit economics. This is a hands-on, in-person role based at a Bold Reuse operations facility in Seattle, WA or Portland, OR, with occasional travel to our other markets. You report to the CEO and lead the managers who run our wash hubs.

### **About Bold Reuse**

Bold Reuse is a full-service reuse platform that eliminates single-use waste. We’ve already eliminated more than 8 million pounds of packaging from the landfill, and we’re just getting started! Our mission is to make the circular economy a reality for any business that wants to reduce its packaging waste.

### **Description**

**Director of Operations**
==========================

**About Bold Reuse**
====================

Bold Reuse is a full-service reuse platform that eliminates single-use waste. We have already kept more than 10 million packaging items out of landfill. We serve stadiums, campuses, arenas, and large events, and we are now scaling our operations footprint to new markets across the US.

 
 

**The Role**
------------

The Director of Operations owns every operational outcome at Bold Reuse: sanitation, logistics, inventory, quality, safety, and operating cost, in every market we serve. You will build and run the operations facilities that wash, sort, inspect, and recirculate millions of reusable items, and you will stand up new facilities fast without sacrificing quality or unit economics.

 
 

This is a hands-on, in-person role based at a Bold Reuse operations facility in Portland, OR, Seattle, WA, San Francisco or Los Angeles, CA with occasional travel to our other markets. You report to the CEO and lead the managers who run our wash hubs.

 
 

We are looking for someone who treats every process as improvable: fewer touches per item, lower cost per unit, higher throughput, and zero quality escapes. When something goes wrong in operations, you own the fix, the root cause, and the system that prevents it from happening again.

Our main product is our service. Stadiums, arenas, and event operators stake their guest experience, their sustainability commitments, and their brand on our service working every time. A late delivery, a short count, or a cleanliness issue is not an internal problem; it is a failure our client feels in front of tens of thousands of fans. This leader must make decisions with that client impact in front of mind, every day and at every site.

 
 

**What You Will Own**
---------------------

End-to-end operational ownership

* Own the full operating P&L for sanitation and logistics across all markets, including labor, consumables, equipment, and facilities.
* Own operational KPIs and report on them weekly: throughput, cost per item, touches per item, on-time and in-full delivery, client service-level adherence, client satisfaction, quality escapes, and safety incidents.
* Be the single accountable owner for operational problems. Lead root-cause analysis and put permanent corrective actions in place, not workarounds.
* Own service delivery for clients, including readiness, staffing, and post-event recovery.

Client success through operational excellence

* Treat client outcomes as the ultimate measure of operational performance. Our clients succeed only when our operations run flawlessly.
* Understand each major client's operating model, event calendar, and sustainability goals, and design service to support them.
* Define and meet service-level commitments for every account: delivery windows, inventory availability, cleanliness, and recovery rates.
* Partner closely with Customer Success and Sales on onboarding, event readiness, and account reviews, so operational capability and client promises stay aligned.
* Weigh client impact in every operational decision, from staffing and scheduling to process changes and cost reductions.
* When service falls short, own the client communication alongside Customer Success, deliver the fix fast, and follow up with a clear corrective plan.

Scaling physical operations facilities

* Plan, launch, and ramp new wash and logistics facilities in new markets, from site selection and layout through equipment install, hiring, training, and steady-state operation.
* Build a repeatable market-launch playbook so each new plant reaches target throughput and cost faster than the last.
* Run capacity planning across markets so that equipment, labor, and inventory stay ahead of contracted demand.
* Make build, buy, and partner decisions on equipment and facilities, with clear ROI cases.

Efficiency, touch reduction, and cost

* Map every process from pickup to recirculation and systematically remove touches, handoffs, and waste.
* Apply lean and continuous-improvement methods (for example, value-stream mapping, standard work, 5S, kaizen) to raise throughput and cut cost per item.
* Identify and implement automation in sorting, washing, drying, inspection, and packing where the ROI supports it.
* Partner with product and engineering to embed operational data into our Circular Intelligence System and use it to drive decisions.

Quality control and food safety

* Own the quality management system for sanitation, including written standards, inspection points, testing, documentation, and audit readiness.
* Ensure every item meets food-contact sanitation standards and applicable health department and client requirements.
* Track and drive down defects, rewash rates, and damaged or lost inventory.
* Lead customer-facing quality responses and corrective action plans when issues occur.

Supply chain and inventory

* Manage inventory of reusable serviceware across its full lifecycle: procurement, deployment, return, loss, and retirement.
* Manage suppliers of equipment, chemicals, and materials, ensuring supply keeps pace with rapid growth at the right cost.

People and leadership

* Hire, develop, and lead market managers, and through them, hourly operations teams.
* Set clear goals and standards while giving local teams autonomy to solve problems.
* Build a culture of safety, accountability, and continuous improvement.
* Identify and advance top performers ready for greater responsibility.
 

 

**What You Bring**
------------------

Required

* 7+ years of operations leadership in manufacturing, warehousing, distribution, commercial laundry, food processing, or similar high-volume physical operations, including 5+ years managing managers.
* A proven record of rapidly scaling physical operations: opening or expanding plants, warehouses, or processing facilities and ramping them to target throughput and cost on a tight timeline.
* Demonstrated results driving efficiency, with specific examples of reducing touches, labor hours, or cost per unit through process redesign, lean methods, or automation.
* Hands-on experience building and managing quality control programs, including standards, inspection, corrective action, and audits. Food-safety or sanitation experience strongly preferred.
* Experience running client-facing or service-level-driven operations, where operational performance directly determined customer outcomes and retention.
* Full P&L or cost-center ownership for an operation, with a track record of hitting budget.
* Strong analytical skills: you build ROI cases, run operations on data, and are comfortable with operational systems and dashboards.
* Clear, direct written and verbal communication with teams, executives, and enterprise clients.

Preferred

* Experience in a fast-growing startup or a multi-site rollout.
* Lean Six Sigma (Green Belt or higher) or equivalent continuous-improvement training.
* Experience with commercial dishwashing, sanitation equipment, or reverse logistics.
* Experience with HACCP, ServSafe, or health department compliance.
* Experience supporting large live events or venues.
 

 

**Our Values and Competency Expectations**
------------------------------------------

At Bold Reuse, how we work matters as much as what we do. The Director of Operations is expected to model these competencies, with Ownership as the defining one for this role.

* Ownership: Owns outcomes across every operational activity, not just effort. Recognizes that our clients' success depends on our operations and acts accordingly. Anticipates problems before they reach clients, makes decisions without waiting, and closes the loop on root causes. Holds self and team accountable to measurable results.
* Boldness: Challenges how work is done and brings solutions, not just problems. Takes smart risks, weighing impact on customers and the business.
* Intentionality: Prioritizes by impact and urgency. Makes thoughtful decisions aligned with values and business goals. Models reliability and professionalism.
* Leadership: Builds alignment across people and teams. Delegates and creates ownership in others. Addresses conflict directly to maintain trust and momentum.
* Collaborative: Works across functions, synthesizes input, and raises the quality of work through feedback.
* Adaptable: Adjusts to changing conditions while keeping rigor and follow-through. Helps others navigate change.
* Loving: Shows emotional intelligence in hard moments. Supports teammates' growth and well-being. Models resilience and a growth mindset.
 

 

**Compensation and Benefits**
-----------------------------

This position has a salary range of $110,000 to $120,000 per year. This range is a good-faith estimate; the final offer depends on qualifications and experience. The package also includes equity options, medical, dental, and vision insurance, paid holidays, and paid time off. We can only hire US-based candidates at this time.

 
 

**How to Apply**
----------------

Send your resume and a cover letter to [email protected]. In your cover letter, describe a process you developed that measurably cut touches or cost, and an example of a time your operation's performance made or broke a customer's success.

 

#### **Salary**

$110,000 - $120,000 per year

role.title: Senior Manager - Technology Operations Engineering
role.description:
Joining Amex Tech means discovering and shaping your contribution to something big. Here, you can work alongside talented tech teams and build a unique career with the Powerful Backing of American Express. With a range of opportunities to work with the latest technologies, and a commitment to back the broader engineering community through open source, our mission is to power your success. Because Amex Tech is powered by our technology, our culture, and our colleagues.

We are seeking an experienced and technically strong **Senior Manager – Technology Operations Engineering** to lead Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), Application Production Support, and operational excellence for enterprise Contact Center Transformation platforms.

This role will be responsible for ensuring the **end-to-end availability, reliability, performance, scalability, and operational stability** of mission-critical voice platforms, contact center applications, cloud-native services, intelligent voice bots, and AI-powered customer engagement solutions.

The ideal candidate will have extensive hands-on experience with **Google Cloud Platform (GCP), SRE practices, enterprise application support, Five9, Genesys, telephony technologies, full-stack observability, distributed tracing, and incident management** . The role also requires knowledge of emerging technologies, including Agentic AI frameworks, AI agent monitoring, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.

The Senior Manager will lead engineering teams responsible for 24x7 production support, proactive monitoring, incident resolution, problem management, change management, automation, and continuous reliability improvements across complex, distributed contact center ecosystems.

 

* **Education & Professional Experience:** Bachelor's degree in computer science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience, with **10+ years of experience** in Technology Operations, Site Reliability Engineering, Application Production Support, or Cloud Engineering, including **5+ years in technical leadership or engineering management roles** .

* **Site Reliability Engineering & Application Support:** Extensive hands-on experience in **SRE, enterprise application production support, distributed systems, microservices, REST APIs, application performance troubleshooting, service reliability, and 24x7 production operations** , including on-call support and critical incident resolution.

* **Google Cloud Platform (Mandatory):** Strong hands-on experience with **Google Cloud Platform (GCP)** and cloud-native technologies, including GKE, Cloud Run, Compute Engine, Pub/Sub, Cloud Monitoring, Cloud Logging, API Gateway, cloud networking, load balancing, and containerized application environments.

* **Contact Center & Telephony Expertise:** Proven experience supporting **Five9, Genesys, or similar enterprise contact center platforms** , with a strong understanding of telephony architecture, SIP, RTP, IVR, ACD, CTI, call routing, intelligent voice bots, and contact center integrations. Experience with SpeechMiner or comparable speech analytics platforms is highly desirable.

* **Full-Stack Observability & Distributed Tracing:** Strong experience with **Grafana, Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, OpenTelemetry, distributed tracing, centralized logging, application performance monitoring, and cloud observability tools** , including the ability to implement end-to-end monitoring and troubleshoot complex distributed application issues.

* **AI, Agentic AI & MCP Technologies:** Experience or strong working knowledge of **conversational AI, intelligent voice bots, Large Language Models (LLMs), Agentic AI frameworks, AI agent monitoring, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers** , including AI workflow observability, execution tracing, integration troubleshooting, and operational reliability.

* **Incident, Problem & Change Management:** Demonstrated expertise in **ITIL-based Incident, Problem, and Change Management** , including major incident leadership, root cause analysis, production change coordination, escalation management, on-call operations, and continuous service improvement.

* **Database & Application Integration Technologies:** Hands-on experience supporting **NoSQL databases, Google Cloud Firestore, Oracle Database, APIs, middleware, and distributed application architectures** , with strong troubleshooting capabilities across database performance, connectivity, transaction processing, and enterprise integrations.

* **Networking, Infrastructure & Automation:** Strong understanding of **TCP/IP, DNS, HTTPS, SIP/RTP, firewalls, load balancers, traffic routing, cloud networking, Kubernetes, and containerized environments** , along with experience in automation, scripting, CI/CD pipelines, and tools such as Python, Bash, or Terraform.

* **Technical Leadership & Operational Excellence:** Proven ability to lead engineering teams, manage complex production environments, collaborate across technology organizations, and drive **SRE maturity, operational automation, observability improvements, incident reduction, service reliability, disaster recovery readiness, and continuous engineering excellence** , supported by strong communication, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

Employment eligibility to work with American Express in the United States is required as the company will not pursue visa sponsorship for these positions.

role.title: Director of Operations
role.description:
### **At Materion, everyone is included, respected and offered opportunity to grow.** ***Join us!***

**Position Summary**
====================

The Director of Operations, Premium Targets provides strategic and operational leadership for a complex, multi-site manufacturing organization with domestic and international operations. This leader is accountable for safety, quality, delivery, cost, customer performance, talent development, capital execution, and continuous improvement. The individual in this role will lead Operations, Supply Chain, and Engineering teams, including manufacturing facilities across multiple locations. As the organization’s senior operations safety leader, the Director sets clear expectations, models visible safety leadership, empowers employees to identify and address hazards, and holds leaders accountable for proactive risk reduction and continuous EHS improvement. Working across Technology, Quality, Supply Chain, Commercial, Engineering, EHS, and other functions, the Director translates business priorities into sustainable results, standardizes manufacturing and business processes, and delivers exceptional service to internal and external customers. The role also leads operations strategy and financial performance, including gross margin, inventory turns, and cost management.

**Operations Leadership and Execution**
=======================================

* Lead a proactive, prevention-focused safety culture in which every employee is empowered and expected to identify hazards, stop unsafe work, and take ownership of a safe and healthy workplace.
* Lead manufacturing operations across Buffalo, Wheatfield, Albuquerque, Limerick, and Brewster, with strong matrix partnerships supporting Alzenau and Taiwan.
* Own performance across safety, quality, delivery, cost, reliability, and customer commitments; establish clear metrics, review performance routinely, and hold site leaders accountable for results.
* Set and execute the Premium Targets operations strategy, multi-year roadmap, and long-range capital and workforce plans.
* Ensure facilities consistently deliver high-quality products on time to internal business units and external customers.
* Partner with Technology, Quality, Supply Chain, Commercial, Engineering, EHS, and other functions to align priorities and improve end-to-end performance.
* Develop, coach, and hold operational leaders accountable for business results, team effectiveness, and talent growth.
* Strengthen communication, operating discipline, and knowledge sharing across all Premium Targets facilities.
* Provide clear, timely business updates and recommendations to senior leaders and key stakeholders.

**Operational Excellence, Strategy, and Capital Leadership**
------------------------------------------------------------

* Champion EHS excellence by ensuring regulatory compliance, audit readiness, effective risk assessments, timely incident and near-miss investigation, corrective-action closure, and consistent use of leading and lagging safety indicators.
* Serve as executive sponsor for the Premium Targets Lean manufacturing transformation.
* Advance daily management, structured problem solving, kaizen, standard work, process improvement, and cost-reduction practices across sites.
* Partner with Lean resources and site leaders to implement improvements and sustain measurable gains.
* Lead major capital programs, equipment installations, expansions, and facility transitions in partnership with Engineering, corporate, business-unit, and capital teams.
* Ensure capital initiatives meet approved cost, schedule, quality, and performance objectives while integrating safety into design, installation, commissioning, and startup.
* Develop manufacturing and supply chain strategies that support production, maintenance, planning, EHS, technical capability, and customer requirements.
* Partner with Commercial teams to deliver an exceptional customer experience.
* Enable best-practice sharing and process standardization across manufacturing locations.
* Lead financial performance improvement, with a focus on gross margin, inventory turns, and cost management.

**Qualifications**
==================

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, operations, business, or a related field.
* At least 10 years of progressive experience in a manufacturing environment, including significant manufacturing operations people leadership responsibility with a demonstrated ability to develop leaders and build high-performing teams.
* Demonstrated success leading safety and EHS performance, manufacturing operations, continuous improvement, engineering, and capital projects.
* Ability to lead end-to-end processes and deliver results through cross-functional and matrixed teams.
* Ability to travel up to 50%.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master’s degree in engineering, business administration, or a related field.
* Leadership experience in a multi-site or international manufacturing organization.
* Experience leading a Lean transformation or enterprise-wide operating system.
* Experience managing major capital programs, facility expansions, installations, or transitions.

**Leadership Competencies**

* Strategic and systems-oriented thinking, with the ability to translate business priorities into executable operating plans.
* Strong influence, collaboration, and negotiation skills, including the ability to secure alignment and resources across functions.
* Clear, concise written and verbal communication with team members, peers, customers, and senior leaders.
* Sound judgment and the ability to navigate ambiguity, reconcile differing viewpoints, and make timely decisions.
* Visible, values-based leadership grounded in safety, integrity, accountability, disciplined execution, and continuous improvement.
* Demonstrated commitment to coaching, succession planning, and the growth of talent across all levels.

Pay Range:

$148,500.00 - $237,100.00

*Actual base salary offered varies based on factors, including but not limited to, relevant skill, prior experience, education, base salary of internal peers, demonstrated performance, and geographic location.*

**The selection of the person to be hired for this position is contingent on the candidate having export compliance eligibility for access to U.S. controlled technology which comes under the licensing jurisdiction of the U.S. Department of State, International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and the U.S. Department of Commerce, Export Administration Regulations (EAR).**

**The candidate selected will have to qualify as either a U.S. citizen, a U.S. National, a lawful permanent resident of the U.S., a Person Admitted into the U.S. as an Asylee or Refugee., a National of a country that is not prohibited from having access to U.S. controlled technology (via a letter of assurance), or a Person to be approved for an export license by the governing agency whose technology comes under its jurisdiction. Please understand that any job offer that requires approval of an export license will be conditional on Materion’s determination that it will be able to obtain an export license in a time frame consistent with Materion’s business requirements.**

**Materion Corporation and its subsidiaries (the “Company”) is an equal employment opportunity employer. It is the Company’s policy to not unlawfully discriminate against an applicant or employee on the basis of race, color, religion, creed, national origin or ancestry, sex, age, physical or mental disability, veteran or military status, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, or any other legally recognized protected basis under federal, state or local laws, regulations or ordinances. The Company also prohibits harassment of applicants and employees based on any of these protected categories. It is also the Company’s policy to comply with all applicable federal, state and local laws respecting consideration of unemployment status in making hiring decisions. The information collected by this application is solely to determine suitability for employment, verify identity and maintain employment statistics on applicants.**

**Applicants with disabilities may be entitled to reasonable accommodation under the terms of the Americans with Disabilities Act and certain state or local laws. A reasonable accommodation is a change in the way things are normally done which will ensure an equal employment opportunity without imposing undue hardship on the Company. Please inform the Company’s personnel representative if you need assistance completing any forms or to otherwise participate in the application process.**

**Materion’s Veteran Employee Resource group supports veterans and promotes the benefits of hiring veterans in the workplace. We honor all those who have served and are a military friendly company. Veterans are encouraged to apply and military experience and skills are transferrable to Materion careers.**

**Please provide complete information. An incomplete application may affect your consideration for employment.**

role.title: Senior Manager, Industrials & Manufacturing
role.description:
**About dss+**

At dss+, you don’t just deliver projects. You help save lives, improve performance, and build a more sustainable future. We are a purpose-led global consultancy helping organizations solve complex challenges across Operational Risk, Operational Excellence, and Sustainability. With roots in DuPont’s industrial operations, we combine deep industry expertise with practical implementation to deliver measurable, lasting results.

**Why This Role**

As a Senior Manager within our Industrials & Manufacturing team, you will play a key role in delivering transformational results for clients while contributing to the growth of our business. You will build trusted client relationships, identify and develop new business opportunities, support the shaping and closing of consulting engagements, and lead complex projects from the boardroom to the plant floor.

Our work spans industrial manufacturing, consumer goods, pharmaceuticals, and building products, helping clients improve safety, operational performance, productivity, reliability, and profitability.

**What You’ll Experience at dss+**

**Meaningful Impact**

Help leading industrial and manufacturing organizations improve safety, performance, resilience, and sustainability.

**Trusted Expertise**

Work alongside industry experts and senior client leaders to solve complex operational challenges.

**Growth & Leadership**

Take on significant client, project, and business development responsibility while developing teams and helping shape the growth of dss+.

**A Collaborative Culture**

Join a purpose-led, inclusive organization where different perspectives, expertise, and ideas are valued.

**Your Impact**

**Grow the Business**

* Own and deliver against defined annual business development and sales targets.
* Build and maintain strong relationships with senior Operations and EHS leaders.
* Identify new opportunities within existing and prospective client accounts.
* Support the shaping, development, pricing, and closing of consulting engagements.
* Expand client relationships by bringing the full breadth of dss+ capabilities to clients.
* Contribute to industry networks, client events, proposals, and thought leadership.

**What You Bring**

* 10+ years of experience in management consulting and/or manufacturing leadership.
* Senior consulting and/or significant operational, project, or plant leadership experience.
* Proven experience contributing to business development, developing client opportunities, and working toward defined annual sales targets.
* Strong client relationship skills with the ability to build credibility with senior Operations and EHS leaders.
* Demonstrated project and program management experience, including leading complex engagements, managing multiple workstreams, budgets, timelines, resources, risks, and client expectations.
* Experience leading large-scale safety, operational excellence, and performance transformations with measurable results.
* Turnaround, restructuring, and/or M&A integration experience.
* Strong knowledge of Operational Excellence, Lean/Six Sigma, safety management systems, and large-scale change.
* Strong executive presence with credibility in both the boardroom and on the plant floor.
* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Science, or a related field; MBA preferred.
* Willingness to travel **80%+**.

**A Bit More About Us**

dss+ is a global operations management consulting firm helping organizations improve safety, operational performance, and sustainability.

We work from the boardroom to the plant floor, combining deep industry expertise with practical implementation to deliver lasting results.

We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone is respected, valued, and able to contribute and grow.

role.title: Sr. Manager, Fab Quality Engineering
role.description:
**Location:** Alhambra, CA (Onsite)

 

**Our Team**

SPP is a vertically integrated photonics business focused on the design, fabrication, and delivery of Indium Phosphide (InP) semiconductor laser and gain chips. SPP operates two wafer fabrication facilities in Southern California supporting advanced photonic devices and customer die demand.

 

**Job Summary**

The Sr. Manager, Fab Quality Engineering serves as the senior quality leader within SPP Operations and is responsible for building and leading the manufacturing quality organization across both fabrication facilities. The role establishes quality systems, inspection practices, quality metrics, and quality culture while partnering closely with Operations, Engineering, and the Sr. Manager, Photonics Quality Engineering to support business growth and manufacturing excellence.

This position provides leadership for manufacturing quality strategy, execution, and organizational development across both fabrication facilities and is expected to maintain a strong presence on the manufacturing floor. The role supports Epitaxial Growth, Wafer Fabrication, Bar Processing, Chip Processing, and Test Operations, and works closely with Epitaxy, Process, Product, and Equipment Engineering, Manufacturing Operations, Planning, Supply Chain, Test Operations, and Reliability & Failure Analysis.

 

**Key Responsibilities**

* Build and lead the SPP Fab Quality organization across both fabrication facilities
* Recruit, develop, and manage quality inspectors while building future technician and quality engineering capabilities
* Establish quality procedures, metrics, escalation processes, reporting systems, and a culture of quality ownership and continuous improvement.
* Establish incoming inspection processes, acceptance criteria, and material-control procedures for critical materials including III-V substrates, epitaxial source materials, specialty gases, precious metals, process chemicals, and optical and test consumables
* Verify material certifications; establish supplier qualification, monitoring, corrective-action, and containment processes
* Ensure traceability and disposition tracking.
* Develop and implement in-process quality control systems, containment and escalation processes for quality excursions, and process controls across manufacturing operations
* Monitor process performance and quality trends
* Drive reduction of defects, scrap, rework, and quality escapes; and ensure consistent quality practices across both fabs.
* Implement and maintain manufacturing quality systems, including Statistical Process Control (SPC), CAPA, Non-Conforming Material Report (NCMR) processes, FMEA, and process control plans
* Provide independent quality review and approval of Engineering Change Notices (ECNs), process changes, and manufacturing transfers
* Establish and maintain ESD control programs and quality documentation and records.
* Lead investigations of manufacturing quality excursions and process escapes in partnership with Process Engineering and Product Engineering
* Monitor process capability (Cp/Cpk)
* Provide quality leadership for measurement-system capability and MSA activities
* Support tool and process qualification and requalification
* Use quality data to improve process stability, defect reduction, and yield.
* Maintain audit readiness across both fabrication facilities
* Support internal, customer, and ISO audits
* Support contamination-control initiatives and cleanroom environmental monitoring
* Ensure quality documentation meets compliance requirements
* Partner with the Sr. Manager, Photonics Quality Engineering on corporate quality initiatives and enterprise quality alignment.
Other relevant tasks, as assigned. 

 
 

**Minimum Qualifications (Education & Experience)**

* Education: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Physics, Materials Science, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or related technical discipline
* Experience: 7+ years of manufacturing quality experience within wafer fabrication, photonics, compound semiconductor, or related advanced manufacturing environments
* Leadership: 3+ years of people leadership experience
* Strong knowledge of SPC, CAPA, NCMR, FMEA, Control Plans, MSA, and manufacturing quality systems
* Experience leading root-cause investigations and corrective-action programs
* Experience supporting semiconductor wafer fabrication or advanced manufacturing operations
* Strong communication, leadership, and organizational skills
Experience working effectively across Operations and Engineering functions 

 

**Desired Qualifications**

* Experience in wafer-fab quality within silicon semiconductor, compound semiconductor, photonics, III-V semiconductor, optoelectronics, or optical communications manufacturing environments
* Experience supporting epitaxial growth operations
* Experience building or scaling manufacturing quality organizations within multi-site manufacturing environments
* Experience with supplier-quality programs and semiconductor MES systems
* Comfortable operating in evolving, high-mix manufacturing environments with limited historical data
Desire to learn InP epitaxial growth, wafer fabrication, and photonics manufacturing technologies 

 

The intent of this job description is to describe the major duties and responsibilities performed by incumbents of this job. Incumbents may be required to perform job-related tasks other than those specifically included in this description.

 

All duties and responsibilities are essential job functions and requirements and are subject to possible modification to reasonably accommodate individuals with disabilities.

We are proud to be an EEO employer M/F/D/V. We maintain a drug-free workplace.

 

A reasonable estimate of the pay range for this position is $130,000 - $180,000. There are several factors taken into consideration in determining base salary, including but not limited to: job-related qualifications, skills, education and experience, as well as job location and the value of other elements of an employee’s total compensation package.

role.title: Director Quality & Safety
role.description:
**Everything we do is underscored by a why — and that why is one another.**

**Location:**

Altru Hospital,1200 South Columbia Road,Grand Forks, ND 58201

**Summary:**

The Director of Quality and Safety provides strategic leadership for organizational quality, patient safety, regulatory compliance, and performance improvement initiatives. This role partners with physicians, clinical leaders, and operational stakeholders to develop and implement programs that advance patient outcomes, ensure regulatory readiness, mitigate risk, and foster a culture of safety and continuous improvement. The Director oversees quality and safety operations, drives achievement of organizational and financial goals, ensures compliance with applicable regulatory standards, and leads the development of high-performing teams dedicated to delivering exceptional care and operational excellence. Through collaboration, innovation, and data-driven decision making, this position supports Altru's commitment to quality, safety, and outstanding patient experiences.
 
 
A master's degree and experience managing cross-functional teams including guiding clinical and administrative employees preferred

**Essential Job Functions:**

* Develops and implements long-range goals that enhance services and support strong relational management with key stakeholders. Develops collaborative relationships with leadership, physicians, clinical, professional and support staff. Sets standards for operational performance for the division/department(s) and fiscal accountability. Develops and achieves annual financial targets and holds managers and employees accountable to budget targets.
* Oversees the facilitation of regulatory requirements identified internally or from external agencies. Oversees the reporting and submission of regulatory compliance to external agencies as required through contractual relationships.
* Maintains competency in all organizational, department standards relevant to services provided.
* Practices process improvement principles and while managing processes to ensure all regulatory standards are met, and accesses internal resources to assist in adhering to standards as well as ensuring staff understand expectations
* Recruits, develops, retains and leads a talented team of leadership and staff committed to accomplishing the goals of Altru Health System. Builds an environment of shared commitment to organizational goals and fosters an environment conducive to maximizing individual and collective productivity, emphasizing performance and collaboration. Conducts performance reviews, actively recognizes and rewards employees and takes appropriate actions when performance is not meeting expectations. Acts as a mentor and promotes professional growth of employees. Takes responsibility for personal growth and development and meets all system educational requirements.
* Seeks out operational efficiency and involves employees and physicians in workforce redesign, as appropriate to better serve the patient, as well as create a workplace that all employees can function at their highest competency and productivity. Leads and participates in acquisition of new technologies to ensure the highest standard of care.
* Maintains competency in all organizational, department and outside agency standards relevant to services provided and ensures compliance. Manages processes to ensure all regulatory standards are met as well as works to prevent potential legal risk to Altru Health System as appropriate. Accesses internal resources to assist in adhering to standards as well as ensures staff understands expectations.
* Performs other duties as assigned or needed to meet the needs of the department/organization.

### **Certifications**

* Driver's License with Acceptable Driving Record | Driver's License - Current State Licensed | Prior to Start Date | HR Primary Sources

**Education:**

* Required: Bachelors - Business

**Work Experience:**

* Required: A minimum of 7 years Related Experience

**Language Requirements:**

This position requires proficiency in reading, writing, and speaking English to ensure effective communication in the workplace and with patients, families, and team members.

 
 

**Physical Demands :**

* Sit: Frequently (34-66%)

* Stand: Occasionally (5-33%)

* Walk: Frequently (34-66%)

* Stoop/Bend: Rarely (1-4%)

* Reach: Occasionally (5-33%)

* Crawl: Rarely (1-4%)

* Squat/Crouch/Kneel: Rarely (1-4%)

* Twist: Rarely (1-4%)

* Handle/Finger/Feel: Continuously (67-100%)

* See: Continuously (67-100%)

* Hear: Continuously (67-100%)

**Weight Demands:**

* Lift -Floor to Waist Level: Sedentary (<10 pounds)

* Carry: Sedentary (<10 pounds)

* Push/Pull: Sedentary (<10 pounds)

* Slide/Transfer: Not Applicable

**Working Conditions:**

* Indoor: Continuously (67-100%)

* Outdoor: Rarely (1-4%)

* Extreme Temperature: Not Applicable

**Driving Requirement Definitions:**

* **Professional Drivers:** Persons who drive as their main responsibility OR transport passengers or hazardous materials.
* **Frequent Drivers:** Persons whose main responsibility is not driving, but drive daily or almost daily.
* **Occasional Drivers** : Persons who drive from once per month to as frequently as once per week.
* **Infrequent Drivers:** Persons who are generally not expected to drive.

**Driving Requirement for this position:**

Infrequent DriverReference ID: R8492

**Making a real difference. For one another.**

To take the best care of our patients and community — including friends, family, and neighbors — we need people who are committed to growth, excellence, and one another.

At Altru, you’ll find a culture where support and teamwork are at the heart of what we do. You’ll have opportunities to advance your skills, work with the latest technologies, experience the fulfillment that comes from giving back, and take your career wherever you want it to go.

Join our team and be a part of a small community with a big heart.

Altru offers a comprehensive benefits package to its full- and part-time employees. Excellent benefits include a health plan and 401(k) retirement plan. Other benefits include a dental plan, vision plan, life and disability insurance, education assistance, paid time off (PTO)

role.title: Director of Quality Engineering
role.description:
The Director of Quality Engineering – Automation & Performance is the senior technical, delivery, and practice leader for iLAB U.S. Automation and Performance Testing. The role is accountable for the day-to-day management of U.S. engineering initiatives and resources, while also providing hands-on consulting leadership for strategic clients.

This leader defines the practice strategy, architecture, standards, delivery assurance, reusable solutions, and capability roadmap for Automation and Performance Testing. Working as part of a global delivery organization, they combine technical credibility, client leadership, people management, and commercial judgment to deliver measurable quality outcomes, strengthen service offerings, and build scalable engineering capability.

* Own the day-to-day delivery, prioritization, staffing, allocation, utilization, performance, and technical direction of all iLAB U.S. Automation and Performance Testing initiatives and resources.
* Define and evolve Automation and Performance Testing strategies, capability roadmaps, service offerings, architectures, standards, frameworks, methods, tools, reusable accelerators, and intellectual property.
* Oversee technical assurance across high-impact deliveries, including solution architecture, automation and performance engineering design, CI/CD integration, AI-enabled engineering guardrails, test-data readiness, and environment readiness.
* Lead critical client-facing activities, including technical discovery, project kickoffs, solutioning workshops, executive presentations, steering reviews, escalations, and project recovery.
* Serve as the senior technical escalation point for complex or at-risk engagements and personally provide architecture, assessment, technical review, troubleshooting, and recovery leadership until delivery is stabilized.
* Lead the technical development and review of RFIs, RFPs, proposals, SOWs, estimates, staffing models, assumptions, deliverables, risks, acceptance criteria, and service commitments
* Establish and oversee practical engineering governance, including quality gates, code and architecture reviews, documentation standards, source-control practices, repository security, and technical approval processes.
* Define and guide responsible, value-focused uses of AI within Automation and Performance Testing, including test design assistance, script development and maintenance, results analysis, defect insight, and knowledge retrieval, while applying company security, privacy, data-handling, and human-review requirements
* Hire, coach, develop, and retain engineering managers, architects, principal engineers, and technical specialists; establish competency expectations, career paths, succession plans, and backup coverage for critical capabilities.
* Collaborate with global delivery leaders to align technical standards, share reusable assets and expertise, and support other geographies with strategic client and delivery needs.
* Partner with Sales, Professional Services, Operations, Finance, and Talent Management on capacity planning, forecasting, utilization, delivery margin and growth opportunities.
* Represent iLAB as a Quality Engineering thought leader through conferences, industry events, client advisory councils, publications, demonstrations, and market-facing content.

* At least 15 years of progressive experience in Quality Engineering, including senior leadership of complex Automation and Performance Testing solutions, consulting engagements, engineering teams, and CxO-level client relationships
* Deep knowledge of Automation and Performance Testing strategies, architectures, frameworks, tools, workload models, execution practices, analysis, reporting, and integration with modern software delivery pipelines
* Experience leading technical delivery across multiple clients, programs, or business units, including distributed teams and critical project recovery.
* Working knowledge of CI/CD integration, testability, observability, test-data and environment readiness, cloud delivery, and AI-assisted engineering practices.
* Proven people leadership, including resource planning, coaching, performance management, prioritization, utilization, and organizational development.
* Strong consulting and client-advisory skills, with the ability to translate business needs into practical technical solutions and delivery plans.
* Experience shaping proposals, SOWs, estimates, resource models, and commercial commitments.
* Sound understanding of consulting engagement economics, including forecasting, utilization, margin, cost-to-serve, and measurable client outcomes.
* A mature, politically astute leadership style; calm in a crisis, able to lead by influence and example, with excellent written and oral communication.
* Willing and able to travel interstate and occasionally internationally for critical client-facing initiatives, project kickoffs, workshops, presentations, escalations, and recovery efforts.
* Demonstrated experience in a Quality Assurance, Quality Engineering, Automation, or Performance Testing consulting or professional-services organization.
* Experience across the consulting lifecycle and multi-country delivery teams; relevant industry expertise and advanced professional certifications are beneficial.

role.title: Director, Quality Engineering
role.description:
**Become a part of our caring community**
=========================================

Humana is committed to helping people achieve their best health by delivering innovative technology solutions that enable exceptional member and provider experiences. 
The Director, Quality Engineering – Test Data Management (EQE) is a senior technology leader responsible for defining, advancing, and operating Humana's enterprise Test Data Management (TDM) function within Enterprise Quality Engineering. Reporting to the VP, Quality Engineering, this role leads the strategy, operating model, and execution of secure, scalable, compliant, and automation-enabled test data capabilities that support software delivery across Humana's business and technology organizations. 
This leader is accountable for building and leading a high-performing organization responsible for core TDM services, including test data provisioning, synthetic data generation, masking, de-identification, data lifecycle management, and environment data coordination. The Director will partner closely with Quality Engineering, Engineering, Product, Architecture, DevOps, Infrastructure, Security, Privacy, Risk, and Data teams to ensure test data is available, fit for purpose, and aligned to delivery, compliance, and release readiness needs. 
The ideal candidate brings deep expertise in test data management, data engineering, governance, privacy, and automation in a complex enterprise environment. This role will drive modernization of TDM practices through automation-first and AI-enabled capabilities, while establishing standards, controls, and reusable services that improve engineering throughput, reduce delivery friction, and strengthen compliance and data protection across non-production environments.

**Responsibilities**

**Leadership, Strategy & Operating Model**

* Lead the enterprise Test Data Management function within EQE, including strategic direction, operating model execution, and organizational development.
* Build, lead, and develop a high-performing team of managers, engineers, and test data specialists across multiple groups supporting segment and enterprise needs.
* Oversee a distributed organization of **50+ associates** and create clear priorities, role clarity, and performance expectations.
* Partner with Quality Engineering, Engineering, Product, Architecture, DevOps, Infrastructure, Security, and Data teams to align TDM services with business and delivery priorities.
* Drive a scalable support model for segment TDM services across multiple portfolios and delivery teams.
* Promote a culture of quality, compliance, continuous improvement, and shared ownership of secure test data practices.

**Test Data Engineering & Management**

 

* Lead enterprise engineering and management of secure, scalable, and compliant test data solutions.
* Oversee delivery of core TDM capabilities, including:Test data provisioningSynthetic data generationData masking and obfuscationData de-identificationData quality enablementTest data automationData lifecycle managementEnvironment data coordination
* Ensure test data is available, fit for purpose, and aligned to quality engineering, release, and environment needs.
* Advance data engineering practices that improve the reliability, reusability, and speed of test data provisioning across delivery pipelines.
* Support complex testing needs across functional, integration, regression, end-to-end, and non-production validation use cases.

**AI-Enabled & Automation-First TDM**

 

* Drive **AI-enabled** and automation-first TDM strategies to improve speed, intelligence, scalability, and coverage of test data operations.
* Expand the use of AI and advanced automation for synthetic data generation, sensitive data detection, masking rule optimization, provisioning efficiency, and data quality insights.
* Integrate TDM automation into CI/CD and engineering workflows where applicable to reduce manual effort and increase release confidence.
* Partner with enterprise engineering and platform teams to modernize TDM tooling, workflows, and reusable patterns.
* Establish metrics to evaluate automation effectiveness, data readiness, cycle time reduction, and business value realization.

**Governance, Standards, Compliance & Privacy**

 

* Define and enforce enterprise TDM standards, governance, and operating policies.
* Ensure compliance with privacy, security, and regulatory requirements related to test data usage, storage, movement, masking, and de-identification.
* Oversee implementation of compliance and privacy controls for non-production data usage.
* Establish standards for secure handling of production-like data in test environments.
* Partner with security, risk, privacy, and compliance stakeholders to maintain appropriate controls and audit readiness.
* Promote consistent governance for test data access, retention, refresh, lineage, and lifecycle management.

**Delivery Enablement & Stakeholder Partnership**

 

* Enable delivery teams through timely, compliant, and high-quality test data services that improve engineering throughput and release readiness.
* Partner with segment quality engineering leaders and application teams to understand demand patterns and align TDM support to delivery roadmaps.
* Coordinate across environments and shared services to reduce delays related to data setup, refresh, and availability.
* Influence engineering and quality practices that improve testability, environment readiness, and quality outcomes.
* Collaborate with enterprise enablement and platform teams to standardize capabilities and reduce duplication.

**Metrics, Governance & Continuous Improvement**

 

* Define and monitor KPIs related to test data availability, provisioning speed, automation adoption, compliance adherence, data quality, and operational efficiency.
* Use data and insights to identify risks, bottlenecks, and improvement opportunities across TDM services.
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives to reduce manual work, increase data reliability, and improve customer satisfaction.
* Provide clear reporting and operational transparency to senior leadership and stakeholders.
* Build maturity roadmaps for enterprise TDM capabilities and measure progress against defined outcomes.

**Use your skills to make an impact**
=====================================

**Required Qualifications**

 

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or any technology related degree or equivalent experience.
* **10+ years** of experience in quality engineering, test data management, data engineering, software engineering, or related technical disciplines.
* **5+ years** of leadership experience managing enterprise-scale technology teams, including managers and geographically distributed associates.
* Experience leading or scaling **test data management**, data engineering, or quality engineering functions in a large enterprise environment.
* Demonstrated success building and operating secure, scalable, and compliant test data solutions.
* Experience with key TDM capabilities such as data provisioning, masking, obfuscation, de-identification, synthetic data generation, and lifecycle management.
* Strong understanding of privacy, security, and compliance considerations for test data in regulated environments.
* Experience driving automation and process modernization across engineering or quality workflows.
* Strong stakeholder management and executive communication skills, with the ability to influence across engineering, quality, data, and business organizations.
* Experience working in Agile and DevOps environments and supporting modern software delivery practices.

**Preferred Qualifications**

 

* Experience in healthcare, payer/insurance, or another highly regulated industry.
* Experience supporting enterprise quality engineering or platform enablement organizations.
* Familiarity with test data management platforms, masking tools, synthetic data solutions, and data quality tooling.
* Knowledge of cloud platforms, distributed systems, APIs, CI/CD pipelines, and enterprise engineering platforms.
* Experience applying AI or machine learning capabilities to test data, quality engineering, or operational optimization.
* Familiarity with data governance, data retention, and environment management practices in large-scale enterprises.

**Success in this Role**

In this role, success will be measured by:

* Improved speed, reliability, and scalability of enterprise test data provisioning and support.
* Increased adoption of secure, compliant, and reusable TDM solutions across segments and teams.
* Reduced delivery delays caused by test data availability, quality, or environment coordination issues.
* Strong compliance with privacy, security, masking, and de-identification requirements.
* Measurable advancement in AI-enabled and automation-first TDM capabilities.
* Improved stakeholder satisfaction across Quality Engineering, Engineering, Product, and Delivery teams.
* Strong associate engagement, capability growth, and retention across the TDM organization.

In certain roles, the minimum recommended internet speed required by Humana may not be sufficient for business needs. Humana reserves the right to require associates to upgrade their internet service if necessary. Work from a dedicated space lacking ongoing interruptions to protect member PHI / HIPAA information. 
Travel: While this is a remote position, occasional travel to Humana's offices for training or meetings may be required.

The compensation range below reflects a good faith estimate of starting base pay for full time (40 hours per week) employment at the time of posting. $156,600 - $215,400 per year 
This job is eligible for a bonus incentive plan. This incentive opportunity is based upon company and/or individual performance.

**Description of Benefits**

Humana, Inc. and its affiliated subsidiaries (collectively, “Humana”) offers competitive benefits that support whole-person well-being. Associate benefits are designed to encourage personal wellness and smart healthcare decisions for you and your family while also knowing your life extends outside of work. Among our benefits, Humana provides medical, dental and vision benefits, 401(k) retirement savings plan, time off (including paid time off, company and personal holidays, paid parental and caregiver leave), short-term and long-term disability, life insurance and many other opportunities.

**About us**
============

About Humana: Humana Inc. (NYSE: HUM) is a leading U.S. healthcare company. Through our Humana insurance services and our CenterWell healthcare services, we make it easier for the millions of people we serve to achieve their best health – delivering the care and service they need, when they need it. These efforts are leading to a better quality of life for people with Medicare and Medicaid, families, individuals, military service personnel, and communities at large. Learn more about what we offer at Humana.com and at CenterWell.com.

**Equal Opportunity Employer**

It is the policy of Humana not to discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment because of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, marital status, genetic information, disability or protected veteran status. It is also the policy of Humana to take affirmative action, in compliance with Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act and VEVRAA, to employ and to advance in employment individuals with disability or protected veteran status, and to base all employment decisions only on valid job requirements. This policy shall apply to all employment actions, including but not limited to recruitment, hiring, upgrading, promotion, transfer, demotion, layoff, recall, termination, rates of pay or other forms of compensation and selection for training, including apprenticeship, at all levels of employment.

role.title: Director-Government and External Quality Programs
role.description:
**Job Description:**

The Director of Government and External Quality Programs sets the enterprise vision and strategy for government quality and public reporting programs. This role anticipates regulatory and policy changes, represents Intermountain externally, establishes standards and governance, and mobilizes organizational partners to improve quality performance, manage risk, and optimize financial outcomes. The Leader also builds and develops a sustainable center of expertise responsible for accurate, timely, and defensible reporting.

**Essential Functions**

* Sets the enterprise vision and strategy for government quality and public reporting programs. Anticipates the future environment, establishes strategic priorities, and aligns the portfolio with Intermountain’s clinical, financial, and operational goals.
* Shapes Intermountain’s response to evolving policy and regulation. Interprets emerging government priorities, evaluates enterprise impact, and advises senior leaders on strategic decisions, risks, opportunities, and organizational readiness.
* Develops Intermountain’s positions and represents the organization externally. Builds enterprise alignment and serves as a senior representative in government, industry, advisory, and measure-development forums to influence practical and meaningful quality programs.
* Builds strategic partnerships that expand Intermountain’s influence. Cultivates senior-level relationships with government agencies, associations, health systems, health plans, and national quality leaders to anticipate change, shape strategy, and advance shared priorities.
* Establishes enterprise standards for quality measurement and reporting. Provides strategic oversight of measure interpretation, data integrity, abstraction, submission, and public reporting to ensure results are consistent, timely, and defensible.
* Drives enterprise quality performance and financial value. Mobilizes clinical, operational, financial, and technical leaders around priority opportunities and ensures government quality programs translate into measurable improvement and optimized organizational outcomes.
* Establishes governance and executive accountability for program risk. Ensures senior leaders have visibility into performance, financial exposure, readiness, and emerging concerns. Directs the organizational response to significant reporting issues, disputes, and adverse determinations.
* Builds and leads an enterprise center of expertise. Provides strategic direction to government quality reporting teams, develops leaders and subject matter experts, and ensures the organization has the talent, technology, partnerships, and resources needed for long-term success.
 

**Skills**

* Strategic Leadership
* Strategic Planning
* Regulatory Interpretation
* Policy Analysis
* External Relations and Advocacy
* Executive Influence and Communication
* Quality Measurement and Reporting
* Performance Improvement
* Risk Management
* Financial Acumen
* Relationship Building
* Communication

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in healthcare administration, public health, nursing, health information management, health policy, business, data analytics, or a related field. Degree must be obtained through an accredited institution. Education is verified.
* Seven years of progressive experience in healthcare quality, regulatory reporting, government healthcare programs, public reporting, value-based care, health policy, or a related field.
* Three years of leadership experience, including responsibility for people, complex programs, or enterprise-wide initiatives.
* Experience interpreting federal or state healthcare regulations, quality program requirements, payment models, measure specifications, or public reporting methodologies.
* Experience developing strategy and leading implementation across multiple departments, facilities, markets, or operational areas.
* Experience advising senior leaders and communicating complex regulatory, clinical, financial, and technical information to varied audiences.
* Experience influencing decisions and achieving results across organizational boundaries without direct authority.
* Experience using quality, operational, and financial information to identify risk, prioritize opportunities, and guide improvement.
 

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master’s degree in public health, healthcare administration, health policy, business administration, nursing, health informatics, or a related field.
* Experience with CMS hospital quality and payment programs, Medicaid quality programs, state-mandated reporting, or national public reporting and recognition programs.
* Experience representing a healthcare organization on government, industry, advisory, association, or measure-development committees.
* Experience developing organizational positions or formal responses related to proposed regulations, measures, benchmarks, payment methodologies, or public-reporting requirements.
* Experience establishing enterprise governance, regulatory readiness, program controls, risk-management processes, or corrective-action structures.
* Experience leading teams responsible for clinical data abstraction, measure interpretation, validation, regulatory submission, or public reporting.
* Experience building strategic partnerships with government agencies, health plans, associations, peer health systems, or national quality organizations.
* Experience leading a center of expertise, developing leaders and subject matter experts, and establishing succession and cross-training strategies.
 

**Physical Requirements**

* Ongoing need for employee to see and read information, documents, monitors, identify equipment and supplies, and be able to assess customer needs.
* Frequent interactions with providers, colleagues, customers, patients/clients, and visitors that require employee to verbally communicate as well as hear and understand spoken information, needs, and issues quickly and accurately.

Manual dexterity of hands and fingers to manipulate complex and delicate equipment with precision and accuracy. This includes frequent computer use for typing, accessing needed information, etc.

**Location:**

Intermountain Health Intermountain Medical Center

**Work City:**

Murray

**Work State:**

Utah

**Scheduled Weekly Hours:**

40

The hourly range for this position is listed below. Actual hourly rate dependent upon experience.

$68.42 - $105.62 
 

We care about your well-being – mind, body, and spirit – which is why we provide our caregivers a generous benefits package that covers a wide range of programs to foster a sustainable culture of wellness that encompasses living healthy, happy, secure, connected, and engaged.

 
 

By applying for a position with Intermountain, I acknowledge that I will comply with all applicable Intermountain policies and expectations. If applying for a remote or hybrid role, this includes remote work expectations related to confidentiality, information security, work schedules, conflicts of interest, and use of company equipment. I further acknowledge that outside employment or activities may not interfere with job responsibilities or create a conflict of interest with Intermountain. Actual or reasonably perceived conflicts may be grounds for disqualification from consideration or, if hired, corrective action up to and including termination of employment.

 
 

Intermountain Health is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status.

 
 

At Intermountain Health, we use the artificial intelligence ("AI") platform, HiredScore to improve your job application experience. HiredScore helps match your skills and experiences to the best jobs for you. While HiredScore assists in reviewing applications, all final decisions are made by Intermountain personnel to ensure fairness. We protect your privacy and follow strict data protection rules. Your information is safe and used only for recruitment. Thank you for considering a career with us and experiencing our AI-enhanced recruitment process.

 
 

All positions subject to close without notice.
