role.description:
**POSITION SUMMARY**

Responsible for the overall strategic direction and leadership of assigned departments including administrative, financial, compliance, quality improvement, technical, and personnel activities in accordance with established policies and standards.

 
 

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Provides oversight in the development and implementation of quality improvement and organizational excellence plans, related to quality functions.
* Directs and coordinates the department's activities, and staff to ensure they are efficient, timely, and meet cost and quality objectives; and that all activities and services are carried out in compliance with local, state, federal, and governmental regulations, and laws.
* Directs and leads process improvement projects and teams that achieve measurable, sustainable change, promoting service, process, and operational excellence.
* Develops strong relationships with internal colleagues, external providers, and the medical community to provide high quality, responsive services.
* Develops and trains personnel within the department and reviews and appraises their performance. Responsible for assuring competency of all staff.
* Develops annual budget for areas of responsibility and works with department leaders and staff to implement the budget. Assures measures for staying within budgetary parameters.
* Develops and implements business plans, evaluates existing programs using established productivity standards and metrics. Continuously improves operations to manage costs, improve efficiencies, quality, and service.
* Acts as a resource and provides ongoing education for department staff and the organization regarding national and regional trends; adjusts quality improvement model to meet financial, regulatory, and clinical goals for the hospital in collaboration with the Executives.
* Maintains professional and technical knowledge by attending educational workshops; reviewing professional publications; establishing personal networks; participating in professional societies.
* Performs other related duties as required and directed.

**QUALIFICATIONS REQUIRED**

* Bachelor’s degree in nursing, healthcare administration, business administration, engineering, or related field from an accredited educational institution.
* Five years of progressively responsible quality management in healthcare related experience that demonstrates a high level of understanding of the required knowledge, skills, and abilities and frequent involvement with senior management and physicians.
* Two years of Regulatory and Accreditation experience such as CMS, Joint Commission, Healthcare Facilities Accreditation Programs, DNV.

 

**QUALIFICATIONS PREFERRED**

* Master's degree in nursing, healthcare administration, business administration, engineering, or related field from an accredited educational institution.
* LEAN/Six Sigma Certification.
* Certification in Quality Improvement/ Patient Safety are of focus (i.e., CPHQ, ASQ, CQIA, Team STEPPS Master Trainer, Project Management)

Additional Information

* Schedule: Full-time
* Requisition ID: 26012493
* Daily Work Times: 8:00AM - 4:30PM
* Hours Per Pay Period: 80
* On Call: No
* Weekends: No

 

#### **About Us**

The McLaren system includes 12 hospitals across the state, ambulatory surgery centers, imaging centers, a 730-member employed primary and specialty care physician network, commercial and Medicaid HMOs covering more than 242,000 Michigan lives, home health, infusion and hospice providers, pharmacy services, a clinical laboratory network, and a wholly owned medical malpractice insurance company. McLaren operates Michigan’s largest network of cancer centers and providers, anchored by the Karmanos Cancer Institute, a National Cancer Institute-designated comprehensive cancer center. McLaren has 20,000 full-, part-time and contracted employees and more than 93,000 network providers throughout Michigan.

role.title: (USA) Director, Quality Assurance Continuous Improvement
role.description:
**Position Summary...**
-----------------------

We’re looking for a Director of Continuous Improvement to lead the monitoring, assurance, risk intelligence, control effectiveness, remediation, and transformation capabilities for Last Mile Delivery (LMD) Risk Operations. This role is responsible for helping the organization identify areas for improvement, why it is needed, whether risks and controls are effectively managed, and whether corrective actions actually solve the underlying problem. This leader will evolve traditional quality assurance into a broader, closed-loop assurance model that identifies systemic issues, determines root causes, drives accountable remediation, and validates effectiveness. The role will also lead the transformation of Risk Operations through process redesign, operational resilience, data-driven risk intelligence, automation, and AI—rethinking how work should operate rather than simply making existing manual processes faster. The continuous improvement org will have both tactical and strategic components to ensure end-to-end program evolution and growth.

**What you'll do...**
---------------------

* **Lead the Monitoring & Assurance strategy** by evolving traditional transaction-level QA into a risk-based assurance capability that identifies recurring defects, systemic weaknesses, performance gaps, and emerging operational issues across Risk Operations.
* **Establish root cause and action management disciplines** that connect findings to underlying causes, accountable owners, remediation plans, target dates, escalation paths, and effectiveness validation—ensuring issues remain visible through sustainable closure.
* **Build the Risk Intelligence capability** by leveraging operational data, incidents, assurance findings, and other risk signals to identify patterns, trends, concentrations, benchmarks, and emerging risks and translate them into proactive recommendations for leadership.
* **Lead risk assessment and control effectiveness activities** to identify key operational risks, assess whether controls are appropriately designed and operating effectively, identify control gaps, and ensure deficiencies are addressed through accountable remediation.
* **Drive process improvement and operational transformation** by applying a TPM/engineering mindset to simplify, redesign, and standardize Risk Operations workflows, reducing unnecessary complexity, manual handoffs, failure points, and unclear ownership.
* **Strengthen operational resilience** by identifying critical processes, dependencies, single points of failure, technology and data vulnerabilities, and contingency needs to ensure critical Risk Operations capabilities can continue through disruption.
* **Lead AI transformation and automation strategy for Risk Operations** identifying opportunities to eliminate repetitive work while also reimagining how AI can reshape intake, investigations, monitoring, analysis, decision support, and reporting—not simply accelerate existing manual processes.
* **Establish reporting, dashboards, and management insights** that provide leadership with a consolidated view of operational health, emerging risks, control effectiveness, recurring issues, remediation status, and transformation progress. 
 
 At Walmart, we offer competitive pay as well as performance-based bonus awards and other great benefits for a happier mind, body, and wallet. Health benefits include medical, vision and dental coverage. Financial benefits include 401(k), stock purchase and company-paid life insurance. Paid time off benefits include PTO (including sick leave), parental leave, family care leave, bereavement, jury duty, and voting. Other benefits include short-term and long-term disability, company discounts, Military Leave Pay, adoption and surrogacy expense reimbursement, and more. You will also receive PTO and/or PPTO that can be used for vacation, sick leave, holidays, or other purposes. The amount you receive depends on your job classification and length of employment. It will meet or exceed the requirements of paid sick leave laws, where applicable. For information about PTO, see https://one.walmart.com/notices. Live Better U is a Walmart-paid education benefit program for full-time and part-time associates in Walmart and Sam's Club facilities. Programs range from high school completion to bachelor's degrees, including English Language Learning and short-form certificates. Tuition, books, and fees are completely paid for by Walmart.

 For information about benefits and eligibility, see One.Walmart.

role.title: Plant Manager
role.description:
As a Plant Manager here at Honeywell, you will be responsible for overseeing the operations and performance of our manufacturing plant. You will develop and implement strategies to optimize plant operations, improve productivity, and reduce costs. Ensuring compliance with safety regulations and promoting a culture of safety throughout the plant will be a key responsibility.

You will report directly to our VP ISC Americas & Pacific and you’ll work out of our Tempe, Arizona location on an On-site work schedule.

In this role, you will impact the success of our business by leading and managing a team to meet production targets and deliver on customer commitments. You will play a critical role in ensuring the efficient production of high-quality products while maintaining a safe and productive work environment. Your leadership and strategic decision-making skills will be essential in driving operational excellence and achieving business objectives.

 

**YOU MUST HAVE**

* Minimum of 6 years of experience in plant management or a similar leadership role.
* Strong knowledge of manufacturing processes and best practices.
* Proven track record of driving operational excellence and achieving business objectives.
* Minimum of 6 years of experience in managing plant budgets and resources effectively to meet financial goals.
* Ability to lead continuous improvement initiatives and implement best practices in a manufacturing environment.
* Minimum of 6 years of experience in Electronic assembly process experience.

**WE VALUE**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations Management, or a related field.
* Experience with Lean Six Sigma certification and continuous improvement methodologies.
* Strong financial acumen and ability to manage budgets effectively.
* Experience in developing and leading diverse teams to achieve operational goals.
Excellent problem-solving skills and strategic decision-making abilities. 

Due to compliance with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidate must be a U.S. person, which is defined as, a U.S. citizen, a U.S. permanent resident, or have protected status in the U.S. under asylum or refugee status.

**ABOUT HONEYWELL TECHNOLOGIES**

Honeywell Technologies is a global, pure-play automation company with a legacy of innovating to help solve the world’s most mission-critical challenges, enhancing the quality of life for people and communities around the world. We serve the building, industrial, and process sectors with a broad portfolio of services, solutions, and products, underpinned by our Honeywell Technologies Accelerator operating system and Honeywell Technologies Forge intelligence layer. By combining the deep domain expertise of our more than 50,000 employees with decades of data from our global installed base, we are uniquely positioned to lead the industrial sector’s transition from automation to autonomy. Learn more

**THE BUSINESS UNIT**

Honeywell Building Automation (BA) is a leading global provider of products, software, solutions, and technologies that enable building owners and occupants to ensure their facilities are safe, energy efficient, sustainable, and productive. BA products and services include advanced software applications for building control and optimization; sensors, switches, control systems, and instruments for energy management; access control; video surveillance; fire products; and installation, maintenance, and upgrades of systems. Revenues in 2022 for BA were $6B and there are approximately 18,000 employees globally. To learn more, please visit https://buildings.honeywell.com/

**BENEFITS OF WORKING FOR HONEYWELL**

In addition to a competitive salary, leading-edge work, and developing solutions side-by-side with dedicated experts in their fields, Honeywell employees are eligible for a comprehensive benefits package. This package includes employer subsidized Medical, Dental, Vision, and Life Insurance; Short-Term and Long-Term Disability; 401(k) match, Flexible Spending Accounts, Health Savings Accounts, EAP, and Educational Assistance; Parental Leave, Paid Time Off (for vacation, personal business, sick time, and parental leave), and 12 Paid Holidays. Learn more

The application period for the job is estimated to be 40 days from the job posting date; however, this may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates. Posting Date: 11/10/2026.

*Honeywell is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will be considered without regard to age, race, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, marital status, affectional or sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, disability, nationality, sex, religion, or veteran status.* Learn more

* Lead and manage the plant operations to meet production targets and deliver on customer commitments.
* Develop and implement strategies to optimize plant operations, improve productivity, and reduce costs.
* Ensure compliance with safety regulations and promote a culture of safety throughout the plant.
* Collaborate with cross-functional teams to drive continuous improvement initiatives and implement best practices.
* Monitor key performance indicators and implement corrective actions to address any deviations from targets.

role.title: Director of Operations
role.description:
**Director of Operations**

**Arden's Garden | Atlanta, Georgia | Full-time, On-site**

**About Arden's Garden**

Since 1995, Arden's Garden has been on a mission to bring good health to all. Today, we operate 19 retail locations, manufacture our own products, and distribute through thousands of grocery stores, including Publix, Kroger, Whole Foods, and Sprouts.

We're a growing, entrepreneurial company looking for an exceptional leader to help take us to the next level.

**The Opportunity**

We're seeking a strategic, results-driven Director of Operations to lead our retail and manufacturing operations. You'll lead and develop our experienced operational leadership team, strengthen accountability, improve profitability, and build the systems that support our growth.

A major part of this role is leading our push to bring AI and modern tools into every part of the business. We're looking for someone who sees how technology can take us to the next level and makes it happen.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead our effort to bring AI, automation, and data into the business, in areas like demand forecasting, labor scheduling, inventory and ordering, production planning, and real-time reporting.
* Lead, coach and develop our retail and manufacturing leadership teams.
* Drive operational excellence, efficiency and profitability across the business.
* Establish clear goals, performance expectations and accountability.
* Identify challenges, develop solutions and ensure successful execution.
* Improve processes, systems and communication across departments.
* Manage operational budgets, performance metrics and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Partner closely with the COO and senior leadership to execute company strategy and support growth.

**In Your First Year, You'll**

* Identify our highest-value opportunities for AI and launch at least three tools, such as forecasting, scheduling, or automated reporting, that measurably save time, cut costs, or improve decisions.
* Help our teams adopt and use these tools day-to-day.
* Strengthen financial accountability and improve profitability across retail and manufacturing.
* Reduce waste and bring labor costs in line with targets.
* Develop your leaders and prepare them for bigger roles.

**Growth Opportunity**

This is a high-impact position with significant autonomy and the chance to make a meaningful difference in a growing company. The Director of Operations reports to the COO and works closely with our senior leadership team. For the right person, there is tremendous potential to advance into a senior executive leadership role.

**Compensation & Benefits**

Competitive compensation, performance-based bonus and benefits.

**We're looking for someone who sees what needs to be done, figures out how to do it, and makes** **it happen, while inspiring others to do the same!**

**What We're Looking For**

* 6+ years of operations leadership, including 3+ years leading managers.
* Proven success leading complex operations and delivering measurable results.
* A track record of implementing technology and AI tools, assisting teams with adoption, and transforming how the business runs.
* A self-motivated, resourceful problem solver who thinks independently, takes ownership, and consistently follows through.
* Strong strategic thinking combined with a hands-on, solutions-oriented approach.
* Demonstrated success developing leaders, delegating effectively, and building accountable teams.
* Strong financial acumen and experience building and improving systems and processes.
* Outstanding communication skills and the ability to build relationships across the organization.
* Experience in multi-unit retail or manufacturing is highly valued; food and beverage experience is strongly preferred.
* A genuine connection to our mission of good health for all.

role.description:
At Dexter, we manufacture and distribute axles, accessories, and towing components primarily serving the commercial trailer, RV, marine, agriculture, and manufactured housing markets. We’re building products and systems that are rooted in a culture of safety, collaboration, and innovation.

Headquartered in Elkhart, Indiana, Dexter has manufacturing and distribution locations throughout the U.S. and Canada. Employing state-of-the-art robotics, precision welding equipment, and automated machining processes, Dexter has achieved over 65 years of success through a commitment to the principles of superior quality, continuous improvement, and unparalleled customer service.

For more information about our company, access Dexter's web site at www.dextergroup.com .

The Plant Manager is the overall leader of the site and business operations. In this role, the Plant Manager directs operations in accordance with the company’s operational imperatives, principles, policies, and procedures as well as:

* Continuously promotes and grows a culture of Safety.
* Drives commitment to quality throughout the operation, assuring excellence in customer service.
* Promotes an environment of trust, employee involvement, and engagement.
* Provides direction, leadership, and development to managers and supervisors.
* Develops annual budget, monthly forecasts, and gap analysis of financial performance.
* Budgets and manages capital expenditures.
* Champions continuous improvement.
* Develops plans for efficient use of materials, machines, and employees.
* Reviews production costs and product quality.
* Modifies production and inventory control programs to maintain and enhance the operation.
* Implements programs to assure the operation maintains compliance with local, state, and federal regulations in all areas.

**Overview:**

* Lead and drive the success of the health, safety, quality, and financial performance of the plant.
* Model operational rigor through daily/weekly/monthly rhythms to provide direction of clear goals and objectives for production areas.
* Responsible for ensuring all direct and indirect employees understand their personal role in achieving company standards.
* Demonstrate and maintain the standard of impeccable integrity
* Foster plant Safety, Quality and Production successes along with continuous improvement to create new ways in which to operate the business better.
* Foster and develop an environment of Zero Accidents.
* Achieve and maintain On Time Delivery of 98% or better.
* Partner with Corporate support resources to develop processes that improve the overall working environment, enhance Safety, and drive productivity for the shop operations.
* Build and nurture a culture in which challenges and opportunities exist for all employees based on individual capabilities and initiative.

**Qualifications:**

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, or related discipline and 10 years’ experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

English, Spanish as second language preferred

Minimal traveling (10%) may be required at frequency of 2x a yr. by air with proximities of 250-1000 miles.

**Dexter cares for our people. Here are some of our great, comprehensive Benefits:**

* Dexter offers a competitive wage
* Full benefits package including Health, Dental, Vision, Life, STD, LTD, FSA, HSA
* 3% profit sharing in our Safe Harbor program
* 401(k) Plan with company contributions
* Paid Holidays and paid time off
* Opportunities for internal career development and growth

**Apply now to join an industry leader and make a difference in what we do for the customers we serve!**

role.description:
**Plant Manager**
=================

Ft.Wayne, IN, US, 46808-1998

Requisition: 68658

**Dana is a global leader in the supply of highly engineered driveline, sealing, and thermal-management technologies that improve the efficiency and performance of vehicles with both conventional and alternative-energy powertrains. Serving two primary markets – passenger vehicle and commercial truck equipment – Dana provides the world's original-equipment manufacturers and the aftermarket with local product and service support through a network of nearly 100 engineering, manufacturing, and distribution facilities.**

**Job Purpose**
---------------

The Plant Manager (PM) must effectively organize, lead & manage all functional elements of the facility. The PM must embrace corporate & business unit initiatives including lean manufacturing & implementation of the Dana Operating System (based on the Toyota Production System (TPS)). The PM will maintain a workforce for highly motivated employees with a morale that is conducive with performance being measured at or above minimum acceptable levels, drive performance to achieve or exceed financial plans & strategic goals. The PM operates within the overall framework of Dana strategies, set objectives, & procedures.

**Job Duties and Responsibilities**
-----------------------------------

* Full plant P&L responsibility including strategy, policies, processes, practices, systems.
* Provide leadership & management of people, processes, & products including, but not limited to:
 
 - Manufacturing &/or assembly operations
 
 - Sales; finance (operating budget, cost controls, capital management, AP/AR etc.)
 
 - Supply chain management (procurement/distribution)
 
 - Inventory management
 
 - Environmental/occupational health & safety
 
 - Employee selection & development
 
 - Labor relations
 
 - Continuous improvement (cost, quality, productivity, operational excellence)
 
 - Metrics & reporting
 
 - Program management
 
 - Product launches
 
 - Facilities & equipment, & engineering
* Communicate successfully at all levels within the organization as well as externally with customers, suppliers & the community.
* Establish credibility (through Lean knowledge, business acumen, & plant-specific knowledge) with business unit & other executive leadership to influence basic strategy & effective inclusion of long-range improvements to business unit plans.

**Education and Qualifications**
--------------------------------

* *Bachelor’s degree or 4+ years of applicable experience*
* *12+ years of experience*

**Skills**
----------

* Ability to set and execute long-term operational strategies that align with business goals, including production efficiency, cost control, and quality improvement.
* Deep understanding of manufacturing systems, lean principles, and continuous improvement methodologies to drive performance across all plant functions.
* Strong grasp of budgeting, cost analysis, and financial metrics to manage plant profitability and resource allocation effectively.
* Proven ability to lead, motivate, and develop diverse teams, fostering a culture of accountability, safety, and engagement.
* Excellent communication skills to coordinate with departments such as engineering, quality, supply chain, and corporate leadership, ensuring alignment and transparency.
* Experience working in an unionized work environment.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and do not discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment because of race, color, sex, age, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, status as a veteran, and basis of disability or any other federal, state or local protected class.

Unsolicited Resumes from Third-Party Recruiters

Please note that as per Dana policy, we do not accept unsolicited resumes from third-party recruiters unless such recruiters were engaged to provide candidates for a specified opening. role.title: Director DTC Operations
role.description:
Description:

**Job Summary**

The Director of DTC Operations provides strategic leadership for the direct-to-consumer business, with primary responsibility for Charles Krug Winery. This role oversees all DTC revenue channels, including the tasting room, wine club, eCommerce, tele-sales, events, and hospitality experiences. The successful candidate will balance strategic thinking with hands-on leadership, maintaining a strong focus on financial performance, customer relationships, employee development, and the long-term success of Charles Krug's direct-to-consumer business.

The Director is accountable for driving revenue growth, profitability, customer acquisition and retention, visitation, and guest satisfaction while ensuring operational excellence and alignment with company objectives. Working closely with Marketing, Finance, Operations, and Executive Leadership, this position develops and executes strategies that strengthen customer relationships and support the long-term success of the DTC business.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

**Strategic Leadership & Revenue Growth**

* Develop and execute DTC strategies to achieve revenue, profitability, visitation, and customer growth objectives.
* Establish annual business plans, budgets, forecasts, sales goals, and performance metrics.
* Identify opportunities to increase customer acquisition, retention, average order value, and lifetime value.
* Monitor market trends and consumer behavior to adapt business strategies and identify new growth opportunities.
* Collaborate with executive leadership on long-term planning and business development initiatives.

**Hospitality, Sales & Customer Development**

* Provide leadership for tasting room, wine club, eCommerce, tele-sales, events, and hospitality operations.
* Drive winery visitation through strategic partnerships, tourism relationships, marketing initiatives, and customer acquisition programs.
* Oversee wine club growth, member retention, customer engagement, and loyalty programs.
* Partner with Marketing to execute customer communication, promotional, and digital sales initiatives.
* Ensure exceptional guest experiences that strengthen brand loyalty and drive sales conversion.

**Financial & Operational Management**

* Maintain accountability for DTC financial performance, including revenue, profitability, labor, operating expenses, and budgets.
* Analyze business results and key performance indicators to identify opportunities for improvement.
* Oversee DTC operational processes, inventory coordination, order fulfillment, and customer service standards.
* Evaluate systems, technology, and processes to improve efficiency, customer experience, and business performance.
* Ensure compliance with company policies and applicable alcohol beverage regulations.

**Team Leadership**

* Lead, coach, and develop DTC managers and team members.
* Establish clear performance expectations, accountability measures, and development plans.
* Oversee staffing, scheduling, workforce planning, and labor management.
* Promote a culture of accountability, collaboration, hospitality, and continuous improvement.
* Foster cross-functional partnerships to achieve business objectives.

**Required Critical Skills**

* Strategic business planning and execution
* Revenue growth, sales leadership, and customer development
* Financial management, budgeting, forecasting, and P&L accountability
* Hospitality and customer experience leadership
* Data analysis and performance management
* Team leadership, coaching, and talent development
* Business development and partnership management
* Strong communication and cross-functional collaboration
* Problem-solving, innovation, and adaptability
* Operational planning and execution

Requirements:

* Bachelor’s degree in business, hospitality, marketing, or related field preferred; equivalent experience considered.
* 7+ or more years of progressive leadership experience in DTC sales, hospitality, retail, or consumer-facing operations, preferably within the wine industry.
* Proven success managing multiple revenue channels and delivering financial results.
* Experience with tasting room, wine club, eCommerce, hospitality, and event operations.
* Strong background in budgeting, forecasting, operational planning, and business analysis.
* Experience developing customer acquisition, retention, and revenue growth strategies.
* Familiarity with DTC technology platforms such as Commerce7, Tock, Mailchimp, and related reporting tools.
* Strong leadership, analytical, communication, and problem-solving skills.
* Ability to work onsite and maintain flexibility for evenings, weekends, and special events.

role.title: Manufacturing Engineering Director
role.description:
RELOCATION ASSISTANCE: Relocation assistance may be available 
 
CLEARANCE REQUIRED FOR START: No 
 
CLEARANCE TYPE: Secret 
 
TRAVEL: Yes, 10% of the Time Description 
 
At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history. 
 
 
 The Director, Manufacturing Engineering provides functional and strategic leadership for the manufacturing engineering organization, accountable for process capability, producibility, and product quality across production programs. This role leads a team of managers and engineers responsible for developing, deploying, and continuously improving manufacturing, test, and related industrial engineering processes to meet safety, quality, delivery, cost, and people objectives in Baltimore, MD .

 Key Responsibilities
 Functional & People Leadership Lead and develop a high‑performing manufacturing engineering organization, including managers, engineers, and supporting staff.
 Define and maintain functional standards, methods, tools, and best practices for manufacturing engineering across the site or business.
 Recruit, develop, and retain talent; drive succession planning, leadership development, and engagement/inclusion activities.
 Provide regular coaching, performance feedback, and career development for managers and engineers.
 
 
 Manufacturing Engineering Ownership Own manufacturing engineering processes from new product introduction through sustainment, ensuring robust process controls, standard work, and documented work instructions.
 Direct the creation and maintenance of MBOMs, routings, work instructions, tooling, and strategies that enable safe, efficient, and high‑quality production.
 Drive producibility into designs by partnering with Design Engineering early in the lifecycle; ensure effective transition to production and rate readiness.
 Establish and manage key performance indicators (yields, scrap, rework, cycle time, labor efficiency) and drive continuous improvement using data‑driven methods.
 
 
 Operations, Quality, and Continuous Improvement Partner closely with Operations, Quality & Mission Excellence, and Supply Chain to ensure stable processes and timely resolution of production issues.
 Oversee manufacturing engineering participation in MRB and nonconformance disposition; ensure effective root‑cause analysis and corrective/preventive actions.
 Champion initiatives to improve safety, quality, delivery, and cost.
 Lead manufacturing engineering support to factory readiness, capacity planning, and rate ramp‑ups.
 
 
 Program, Financial, and Strategic Management Align functional objectives, resources, and priorities with program and business needs; balance near‑term execution with long‑term capability development.
 Partner with Program Management and Business Management to support bids, proposals, and program execution, including manufacturing scope, risk, and cost/schedule inputs.
 Own manufacturing engineering budgets (labor, capital, and expense) and apply sound financial management.
 Develop and execute technology roadmaps and capital investment plans for manufacturing processes, equipment, and facilities.
 
 
 Compliance, Governance, and Stakeholder Management Ensure manufacturing engineering processes comply with regulatory requirements, customer standards, and internal procedures.
 Represent manufacturing engineering in internal and external reviews, audits, and customer engagements.
 Build strong relationships with sector/site leadership, program teams, and functional peers to drive alignment and resolve cross‑functional constraints.
 
 
 Basic Qualifications 
 Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related discipline with 10 or more years of relevant experience; OR a Master’s degree in Engineering or a related discipline with 8 or more years of relevant experience.
 3 or more years of functional management experience leading organizations of at least 100 employees.
 Progressive leadership experience in manufacturing/production, operations, program management, testing, or a related area, including direct leadership of engineers and/or first‑line managers.
 Demonstrated experience in manufacturing or production engineering supporting complex hardware (e.g., aerospace, defense, electronics, or similar).
 Proven track record of improving manufacturing and test processes, yields, cycle times, and product quality using data and metrics.
 Working knowledge of manufacturing process controls, quality systems, and relevant industry/regulatory standards.
 Demonstrated financial acumen including budgets, rates, and cost management
 Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to clearly present technical and operational content to leadership and customers.
 U.S. citizenship and an ability to obtain U.S. Government Secret security clearance or greater; OR DoE equivalent or greater
 
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Advanced degree in Engineering, Engineering Management, Business Administration, or related field.
 Experience in a Director or senior manager role leading a manufacturing engineering or test engineering organization in an aerospace/defense or similarly regulated environment.
 Experience working across multiple disciplines (design, manufacturing, and test engineering) with a strong focus on product development, producibility, and transition to production.
 Hands‑on experience with continuous improvement frameworks
 Experience managing capital equipment roadmaps and facilities upgrades to support long‑term manufacturing capacity and capability.
 Proven ability to build and develop high‑performing teams, including succession planning, leadership development, and engagement initiatives.
 Experience supporting proposals and customer reviews, including articulation of manufacturing engineering approaches, risks, and mitigations.
 Experience working in a matrixed organization, balancing program demands with functional standards and development needs.
 
 
 
Primary Level Salary Range: $194,600.00 - $292,000.00 
 
The above salary range represents a general guideline; however, Northrop Grumman considers a number of factors when determining base salary offers such as the scope and responsibilities of the position and the candidate's experience, education, skills and current market conditions. 
 
Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay. Annual bonuses are designed to reward individual contributions as well as allow employees to share in company results. Employees in Vice President or Director positions may be eligible for Long Term Incentives. In addition, Northrop Grumman provides a variety of benefits including health insurance coverage, life and disability insurance, savings plan, Company paid holidays and paid time off (PTO) for vacation and/or personal business. 
 
The application period for the job is estimated to be 20 days from the job posting date. However, this timeline may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates. 
 
Northrop Grumman is an Equal Opportunity Employer, making decisions without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, national origin, age, veteran status, disability, or any other protected class. For our complete EEO and pay transparency statement, please visit http://www.northropgrumman.com/EEO. U.S. Citizenship is required for all positions with a government clearance and certain other restricted positions.

role.title: Director, NG9X4 Vehicle Operations
role.description:
Application close date:
Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed. 
 At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!    
 
 
This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities. 
 
 At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We're working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

 This role is part of Blue Origin's Launch Operations organization, where our focus is launching and recovering New Glenn safely, reliably, and at an ever-increasing cadence. Launch Operations owns everything required to turn a rocket into a flight-ready vehicle on the pad and to recover and refly it, from vehicle preparation and integration to pad operations and booster recovery.

 The 9x4 is the next step for New Glenn: a larger, more capable vehicle with a nine-engine booster, built, stacked, and launched vertically. The design decisions made about it now will determine, for the life of the program, how fast, how safely, and how reliably we can assemble, stack, and launch it. As Director of NG9x4 Vehicle Operations, you will be the single leader thinking about the 9x4 from the point of view of the people who will operate it, and the voice of Launch Operations in every decision meeting about the vehicle.
 Reporting to the Vice President of Launch Operations, you will start with a team of about a dozen engineers. Together you will evaluate the vehicle design and the concept of operations and shape both, help define and install the tooling and facilities in our new vertical integration facility, and write the first draft of the work orders for final assembly of the booster and for everything it takes to get the rocket to launch. Some of your scope will also reach the new launch pad being built for this vehicle. If you are successful, you will go on to build the organization that staffs the vertical integration facility and builds and stacks the first 9x4.

 This is a mission-critical leadership role for Blue Origin. We need a leader who drives relentlessly toward results, unencumbered by the old way of doing things, and constantly inventing new ways to solve problems and perform our mission. This leader must not be afraid to get hands-on with engineers and technicians, on the tooling, in the facility, and eventually on the vehicle itself, when the mission requires it, including in the middle of the night. At the same time, your long-term measure of success is building in, from the start, a vehicle and a set of processes that let the Launch Operations teams assemble, stack, and launch at a fast, repeatable, "boring" cadence. You'll make the impossible look routine through detailed, quantitative, hands-on command of the work your team executes down to the individual work order.
 


 WHAT YOU'LL DO
 Be the Voice of Operations on the 9x4 
 Represent Launch Operations in all design, configuration, and readiness decisions for the vehicle, bringing the perspective of the people who will assemble, stack, and launch it
 Evaluate the vehicle design and challenge requirements, driving design changes that make final assembly of the booster, stacking, and launch easier, faster, and safer
 Bring the lessons learned from today's horizontal integration operations into the design of vertical operations, and question which of them still apply
 Partner with vehicle design and engineering, facility, and pad teams so that operations needs are in the design before changes become expensive
 Stand Up Vertical Operations 
 Help shape the tooling, ground support equipment, and other installations in the new vertical integration facility, and help get them procured and installed
 Formalize the concept of operations in greater detail: how the nine-engine booster is finally assembled, how the second stage and payload are stacked vertically, and how the vehicle is prepared and launched
 Write the first draft of the work orders for final assembly of the booster and for all of the preparation needed to get the rocket to launch, and set the standard for high-quality, executable work orders (clear, sequenced, measurable, and completable by shift) so launch readiness is derived from objective data
 Take on operations scope for work at the new launch pad being built for this vehicle
 Lead Execution and Manage Risk 
 Manage technical and schedule risk as the vehicle, the facility, and the tooling come together; when schedule slips, personally own and drive the recovery plan rather than simply reporting the slip
 Perpetuate a high-standard safety culture across all vehicle work, given the significant personnel, process, and material hazards involved
 Be willing to get on the ground with engineers and technicians to solve problems directly, at any hour, when the mission requires it
 Drive Cross-Functional Integration 
 Serve as the primary point of contact between the operations teams and New Glenn vehicle design/engineering, facility, tooling, and pad leadership
 Partner with the business operations function (scheduling and operations analytics) to maintain an objective, data-driven view of remaining work and schedule risk
 Build the organization's own engineering ownership and judgment over time, reducing reliance on borrowed engineering support from other Blue Origin programs
 Build and Lead a High-Performing Organization 
 Lead an initial team of about a dozen engineers, and grow it into the organization that staffs the vertical integration facility and builds and stacks the first 9x4
 Build, mentor, and develop a bench of leaders and engineers in a fast-growing organization
 Take difficult, immature processes and mature them into fast, repeatable operations that don't require nightly heroics to execute
 Foster a culture where every technician and engineer is genuinely excited about Blue Origin's mission and understands the "why" behind the work
 Champion the use of AI to reduce engineering workload (including work-order authoring) and to accelerate the ramp of less experienced engineers
 Deliver Results 
 Use your own data and numerical analysis to understand team performance, drive decisions, and communicate progress
 Set quantitative targets for the labor hours and calendar time to assemble, stack, and launch the 9x4, and shape the vehicle and the processes to meet them, so the vehicle supports a much higher launch cadence
 Present vehicle design, readiness, and risk to Blue Origin's most senior executive leadership, including with little to no coaching
 
 WHAT YOU BRING

 Minimum Qualifications 
 Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Aerospace, or Industrial Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience building and leading complex vehicle or aircraft programs
 7+ years of progressive leadership experience building, integrating, or maintaining complex vehicles, aircraft, or other high-reliability systems: aerospace, defense, marine, oil & gas, or similar heavy/complex-machine environments
 Experience representing operations, manufacturing, or production in design decisions, with a demonstrated track record of challenging engineering requirements and driving design changes to improve manufacturability or maintainability
 Leadership experience with budget and resource management responsibility for technical/operational organizations
 Experience leading multidisciplinary technical teams, with the ability to grow a team and lead through subordinate managers
 A specific, demonstrated track record of driving measurable rate or throughput improvements in a complex manufacturing, assembly, or operations environment
 A demonstrated track record of building and perpetuating a high-standard safety culture in environments with significant personnel, process, or material hazards
 Demonstrated ability to make high-stakes technical and operational decisions under schedule pressure
 Strong executive presence with excellent written and verbal communication skills; demonstrated ability to influence stakeholders at all levels, including senior executive leadership
 Strategic thinker with a bias for action and a track record of hands-on operational execution
 
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Direct experience in final assembly, integration, or maintenance of military or civilian aircraft, weapons systems, or launch vehicles
 Experience with vertical assembly or stacking of large vehicles or structures, such as launch vehicles, or comparable heavy lifting and integration
 Experience standing up a new factory, production line, or facility, including shaping the tooling and the concept of operations
 Experience writing the first work instructions or work orders for a new vehicle or product
 A track record of taking a new vehicle, aircraft, or complex product from first-unit production to rate production
 Hands-on experience as an aircraft mechanic (or similar trade) and/or as a manufacturing engineer
 Working knowledge of aerospace standards and workmanship requirements
 Experience building or scaling an engineering/technical organization from a nascent, dependent state to self-sufficiency
 Master's degree in a related engineering field, or an MBA
 Culture Statement 
 Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

 Export Control Regulations 
 Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

 Background Check 
 Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check
 Required for Certain Job Profiles:  Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation
 Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
 Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical
 
 Benefits 
 Benefits include:  Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program.
 Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)
 Paid Time Off:  Up to four (4) weeks per year based on weekly scheduled hours, and up to 14 company-paid holidays.
 Dependent on role type and job level, employees may be eligible for benefits and bonuses based on the company's intent to reward individual contributions and enable them to share in the company's results, or other factors at the company's sole discretion. Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details. 
 
 Equal Employment Opportunity 
 Blue Origin is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer and is committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly qualified and dedicated work force. Blue Origin hires and promotes people on the basis of their qualifications, performance, and abilities. We support the establishment and maintenance of a workplace that fosters trust, equality, and teamwork. We provide all qualified applicants for employment and employees with equal opportunities for hire, promotion, and other terms and conditions of employment, regardless of their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin/ethnicity, age, physical or mental disability, genetic factors, military/veteran status, or any other status or characteristic protected by federal, state, and/or local law. Blue Origin will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the Washington Fair Chance Act, the California Fair Chance Act, the Los Angeles Fair Chance in Hiring Ordinance, and other applicable laws. For more information on “Know Your Rights,” please see here .

 Affirmative Action and Disability Accommodation 
 Applicants wishing to receive information on Blue Origin’s Affirmative Action Plans, or applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation in order to participate in the application and/or interview process, please contact us at  EEOCompliance@blueorigin.com . Please note this is a publicly managed inbox. Please do not include any personal medical information in your request.

role.title: Head of Operations, Intelligence Systems
role.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE TEAM

 Anduril Intelligence Systems (AIS) is focused on positioning Anduril as a lead provider of specialized engineering and products for Intelligence Community (IC) customers. We work within the IC to understand their requirements, shape their concepts of operation, and deliver exquisite capability across their problem set. We aim to develop and deploy critically needed capabilities that address our customers’ most pressing national security requirements.

 ABOUT THE JOB

 We are looking for a Head of Operations to join our rapidly growing Intelligence Systems team. In this role you will be responsible for all business operations for the business line you support. Your work will vary from quick-turn operational fire-fighting, to building and redesigning processes, to leading high-impact strategic projects. This role requires you to be a trusted partner to each part of the business, and to work with and support the Division leadership teams to achieve our strategic objectives.

 WHAT YOU'LL DO

 
 Partner to the GM — Serve as the right hand to the General Manager of Intelligence Systems, responsible for all internal operations of the business line.

 Act as COO of the business line — Drive day-to-day business operations for Intelligence Systems. This includes business planning & organization design, financial tracking, talent planning & people operations, staffing and hiring, corporate governance, go-to-market, real estate & facility planning, security & infrastructure compliance, proposal & legal support, and sharing the division's narrative — working with cross-functional partners across each of these domains.

 Lead the BizOps team — Lead the Business Operations team within Intelligence Systems, composed of a Business Execution/Services team and Business Analytics, with the potential to include Production Operations/Analytics.

 Own the bottom line — Own the business line P&L and burn rate. Partner with Finance and FP&A to track financial health against division goals, take action to keep operating expenses within budget, and recommend strategies to drive toward margin targets.

role.title: Director of Quality and Informatics
role.description:
### **Director of Quality and Informatics**

**Status:** Full-time **| Location:** Remote (AZ) w/ Occasional On-Site Presence in Tempe 
**Department:** Quality Management | **Reports To:** CMO 
**FLSA Status:** Exempt | **Pay Class:** Salary 
**Salary Range:** $79,793.00 - $105,455.00

SCHEDULE: 40 HOURS WEEKLY, MONDAY-FRIDAY

### **Position Summary**

The Director of Quality and Informatics plays a pivotal leadership role in ensuring the delivery of high-quality, data-informed behavioral healthcare services. This position is responsible for overseeing quality improvement initiatives, clinical data analysis, and informatics strategies that drive performance outcomes, enhance client care, and support regulatory compliance. The Director will lead their team in developing, implementing, and monitoring evidence-based practices, performance metrics, and data systems. This individual will play a pivotal role in driving population health outcomes across all service lines and advancing the organization's value-based care initiatives.This role requires a dynamic individual with a strong background in healthcare quality, informatics, and behavioral health operations who can bridge clinical excellence with data-driven decision-making.

At CPR, we are committed to making diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging an integral part of our daily operations. We strive to hire and retain talented, diverse, and creative individuals, and we are dedicated to ensuring equitable treatment by promoting fairness and respect at every level of our organization.

### **Knowledge and Skills**

* Experience in clinical quality management, regulatory compliance, and outcome measurement
* Proven leadership and team development skills across interdisciplinary teams
* Knowledge of federal and state regulations, including Board of Medical Facilities Licensing (BMFL), Arizona Health Care Cost Containment System (AHCCCS), and Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS), as well as the standards for healthcare quality and compliance.
* Well developed understanding of best clinical practices and evidence -based treatment models for behavioral health
* Extensive knowledge of population health, value-based care models, and risk stratification
* Ability to analyze complex data to inform strategic decisions and drive improvement
* Strong project management and process improvement expertise
* Proficiency with healthcare IT systems (EHR, HIE, data integration)
* Excellent verbal and written communication for reporting and stakeholder engagement
* Understanding of Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) and their impact on health outcomes

### **Primary Duties and Responsibilities**

* Lead initiatives to enhance clinical quality, including process improvements, audits, and compliance with regulatory standards
* Manage technology systems to support quality improvement and clinical performance, including overseeing EHR optimization and data integration
* Oversee population health management programs, including monitoring and reporting on Value-Based Contracts (VBC) and shared savings agreements
* Collaborate with health plans and other stakeholders to develop and implement targeted interventions for improving patient outcomes and addressing SDOH
* Facilitate cross-functional meetings to ensure alignment with business goals, including regular reviews of VBC performance, quality metrics, and operational efficiencies
* Conduct data analysis and report on performance, outcomes, and opportunities for improvement across all departments
* Lead special projects to drive innovation and efficiency, including Targeted Investments (TI) and Data Analytics & Performance (DAP) initiatives
* Provide oversight of client satisfaction surveys and ensure continuous feedback loops to improve service delivery
* Develop and maintain key strategic partnerships to ensure the success of population health initiatives, with a focus on behavioral health integration
* Provide departmental leadership and supervision to direct reports, including performance management, coaching, hiring, and training
* Manage the department’s budget, resources, and operational strategies to support departmental goals.
* Reliable and predictable attendance is an essential job function.
* Other duties as assigned

### **Qualifications and Education Requirements**

* Bachelor’s degree in Social Work, Counseling, Healthcare Administration, or related field required.
* Minimum of 2 years in a management or supervisory role in behavioral health or healthcare required.
* Master’s degree in Social Work, Counseling, Healthcare Administration, or related field preferred but not required.
* Current, unrestricted license issued by the Arizona Board of Behavioral Health Examiners: LCSW (Licensed Clinical Social Worker), LPC (Licensed Professional Counselor), Ph.D (Doctor of Philosophy), Psy.D (Doctor of Psychology) preferred but not required.

### **Other Requirements**

* Provide evidence of professional liability insurance coverage in the amount acceptable, minimum $1/$3 million.
* Must comply with training and supervision requirements during first 90 days of employment, and throughout employment.
* All licensed, certified, and registered staff will be monitored regarding restrictions.
* Appropriate reference checks by letter and telephone as requested.
* State-required background check.
* Medicare/Medicaid sanctions, criminal violations, subsequent malpractice actions, and any settlement(s) made on behalf of practitioners.
* Within seven (7) days of hire, apply for and/or present and maintain a Class One Fingerprint Clearance card. If application is necessary, a copy must be submitted for inclusion in the personnel file until card (and/or renewals) is received.
* All required renewals must be submitted 30 days prior to expiration date. It is the duty of the licensee to keep all renewals active and current and report any mandated changes to Arizona Board of Behavioral Health Examiners immediately.

role.description:
Job Summary:

### **Position Summary**

The Director of Quality is an execution-focused leader responsible for translating WellBe’s enterprise quality strategy into disciplined, measurable operations across markets and health plan contracts.

This role leads the day-to-day Quality function, manages and develops team members, and redesigns care-gap closure workflows to be simpler, standardized, scalable, and integrated into clinical practice.

The Director partners closely with market, clinical, pharmacy, analytics, technology, coding, and health plan stakeholders to improve HEDIS and Medicare Advantage Stars performance, strengthen data reliability, increase frontline accountability, and ensure the organization consistently converts quality insights into action.

Job Description:

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities** 
Lead day-to-day execution of the Quality program across Part C and Part D, converting enterprise goals into clear workplans, owners, timelines, operating rhythms, and measurable results. 
Directly manage, coach, and performance-manage Quality team members; establish clear productivity, quality, service, and accountability standards. 
Map end-to-end care-gap closure workflows across measures, markets, and health plan contracts; identify handoffs, rework, manual steps, failure points, and unnecessary variation. 
Redesign and standardize workflows so care-gap identification, outreach, documentation, closure, submission, and reconciliation are consistently executed and sustainable at scale. 
Engage Markets using structured working sessions that diagnose barriers, assign actions, monitor commitments, and drive closure at the patient, provider, measure, and market levels. 
Partner with clinical operations and technology teams to surface prioritized care gaps at the point of care and embed closure activities into APP workflows. 
Lead implementation and adoption of Quality workflow tools, including in-house technologies, point-of-care solutions, telephony or workforce-management tools, and future AI-enabled capabilities. 
Oversee HEDIS chart abstraction, primary source validation, medical record retrieval, supplemental data submissions, and health plan audit support, with an emphasis on accuracy, timeliness, and reduced manual effort. 
Manage medication adherence and other Part D outreach operations; use performance and workflow data to improve productivity, assess capacity, and inform staffing decisions. 
Partner with analytics, IT, and health plan teams to strengthen WellBe-owned quality reporting using claims, EMR, pharmacy, and supplemental data; reconcile numerator, denominator, timing, and data-integrity differences. 
Use market-, provider-, measure-, and patient-level data to prioritize interventions, forecast performance, monitor outcomes, and adjust tactics quickly when results are off track. 
Evaluate and implement practical automation and AI-assisted solutions that reduce repetitive work, improve chart-review efficiency, and allow the team to focus on higher-value intervention and market partnership. 
Own point-of-care solution assessment and implementation, including identification of operational pain points, vendor coordination, rollout planning, training, adoption, and performance monitoring. 
Maintain current knowledge of NCQA, HEDIS, CMS, Stars, and applicable health plan requirements; ensure workflows, documentation, submissions, and controls remain compliant. 
Build effective cross-functional relationships and drive decisions with stakeholders across clinical operations, pharmacy, coding, analytics, technology, finance, compliance, markets, and external vendors.

Job Requirements:

### **Required Qualifications**

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in nursing, healthcare administration, public health, health sciences, business, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.

**Experience:** Seven or more years of progressive experience in healthcare quality, managed care, provider operations, population health, HEDIS, or Medicare Advantage Stars, including 3–5 years of people-management experience. Demonstrated experience setting expectations, coaching team members, managing performance, delivering measurable operational results, and mapping, redesigning, implementing, and sustaining complex workflows across multiple teams, markets, or contracts.

**Skills:** Strong working knowledge of NCQA HEDIS specifications, Medicare Advantage Stars, care-gap closure, medical record review, supplemental data, and quality operations. Proven ability to move between strategy and execution, manage multiple priorities, remove barriers, and deliver results in a fast-paced, matrixed organization. Strong people leadership, change-management, project-management, process-improvement, problem-solving, and written and verbal communication skills. Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel and presentation tools; experience with workflow platforms, reporting tools, automation, or AI-enabled healthcare solutions preferred. High attention to detail, sound judgment, and the ability to maintain confidentiality.

### **Physical and Mental Requirements**

* Ability to stand or sit for extended periods.
* Visual acuity and fine motor.
* Ability to travel locally or nationally as needed.

### **Work Environment**

This role operates in a corporate, primarily remote environment and requires frequent collaboration across functions, markets, and external partners. Occasional travel and schedule flexibility may be required to support market operations, implementations, audits, and business priorities. No routine on-call responsibilities are expected.

### **Sponsorship Statement**

WellBe does not offer employment-based visa sponsorship for this position. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship now or in the future.

### **Pay Transparency Statement**

Compensation for this position will be disclosed in accordance with applicable state and local pay transparency laws.

### **Safety-Sensitive Statement**

This position has been designated as safety-sensitive. As such, the employee must be able to perform job duties in a manner that ensures the safety of themselves, coworkers, patients, and the public. The role requires full cognitive and physical functioning at all times.

Employees in safety-sensitive positions are subject to drug and alcohol testing, including for substances that may impair judgment or motor function, in accordance with applicable federal and state laws and company policy. Due to the safety-sensitive nature of this role and in alignment with federal law and workplace safety standards, the use of marijuana—including medical or recreational use—is prohibited. WellBe Senior Medical will comply with applicable state laws regarding medical marijuana and reasonable accommodations, where such laws do not conflict with safety requirements or federal regulations.

### **Drug Screening Requirement**

As a condition of employment, WellBe Senior Medical requires all candidates to successfully complete a pre-employment drug screening. Ongoing employment may also be contingent upon compliance with the company’s Drug-Free Workplace Policy, which includes random, post-accident, and reasonable suspicion drug testing. The company reserves the right to test for substances that may impair an employee’s ability to safely and effectively perform their job duties.

### **Background Check Statement**

Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a background check, as permitted by law. As a healthcare organization, WellBe conducts monthly FACIS (Fraud and Abuse Control Information System) checks on all employees. Continued employment is contingent upon satisfactory results of these checks, in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

### **Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) Statement**

WellBe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or any other legally protected status.

### **Americans with Disabilities Act**

WellBe Senior Medical is committed to complying with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and applicable state and local laws. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job. If you require an accommodation during the application, interview or employment process, please contact Human Resources at HRPeopleLine@wellbe.com

### **At-Will Employment Statement**

Employment with WellBe is at-will unless otherwise specified by contract. This job description does not constitute an employment contract.

### **Disclaimer**

This job description is intended to describe the general nature and level of work performed. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required. Management reserves the right to modify, add, or remove duties as necessary.

**Job Description**

**General Summary:**

The Senior Director, Device Quality provides strategic Quality leadership and oversight for Vertex device and combination product operations across development, manufacturing, testing, clinical, commercial, and post-market activities.

The role is accountable for **risk-based operational Quality oversight of internal activities and external partners** , including CDMOs, testing laboratories, and critical suppliers. The role ensures compliance with **ISO 13485, 21 CFR Part 820, ISO 14971** , and applicable global device and combination product requirements.

The Senior Director serves as the **Management Representative for the Device QMS** , providing leadership for QMS effectiveness, regulatory compliance, management review, inspection readiness, and continual improvement. The role partners with senior Quality and business leaders on **enterprise Quality initiatives** .

 

**Key Duties and Responsibilities:**

• Define and execute the **Device Operational QA strategy** aligned with business, portfolio, and product priorities.

• Provide Quality oversight of **CDMOs, suppliers, testing laboratories, and other external partners** , including quality agreements, audits, performance, and risk management.

• Provide Quality oversight of **internal design control, design transfer, manufacturing, testing, and product realization activities** .

• Serve as **Management Representative** for the Device QMS, ensuring QMS effectiveness, management review, compliance, and continual improvement.

• Ensure compliance with **ISO 13485, 21 CFR Part 820, ISO 14971** , and applicable global regulatory requirements.

• Provide strategic oversight of **deviations, investigations, CAPA, change control, complaints, supplier quality, audits, and inspection readiness** .

• Establish and monitor **Quality metrics, risks, trends, and performance** , driving timely escalation and resolution of significant issues.

• Provide Quality leadership for **regulatory inspections, notified body audits, product milestones, and launch readiness** .

• Partner with senior leaders on **enterprise-wide Quality initiatives** that improve compliance, operational effectiveness, and business performance.

* Build organizational capability through **talent development, coaching, and strong cross-functional leadership** **.**

 

**Knowledge and Skills:**

• Broad expertise in **Device and Combination Product Quality Assurance, QMS, and operational Quality oversight** .

• Strong knowledge of **ISO 13485, 21 CFR Part 820, ISO 14971** , and applicable global regulatory requirements.

• Demonstrated experience with **CDMO/external partner oversight, supplier Quality, testing, audits, and inspection readiness** .

• Strong understanding of **design controls, design transfer, risk management, manufacturing controls, supplier controls, and product realization** .

• Proven experience with **CAPA, investigations, deviations, change control, complaints, and quality risk management** .

• Demonstrated capability to serve as **Management Representative** , including QMS performance, management review, compliance oversight, and risk escalation.

• Strong **strategic thinking, business acumen, risk-based decision-making, and problem-solving** skills.

• Ability to influence senior leaders and drive outcomes in a **complex, matrixed organization** .

• Demonstrated leadership in **cross-functional strategic initiatives** .

• Strong people leadership skills with demonstrated ability to **develop talent, build organizational capability, and foster Quality ownership** .

 

**Education and Experience:**

* Bachelors degree in a scientific, allied health, or operations research field

You will own evaluation and quality assurance for every layer of the product — from whether the system is being correctly triggered for the right set of user requests, through whether it surfaces and ranks the right results, to whether the underlying transactions execute correctly, including integrations with external partner APIs, and financial systems.
Quality here isn't a single test suite — it spans conversational understanding, relevance and ranking, and revenue-bearing correctness, all against a large, constantly evolving real-world dataset.
You will create and drive the evaluation and quality strategy and implementation for the product.
