role.title: Sr. Manager, Quality Assurance
role.description:
**Company Summary: PuraGraft, a Young Innovations Company**

PuraGraft represents the leading manufacturers of biomaterial solutions for bone and tissue regeneration. No single material can suit all medical requirements and indications. However, through PuraGraft® you have access to the widest choices of products.

At Young Innovations, we foster a dynamic environment where team members make an impact every day as part of a collaborative, inclusive culture. Together, we serve the dental profession and their patients, united in our mission of achieving a Lifetime of Oral Health™

We embrace diverse perspectives and encourage bold thinking, challenging traditional approaches with a bias for action. Whether you’re looking to expand your skills or grow your career, Young is here to support your goals and continuous learning. At Young, YOU are at the core of what we do.

**Position Overview:**

Reporting to the VP Quality Regulatory Affairs, the Sr. Manager, Quality Assurance will be tasked with ensuring Quality standards are met or exceeded in all facets of the multi-site operation. He/she will partner internally in the development and implementation of new or adjusted quality standards, policies, and procedures, as required at Kingwood, TX and Scottsdale, AZ.

**You’ll like this role if:**

* You enjoy leading a team, solving complex quality challenges, and turning data into practical improvements. You take ownership of compliance and thrive in a hands-on role supporting quality standards across multiple sites.

**Why You’ll Love Working Here:**

* Medium sized company – not too big, not too small – just enough to get things done and see your impact.
* Did we say benefits? Full medical, dental, vision, 401k, parental leave, paid holidays, paid time off, short & long term disability insurance, employee assistance program, and more!
* Lead and inspire a dedicated team, build meaningful relationships, and help your employees grow and succeed.

**Who you’ll work with:**

* You’ll report to the VP of Quality & Regulatory Affairs and lead Quality Associates supporting our Kingwood, TX and Scottsdale, AZ operations.
* You’ll partner closely with QRA, Sourcing, Distribution, and Production teams to strengthen quality systems and drive continuous improvement.

**What You’ll Do:**

* Act as the site’s Sr. Quality and Compliance Leader, and when necessary, as the site’s Designated Management Representative to ensure compliance with all regulatory, corporate and facility requirements.
* Ensure compliance of two sites.
* Ensure outstanding Quality System performance via monitoring and measuring of process performance, and driving any appropriate action, including issuing and follow-up on activities required for sourcing, warehousing, and distributing pharmaceuticals.
* Supervise & Manage Quality Associates and develop culture of collaboration and cross-functional success within the department and business.
* Reviews and monitors Quality metrics and reports trends, to determine if there is a need to escalate issues to the management.
* Perform, review and monitor the Quality Management processes which include but is not limited to:
 + Ensure compliance with FDA, DEA and BOP requirements, including DSCSA traceability of pharmaceuticals.
 + Oversee Regulatory activities associated with distribution licensing, drug distribution reports, and permits for warehousing and distribution of controlled substances.
 + inspection and product release, label approval, calibration, warehousing controls, record retention, document control, training, control of non-conforming product, quarantined Products, control of access and drugs storage, including temperature monitoring.
 + Host and manage internal and external audits. Ensure the site’s readiness for assessments and lead implementation of corrective actions.
 + Effectively assess processes and identify opportunities for improvement.
 + Review, Analyze and Report Statistical findings through critical thought and storytelling of key findings and opportunities to all levels within a matrixed organization.
 + Partner with other departments to identify critical to quality metrics, and support the operationalization of monitoring and management to deliver improved performance across processes.
 + Create effective and compelling visual materials/presentations that support the process/product improvement impact to the organization and adequately represent the impact to quality, cost and time.
 + Define, track, and monitor key success measures associated with Quality Management Systems. Successfully deploy and support change management and appropriate training plans.
* Manage document control functions, including creation, review, and approval of procedures, work instructions and all other documentation for the Quality System.
* Manage the complaint handling system, including trending and review to identify opportunities for improvement.
* Manage the training of the Site, by maintaining the training log, tracking training completion of training by site personnel, creating training content and hosting group training as needed.
* Develop and host the Quarterly Management Review
* Manage the Recall process, from notification, tracking responses & expenses, reporting, and closure.
* Develop, refine, and/or maintain quality standards, policies, and procedures for the facility, including identifying, recommending, and fully implementing changes, in partnership with corporate QRA and local operations teams. Other duties as assigned

**What You’ll Bring:**

* Bachelor’s degree in technical field.
* Minimum of 3 Years of experience managing manufacturing and/or distribution of pharmaceuticals.
* Minimum of 3 Years of experience having direct responsibility for managing a Quality group.
* Direct experience managing FDA or DEA Inspections.
* Demonstrated proficiency in verbal and written communication in English, with the ability to convey information clearly, accurately, and professionally across all levels of the organization.

**Travel Requirements**

* Up to 15%

**Work Environment:**

**Office Environment**

This position is based in an office environment and is primarily sedentary in nature. It requires regular use of standard office equipment, including computers, phones, photocopiers, scanners, filing cabinets, and fax machines. Some roles may involve wearing a headset and sustained computer use for 8 or more hours per day. Employees may be required to sit, stand, or walk for extended periods, and occasional bending, lifting, or carrying items up to 50 pounds may be necessary.

**Manufacturing/Distribution Environment**

This position operates in a manufacturing plant environment. The role routinely involves working around machinery, equipment, and moving mechanical parts. The facility may be subject to varying temperatures, loud noise levels, and airborne particles such as dust or chemical fumes, depending on the area of the plant. This role may require periods of standing, sitting, or walking throughout the workday. Occasional bending, lifting, or carrying items up to 50 pounds may be necessary.

Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus. While performing the duties of this Job, the employee is regularly required to sit; use hands to finger, handle, control, or feel; reach with hands and arms and talk. Hearing abilities required for this environment include being able to clearly hear and respond to audible alarms, production equipment, forklifts, and other machinery to maintain a safe work environment. Individuals must be able to distinguish and understand verbal communication including instructions, safety warnings, and team discussions, sometimes in an environment with moderate to high background noise.

*US: Young Innovations, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer and E-Verify participating employer.*

role.title: Director Operational Excellence
role.description:
As a Director of Operational Excellence here at Honeywell, you will be responsible for leading and overseeing the implementation of Honeywell Manufacturing Excellence (HMX) across multiple business units.

As a Director of Operational Excellence here at Honeywell, you will be responsible for leading and overseeing the implementation of Honeywell Manufacturing Excellence (HMX) across multiple business units. You will play a critical role in driving operational excellence and continuous improvement. As a strategic leader, you will collaborate with senior leaders to identify improvement opportunities and develop a strategic roadmap for HOS aligned with business goals. If you are a visionary leader with a passion for driving change and operational excellence, this is the perfect opportunity for you. Join us at Honeywell and be part of a talented team dedicated to shaping the future.

 

YOU MUST HAVE

* 8+ years of experience and mastery in implementing and driving continuous improvement initiatives
* 8+ years of experience in proven leadership of managers and individual contributors
* Strong knowledge of Lean Six Sigma methodologies
* Ability to work effectively in a cross-functional team environment
* Ability to clearly and concisely communicate at all levels of the organization.
Ability to travel up to 50% 

WE VALUE

* Strategic mindset and ability to align HOS initiatives with business objectives
* Ability to lead and inspire cross-functional teams
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
Passion for continuous improvement and driving change 

The annual base salary range for this position is $189,000 - $235,000. This position is incentive plan eligible. Please note that this salary information serves as a general guideline. Honeywell considers various factors when extending an offer, including but not limited to the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate's work experience, education and training, key skills, as well as market and business considerations.

In addition to a competitive salary, leading-edge work, and developing solutions side-by-side with dedicated experts in their fields, Honeywell employees are eligible for a comprehensive benefits package. This package includes employer subsidized Medical, Dental, Vision, and Life Insurance; Short-Term and Long-Term Disability; 401(k) match, Flexible Spending Accounts, Health Savings Accounts, EAP, and Educational Assistance; Parental Leave, Paid Time Off (for vacation, personal business, sick time, and parental leave), and 12 Paid Holidays. For more information visit: Benefits at Honeywell

The application period for the job is estimated to be 40 days from the job posting date; however, this may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates.

 

Key Responsibilities

* Strategize and oversee the success of the implementation of Honeywell Manufacturing Excellence (HMX) across the business
* Work with the individual sites to Develop and execute the strategic roadmap for HMX, aligning it with business goals and objectives
* Provide guidance and mentorship to HMX Senior Managers and teams in implementing Lean methodologies and tools
* Monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of HMX site assessments initiatives, making recommendations for enhancements
* Prepare monthly updates with sites and Senior management aligned with deliverables for each of the sites under scope of responsibilities.
* Participate in operational improvements as needed within the sites under scope of responsibilities to include productivity improvements tied to continuous improvement.

 
Honeywell Technologies is a global, pure-play automation company with a legacy of innovating to help solve the world’s most mission-critical challenges, enhancing the quality of life for people and communities around the world. We serve the building, industrial and process sectors with a broad portfolio of services, solutions and products, underpinned by our Honeywell Technologies Accelerator operating system and Honeywell Technologies Forge intelligence layer. By combining the deep domain expertise of our more than 50,000 employees with decades of data from our global installed base, we are uniquely positioned to lead the industrial sector’s transition from automation to autonomy.

role.title: Director of Manufacturing, Operations & Assembly
role.description:
Application close date:

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities.

**About Blue Origin**

We are a team of collaborators, doers, and problem-solvers who are relentlessly committed to a culture of safety. These positions will directly impact the history of space exploration and will require your commitment and detailed attention towards safe and repeatable spaceflight. Join us in lowering the cost of access to space and enabling Blue Origin's vision of millions of people living and working in space to benefit Earth.

We are looking for senior leaders to apply their technical expertise , leadership skills, and commitment to quality to positively impact safe human spaceflight. Passion for our mission and vision is required .

**About This Opportunity**

Blue Origin is actively building its senior manufacturing and operations leadership team across multiple sites. We are seeking experienced Directors and Senior Directors with a strong aerospace background to lead high-performing teams in support of rocket engine and spacecraft production programs.

By expressing interest in this opportunity, you will be considered for current and future openings aligned to your experience and location preference. Roles span the following functional areas:

**Manufacturing**

Provides senior leadership across production operations including assembly, machine shop, heat treat, welding, and component fabrication for space systems and propulsion programs. Accountable for establishing and maintaining process controls, driving production efficiency, and ensuring safe, repeatable spaceflight hardware delivery at all stages of the product lifecycle.

**Test**

Provides leadership across test operations supporting engine, component , and system-level testing. Accountable for ensuring test processes are executed safely, efficiently, and in alignment with program requirements. Drives continuous improvement in test throughput, first-time quality, and the feedback loop between test results and production processes.

**Fabrication**

Provides leadership across fabrication operations including machining, welding, composites, additive manufacturing, cleaning, and post-processing of flight hardware. Accountable for the development, qualification, and continuous improvement of fabrication processes and capabilities that meet the demanding quality and schedule requirements of space and propulsion programs.

**Integration**

Provides leadership across integration operations supporting the assembly and verification of complex space systems, launch vehicles, and propulsion hardware. Accountable for coordinating cross-functional teams to ensure the safe, on-time integration of hardware in alignment with engineering requirements, mission assurance standards, and program milestones.

**Key Responsibilities:**

Leaders across these functional areas are expected to:

* Lead and develop teams of Managers , Senior Managers , and Directors driving manufacturing and operations execution across space and propulsion programs
* Champion a culture of safety, quality, and continuous improvement across all functional teams
* Own departmental KPIs, budgets, staffing plans, and capital project portfolios
* Partner with Program Management, Site Leadership, and cross-functional stakeholders to meet production schedules and customer expectations
* Drive process definition, development, deployment, and improvement initiatives including Lean Manufacturing and root cause analysis
* Collaborate with engineering teams to advance Design for Manufacturability principles and accelerate the transition from development to production
* Implement and mature production frameworks that support world-class manufacturing capabilities
* Communicate and enforce mission assurance and safety principles throughout the organization
* Recruit, develop, coach, and mentor talent at all levels of the organization

**Minimum Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in Mechanical , Manufacturing, Industrial, Aerospace, or Electrical Engineering, or equivalent experience
* 15 or more years of progressive experience in aerospace manufacturing or a closely related industry, such as launch vehicles, aircraft , spacecraft systems, or defense
* 5 or more years in a senior leadership role managing managers and large, cross-functional teams
* Demonstrated experience leading manufacturing and operations teams in fast-paced, complex environments
* Proven ability to manage budgets, schedules, and capital projects at a department or program level
* Strong quality mindset with expertise in root cause analysis and corrective action methodologies
* Experience with process definition, development, deployment, measurement, and continuous improvement
* Effective communicator across all levels of an organization, including executive leadership
* Must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Master's degree, MBA, or advanced degree in a relevant engineering or business field
* Prior experience in aerospace environments supporting space hardware, rocket propulsion, or other mission-critical, high-value components
* Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing, the Toyota Production System, or Six Sigma; Black Belt certification preferred
* Experience transitioning manufacturing capabilities from development and prototyping into full-rate production
* Knowledge of fabrication processes including machining, welding, composites, additive manufacturing, cleaning, and non-destructive testing
* Experience with facility activation, new production line startup, or multi-site manufacturing operations
* Proficiency with MRP/ERP, PLM, and Manufacturing Execution Systems

 

Base Pay Range for:

WA applicants is $203,165.00 - $284,430.30

**Other site ranges may differ**

 

**Culture Statement**

Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

 

**Export Control Regulations**

Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

 

**Background Check**

* Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical 

 

**Benefits**

* Benefits include: Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program.
* Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)
* Paid Time Off: Up to four (4) weeks per year based on weekly scheduled hours, and up to 14 company-paid holidays.
Dependent on role type and job level, employees may be eligible for benefits and bonuses based on the company's intent to reward individual contributions and enable them to share in the company's results, or other factors at the company's sole discretion. Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details. 

 

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

Blue Origin is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer and is committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly qualified and dedicated work force. Blue Origin hires and promotes people on the basis of their qualifications, performance, and abilities. We support the establishment and maintenance of a workplace that fosters trust, equality, and teamwork. We provide all qualified applicants for employment and employees with equal opportunities for hire, promotion, and other terms and conditions of employment, regardless of their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin/ethnicity, age, physical or mental disability, genetic factors, military/veteran status, or any other status or characteristic protected by federal, state, and/or local law. Blue Origin will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the Washington Fair Chance Act, the California Fair Chance Act, the Los Angeles Fair Chance in Hiring Ordinance, and other applicable laws.

 

**Affirmative Action and Disability Accommodation**

Applicants wishing to receive information on Blue Origin’s Affirmative Action Plans, or applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation in order to participate in the application and/or interview process, please contact us at EEOCompliance@blueorigin.com . Please note this is a publicly managed inbox. Please do not include any personal medical information in your request.

role.title: Americas Procurement Director, External Manufacturing
role.description:
**Americas Procurement Director, External Manufacturing**
=========================================================

HUNT VALLEY, MD, US, 21031

You may know McCormick as a leader in herbs, spices, seasonings, and condiments – and we’re only getting started. At McCormick, we’re always looking for new people to bring their unique flavor to our team.

McCormick employees – all 14,000 of us across the world – are what makes this company a great place to work.

 

We are looking to hire an **Americas Procurement Director, External Manufacturing** immediately in a Hybrid (50/50) capacity at our Global Headquarters in Hunt Valley, Maryland.

 

**What We Bring To The Table:**

The best people deserve the best rewards. In addition to the benefits you’d expect from a global leader (401k, health insurance, paid time off, etc.) we also offer:

* Competitive compensation

* Career growth opportunities

* Flexibility and Support for Diverse Life Stages and Choices

 

**Position Overview**
 
Leads the commercial strategy, supplier relationships, and performance management for the Americas external manufacturing network, including co-manufacturers, co-packers, and strategic third-party manufacturing partners.
 
Accountable for delivering safe, compliant, reliable, cost-competitive, and scalable supply in support of business growth, innovation, customer service, and profitability objectives. Leads a procurement team and partners closely with Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Quality, Food Safety, Regulatory, R&D, Finance, Legal, and Commercial teams to deliver total value, manage risk, and strengthen supplier capability.

 

**Key Responsibilities**

* Develops and executes the Americas external manufacturing procurement strategy, including supplier segmentation, network optimization, make-buy analysis, capacity strategy, sourcing, and long-term value creation.
* Leads complex commercial negotiations and contracting, including manufacturing service agreements, pricing, capacity commitments, service levels, change control, risk allocation, and supplier exit provisions.
* Leads strategic supplier relationship management, including executive engagement, supplier scorecards, quarterly business reviews, corrective-action plans, and joint productivity and innovation initiatives.
* Ensures supply assurance and business continuity by identifying and mitigating supplier, capacity, quality, financial, geographic, and operational risks. Leads commercial response and recovery plans for material supplier disruptions.
* Partners with Quality, Food Safety, Regulatory, Manufacturing, Planning, R&D, Finance, and Legal to support commercialization, product transitions, compliance, supplier qualification, and operational performance.
* Leads annual operating plan, forecasting, standard-cost, productivity, inflation-mitigation, and financial performance management for the external manufacturing portfolio.
* Leads, develops, and retains a high-performing procurement team. Drives change management, capability development, process improvement, and adoption of data-driven procurement practices.
 

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s Degree in Supply Chain, Business, Finance, Accounting or applicable field of study required.
* 10+ years of progressive procurement, supply chain, operations, or strategic sourcing experience required.
* 5+ years of people leadership and/or leadership of complex cross-functional teams required.
* Experience managing strategic supplier relationships, complex commercial negotiations, and significant spend or P&L impact required.
* Experience in external manufacturing, or a similarly complex outsourced operations environment required.
* Strong financial acumen, including total cost of ownership, cost modeling, forecasting, productivity, and risk management required.
* Demonstrated ability to influence senior internal stakeholders and executive-level supplier partners. Strong negotiation, communication, change leadership, conflict resolution, and decision-making skills required.
* Strategic thinking; supplier relationship management; contract management; analytical and problem-solving capability; project and change management; customer focus; collaboration; accountability; agility; continuous improvement; and inclusive people leadership.
 

#LI-CG1

 

**As a general policy, McCormick does not offer employment visa sponsorships upon hire or in the future.**

McCormick & Company is an equal opportunity/affirmative action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law.

 

===

 

Base Salary: $140,500 - $239,000

Base salary compensation will be determined based on factors such as geographic location, skills, education, experience for this role, and/or internal equity of our current employees as part of any final offer. This position is also eligible to participate in McCormick’s Incentive Bonus (MIB) Plan. In addition to a competitive compensation package, permanent employees of McCormick are eligible for our extensive Total Rewards programs that include:

* Comprehensive health plans covering medical, vision, dental, life and disability benefits

* Family-friendly benefits such as paid parental leave, fertility benefits, Employee Assistance Program, and caregiver support

* Retirement and investment programs including 401(k) and profit-sharing plans

**WHY WORK AT MCCORMICK?**
--------------------------

As a McCormick employee you’ll be empowered to focus on more than your individual responsibilities. You’ll have the opportunity to be part of something bigger than yourself—to have a say in where the company is going and how it’s growing.

Between our passion for flavor, our 130-year history of leadership and integrity, the competitive and comprehensive benefits we offer, and our culture, which is built on respect and opportunities for growth, there are many reasons to join us at McCormick.

**Nearest Major Market:** Baltimore

role.title: Director of Operations
role.description:
**Director of Operations** 
**Micro-Tronics, Inc. | Tempe, AZ**

Full-Time | Exempt 
Shift: Monday-Friday, 6:00 am to 4:00 pm

**About Micro-Tronics**
=======================

Micro-Tronics, Inc. is a precision aerospace manufacturing company committed to operational excellence, quality, and continuous improvement. We are seeking a results-driven Director of Operations to lead our manufacturing operations and drive performance across production, quality, supply chain, maintenance, and workforce planning. This role is instrumental in delivering customer commitments, achieving revenue objectives, improving operational efficiency, and fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

**Position Summary**
====================

The Director of Operations oversees daily plant operations with primary accountability for reducing past-due orders, improving manufacturing efficiency, and achieving company revenue targets while maintaining the highest standards of quality and safety. This position provides strategic and operational leadership across manufacturing operations, labor planning, production scheduling, budgeting, and continuous improvement initiatives. The Director of Operations aligns production capacity, scheduling, and shipments with customer commitments and business objectives while driving corrective actions when performance falls short.

**Key Interactions and Relationships**
======================================

Internal: Senior Management, Assembly, Machining, Elastomer Manufacturing, Quality Control, Maintenance, Supply Chain, Human Resources.

External: Customers, Suppliers, Regulatory Agencies and Governing Bodies.

**Key Responsibilities**
========================

* Supervise and manage plant personnel, including recruiting, training, coaching, and performance management.
* Plan, organize, direct, and manage daily operations to reduce past-due orders, improve manufacturing efficiency, and achieve revenue objectives.
* Develop and improve manufacturing processes to increase throughput and labor productivity while reducing cycle times, downtime, scrap, and rework.
* Oversee production scheduling, maintenance, and logistics to ensure customer delivery commitments are achieved.
* Monitor past-due orders, prioritize recovery efforts, and eliminate material and capacity constraints.
* Manage operational budgets and expenses.
* Ensure all products meet customer requirements, regulatory standards, and company quality objectives.
* Maintain a safe work environment through enforcement of company policies, procedures, and OSHA requirements.
* Manage operational budgets and expenses while aligning production and shipment performance with monthly and quarterly revenue goals.
* Establish and maintain effective controls over capital expenditures, operating expenses, staffing, and labor costs.
* Maintain and review operational scorecards and KPIs while coordinating corrective actions with Quality, Supply Chain, Finance, and Human Resources.
* Drive resolution of safety incidents, customer returns, nonconformances, production scrap, inventory concerns, and supplier performance issues.

**Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)**
=====================================

* Operational efficiency and productivity
* Product quality and compliance
* On-time delivery and backlog reduction
* Revenue growth and budget management
* Safety and risk performance
* Scrap, nonconformance, and customer return reduction
* Inventory accuracy and customer satisfaction

**Qualifications**
==================

**Education, Licenses and Certifications**

A bachelor's degree in engineering, manufacturing, business administration, or a related field is required.

**Leadership Skills / Soft Skills**

* Excellent leadership and communication skills.
* Strong problem-solving capabilities.
* Ability to foster a positive and productive work environment.
* Mentorship and team-building skills.
* Adaptability and a continuous improvement mindset.

**Individual Contributor Knowledge and Skills**

* Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.
* Experience with ERP/MRP systems.
* Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement methodologies.
* Strong organizational and time management skills.
* Ability to analyze operational data and make informed decisions.
* Knowledge of industry regulations and compliance requirements.

**Physical Requirements**
=========================

This is an active position requiring the ability to:

* Stand and walk for extended periods.
* Sit for extended periods as business needs require.
* Operate forklifts, scissor lifts, and other material handling equipment.
* Lift and move up to **50 pounds**.
* Work throughout manufacturing environments, including elevated work areas and outdoor conditions when necessary.
* Wear required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE).

**Our Values**
==============

* **Being Accountable** – Taking ownership of responsibilities, following through on commitments, acting with integrity, and producing quality results.
* **Being Collaborative** – Working respectfully and effectively with others, sharing knowledge, communicating openly, and contributing to team success.
* **Being Empowered** – Demonstrating initiative, solving problems proactively, embracing continuous improvement, and making informed decisions within the scope of the position

**Benefits**
============

At Micro-Tronics Inc., we recognize how important your career and benefits are to you and your family. We offer a full suite of benefits, including medical, dental, vision, short- and long-term disability coverage, accident insurance, critical illness insurance, basic and supplemental life insurance, employee assistance plan, retirement savings and matching, and other developmental opportunities. We are committed to supporting the way you live and work.

**Apply Today**
===============

If you are passionate about operational leadership, manufacturing excellence, continuous improvement, and driving business results, we encourage you to apply and become part of the Micro-Tronics team.

**Micro-Tronics is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected status. Applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to complete the application process may contact Human Resources.**

**This position requires access to information subject to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). Employment is contingent upon the applicant being a “U.S. person” as defined by ITAR (22 CFR §120.15), which includes U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, refugees, or asylees, as required by U.S. export control laws**.

role.description:
Application close date:

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities.

**About Blue Origin** 
We are a team of collaborators, doers, and problem-solvers who are relentlessly committed to a culture of safety. These positions will directly impact the history of space exploration and will require your commitment and detailed attention towards safe and repeatable spaceflight. Join us in lowering the cost of access to space and enabling Blue Origin's vision of millions of people living and working in space to benefit Earth.

 

As a Sr. Director for Manufacturing at Blue Origin’s manufacturing, production, and launch facilities, this role will have a direct impact on the success of Blue’s mission.

We are looking for senior leaders to apply their technical expertise, leadership skills, and commitment to quality to positively impact safe human spaceflight. Passion for our mission and vision is required.

 

**About This Opportunity** 
Blue Origin is actively building its senior manufacturing and operations leadership team across multiple sites. We are seeking an experienced Sr. Director with a strong aerospace background to lead high-performing teams in support of our rocket production program. This role will span the following functional areas:

Manufacturing and Integration
 
Provides senior leadership across production operations including structural fabrication, thermal protection systems, systems integration, testing, and final assembly for Blue Origin’s booster manufacturing. Responsible for establishing and maintaining process controls, driving production efficiency, and ensuring safe, repeatable spaceflight hardware delivery at all stages of the product lifecycle. This role will also provide leadership across integration operations supporting the assembly and verification of complex space systems, launch vehicles, and propulsion hardware. Accountable for coordinating cross-functional teams to ensure the safe, on-time integration of hardware in alignment with engineering requirements, mission assurance standards, and program milestones.

**Key Responsibilities:** 
Leaders across these functional areas are expected to:
 

* Lead and develop teams of Managers, Senior Managers, and Directors driving manufacturing and operations execution across space and propulsion programs
* Champion a culture of safety, quality, and continuous improvement across all functional teams
* Own departmental KPIs, budgets, staffing plans, and capital project portfolios
* Partner with Program Management, Site Leadership, and cross-functional stakeholders to meet production schedules and customer expectations
* Drive process definition, development, deployment, and improvement initiatives including Lean Manufacturing and root cause analysis
* Collaborate with engineering teams to advance Design for Manufacturability principles and accelerate the transition from development to production
* Implement and mature production frameworks that support world-class manufacturing capabilities
* Communicate and enforce mission assurance and safety principles throughout the organization
* Recruit, develop, coach, and mentor talent at all levels of the organization

 
**Minimum Qualifications:** 

* Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Manufacturing, Industrial, Aerospace, or Electrical Engineering, or equivalent experience
* 15 or more years of progressive experience in aerospace manufacturing or a closely related industry, such as launch vehicles, aircraft, spacecraft systems, or defense
* 5 or more years in a senior leadership role managing managers and large, cross-functional teams
* Demonstrated experience leading manufacturing and operations teams in fast-paced, complex environments

 

**Preferred Qualifications:** 

* Master's degree, MBA, or advanced degree in a relevant engineering or business field
* Prior experience in aerospace environments supporting space hardware, rocket propulsion, or other mission-critical, high-value components
* Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing, the Toyota Production System, or Six Sigma; Black Belt certification preferred
* Experience transitioning manufacturing capabilities from development and prototyping into full-rate production
* Knowledge of fabrication processes including machining, welding, composites, additive manufacturing, cleaning, and non-destructive testing
* Experience with facility activation, new production line startup, or multi-site manufacturing operations
* Proficiency with MRP/ERP, PLM, and Manufacturing Execution Systems

 

Base Pay Range for:

WA applicants is $203,165.00 - $284,430.30

**Other site ranges may differ**

 

**Culture Statement**

Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

 

**Export Control Regulations**

Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

 

**Background Check**

* Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical 

 

**Benefits**

* Benefits include: Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program.
* Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)
* Paid Time Off: Up to four (4) weeks per year based on weekly scheduled hours, and up to 14 company-paid holidays.
Dependent on role type and job level, employees may be eligible for benefits and bonuses based on the company's intent to reward individual contributions and enable them to share in the company's results, or other factors at the company's sole discretion. Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details. 

 

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

Blue Origin is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer and is committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly qualified and dedicated work force. Blue Origin hires and promotes people on the basis of their qualifications, performance, and abilities. We support the establishment and maintenance of a workplace that fosters trust, equality, and teamwork. We provide all qualified applicants for employment and employees with equal opportunities for hire, promotion, and other terms and conditions of employment, regardless of their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin/ethnicity, age, physical or mental disability, genetic factors, military/veteran status, or any other status or characteristic protected by federal, state, and/or local law. Blue Origin will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the Washington Fair Chance Act, the California Fair Chance Act, the Los Angeles Fair Chance in Hiring Ordinance, and other applicable laws.

Applicants wishing to receive information on Blue Origin’s Affirmative Action Plans, or applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation in order to participate in the application and/or interview process, please contact us at EEOCompliance@blueorigin.com . Please note this is a publicly managed inbox. Please do not include any personal medical information in your request.

role.title: Plant Manager
role.description:
**Purpose**
 
Under minimal supervisor, manages the daily, on-going production operations of an assigned plant(s). Oversees plant personnel providing guidance and direction to lower level management. Drives customer focused business strategy through maintaining optimal plant operation and accurate inventory management.
 
 
**Focus & Scope**
 
*Essential duties and responsibilities, i.e. those which are basic, necessary, and an integral part of the job, are indicated below:*

* Oversees the daily aggregate mining, processing and asphalt operations at an assigned plant(s).

* Manages assigned staff to include: hiring, training, and development. Determines workflow and staff priorities.

* Conducts business in a professional, legal and environmentally sound manner in adherence to company policies.

* Analyzes financial and operational plant performance including operating margin, cost, key production indicators, and inventory management.

* Administers short and long range plant planning, coordinates production schedules and costs, as well as plant flow evaluation, maintenance and inventory control.

* Ensures that plants are in good operating condition at all times and proposes changes and modifications as required. Maximizes efficiencies through systems and automation.

* Collaborates with the Engineering Department to develop capital expenditure analysis for plant improvements.

* Confers with sales personnel in preparation of annual sales budgets.

* Determines annual plant operating budget and manages to budget.

* Monitors union contracts for workforce and company compliance. May participate in union/company contract negotiations.

* Develops a Zero Injury culture by setting expectations, coaching behavior, and adhering to all company safety policies and practices.

 
**Qualifications, Requirements, & Competencies**
 
 
Education

* Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering, Construction Management or Business or an equivalent combination of training, education and experience.

 
Experience & Industry Expertise:

* A minimum of five (5) years of experience in an aggregate or asphalt environment or an equivalent combination of training and related experience. An advanced understanding of Aggregate plant operations and products.

 
Specific Job Requirements:

* Three (3) years experience managing staff.
* Must demonstrate ability to effectively lead, manage, coach, mentor and develop staff.
* Must demonstrate ability to formulate and implement new or improved processes, procedures or tactics.
* Must demonstrate ability to work in a fast-paced environment, prioritize and manage multiple assignments.
* Must demonstrate the ability to originate and drive operation initiatives, changes and enhancements.
* Must develop and maintain strong working relationships internally and externally with diverse groups of people.
* Must possess excellent verbal and written communications skills with the ability to speak, write and understand English at a proficient and understandable level.
* Must demonstrate the ability work well under pressure, remaining composed and professional. Must demonstrate strong organizational skills and time management practices.
* Must be able to maintain a high level of confidentiality.
* Must have advanced knowledge of computer software programs including Word, Excel and Outlook; familiar with department specific programs such as Oracle, JD Edwards and JWS.
* Must possess a valid California Driver License and must maintain an acceptable driving record when driving is a job requirement.

 
Competencies

* Building Successful Teams
* Safe Work Ethic
* Communication
* Judgment/Decision-Making
* Managing Complexity
* Strategic Thinking

 
**Physical Demands and Work Environment**

* Physical Demands: Employees occasionally may experience the following physical demands for extended periods of time: Viewing of computer monitor. Keyboarding; use of fingers to make small movements such as typing and mouse usage. Driving to plant sites, other offices or meeting sites. Position may require lifting of materials and equipment up to 10 lbs. May require walking on uneven ground, climbing, reaching, bending or stooping.
* Work Environment: Plant locations may contain dust, fumes, debris, medium to loud levels of noise and extreme weather conditions including excessive heat or cold and rain prevalent at times. Travel may be required to other locations, site facilities or educational seminars. Typical office environment with adequate temperatures and lighting, low levels of noise.

 
**BASE SALARY RANGE:**
 
$135,833.33 - $190,166.67
 
*The range displayed reflects the range the company reasonable expects to pay for the position. The actual base salary is subject to variation due to the role, level, geographic location, relevant education, training, or experience, among other factors.*

People Leadership

* Drives a culture of positive employee relations, including responsiveness to safety, employee relations issues, disciplinary actions, communicating clear expectations and accountability processes, demonstrating effective leadership presence.
* Develops direct reports and ensures tools are in place to develop staff and succession planning.

Customer Relationship

* Resolves escalated Customer issues from the sterilization process.

Delivering Results

* Ensures performance across a range of activities and metrics within their area at the facility/campus level
* Manage Safety Program to ensure safe working environment. No OSHA Recordable Injuries or Days

role.title: Plant Manager
role.description:
**Position Summary**

We are seeking a team-oriented, hands-on Plant Manager with a robust background in maintenance leadership. This role is responsible for overseeing all aspects of plant operations, with a particular emphasis on developing and executing a world-class maintenance program at our mill in St. Maries, Idaho. The ideal candidate will drive operational excellence, safety, and continuous improvement, ensuring the facility meets production goals while maintaining the highest standards of equipment reliability and team development.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead the plant’s manufacturing and maintenance operations, ensuring safe, efficient, and reliable production.
* Oversee preventive, predictive, and proactive maintenance programs, including planning, scheduling, and execution.
* Direct and develop a multidisciplinary team, including Maintenance Planners, Millwrights, Electricians, Mechanics, and Production Supervisors.
* Foster a “Safety First” culture, ensuring compliance with all safety and environmental regulations and serving as a role model for safe industrial behavior.
* Collaborate with other departments (Finance, HR, Sales, Marketing, Resources) to align plant performance with company goals and market demands.
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives, leveraging best practices in manufacturing and maintenance to optimize resources and processes.
* Lead and support improvement projects, including research, cost analysis, financial justification, and project management from conception to completion.
* Manage key performance indicators for maintenance and production, such as safety compliance, PM completion, downtime, overtime, expense controls, and plant cleanliness.
* Develop and retain high-performing teams through effective communication, training, and empowerment.
* Build strong relationships across the organization, ensuring active communication and teamwork.
* Utilize modern maintenance management tools (e.g., CMMS, AutoCAD, MS Suite) and interpret technical documents (e.g., blueprints).

**Qualifications**

* Proven experience in plant management or senior manufacturing leadership, with a strong track record in maintenance supervision and program development.
* Minimum of five years in maintenance leadership, with hands-on experience in preventive, predictive, and proactive maintenance.
* Strong technical skills in troubleshooting mechanical, electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, and strong understanding of PLC systems.
* Demonstrated ability to lead, motivate, and develop teams in a continuous improvement environment.
* Excellent analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
* Effective communicator, able to set clear expectations and drive accountability.
* Experience with process optimization.
* Business acumen to manage budgets, control costs, and justify investments.
* High school diploma required; college-level education in a related field preferred.

role.title: Plant Manager - Ready Mix Concrete - Plymouth, NC
role.description:
About the Opportunity:

Are you a proven leader who thrives on building strong teams and delivering exceptional service? At SRM Concrete, our Plant Managers are the driving force behind our commitment to operational excellence and customer satisfaction. As a Plant Manager, you’ll lead by example—empowering your team, optimizing daily operations, and ensuring every load meets the highest standards of safety, quality, and service.

If you’re passionate about leadership, logistics, and making a positive impact in your community, this is your opportunity to join a company that values integrity, teamwork, and growth.

Your Mission & Key Responsibilities:

* Lead with purpose: Inspire, coach, and develop your plant team to achieve operational excellence and deliver outstanding service to every customer.
* Oversee daily plant operations: Manage staff scheduling, load planning, and route optimization to ensure efficient and timely concrete deliveries.
* Champion customer service: Collaborate with drivers, dispatch, and sales teams to exceed customer expectations and resolve any issues with urgency and care.
* Drive performance: Implement and monitor key metrics to assess plant efficiency, productivity, and service quality.
* Foster a culture of safety: Ensure full compliance with safety regulations and company policies, creating a safe and positive work environment for all.
* Promote teamwork: Conduct regular meetings to review performance, address challenges, and celebrate successes.
* Build relationships: Develop strong connections with customers, suppliers, and SRM team members to support seamless operations.
* Contribute to growth: Participate in strategic planning and budgeting, sharing insights to enhance plant efficiency and profitability.

What Sets You Apart:

* Inspirational leadership style with a passion for developing high-performing teams.
* Commitment to delivering exceptional customer service and building lasting relationships.
* Strong organizational and problem-solving skills; able to prioritize and adapt in a fast-paced environment.
* Deep understanding of logistics, supply chain management, or plant operations—experience in the concrete or construction industry is highly valued.
* Proficiency with dispatch software, Microsoft Office Suite, and a willingness to learn new systems.
* Knowledge of DOT regulations and safety standards for transportation and delivery.
* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills; you build trust with team members, customers, and partners.
* Dedication to safety, quality, and continuous improvement.
* Willingness to undergo SRM’s pre-employment screenings.

About SRM:

SRM Concrete (Smyrna Ready Mix) is a family-owned, values-driven leader in the ready mix concrete industry. Founded in 1999 with a single plant in Smyrna, Tennessee, we’ve grown to over 600 locations nationwide by focusing on quality, integrity, and service. Our mission is to serve our customers, our communities, and our team members with excellence—every load, every day.Why Join SRM Concrete?

**Why Join SRM Concrete?**

* **Growth & Advancement:** Be part of a rapidly expanding company with real opportunities to grow your career.
* **Impact:** Lead a team that plays a pivotal role in building America’s future.
* **Competitive Pay & Exceptional Benefits:** Low-cost medical, dental, vision, STD, LTD, and life insurance; paid holidays; PTO/vacation; 401k with $100 weekly match; family days; and more!
* **Team Culture:** We value hard work, respect, and teamwork. We support each other, recognize a job well done, and believe in doing what’s right—on the job and in the community. You’ll find a straightforward, dependable environment where every team member matters.

At SRM Concrete, you’re more than a manager—you’re a valued team member helping to build America’s future. If you’re ready to say “YES” to new opportunities and deliver service that sets the standard in our industry, apply today and join the SRM family!

**Job Description:**

**JOB SUMMARY**

Owns overall site performance and full P&L responsibility for the plant. Accountable for delivering Safety, Quality, Customer Service, and Cost commitments while building the organization, systems, and continuous improvement capability required to scale the operation from commissioning through full-rate production.

**DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES**

**P&L & Cost Management**

* Owns the plant P&L: develops, proposes, and manages the annual operating and capital budgets; drives cost, margin, and productivity performance against plan and explains variances with corrective action plans.
* Reviews, proposes, and approves as appropriate plans controlling budget spending, labor efficiency, material efficiency, engineering effectiveness, and customer service.
* Reviews cost control reports, cost estimates, headcount utilization, and conversion cost per unit for the operation.
* Reviews and proposes projects involving functional or organizational changes within the operation; builds the business case and tracks realized benefit.

**Operations & Production Standards**

* Maintains production operations standards consistent with company and site Safety, Quality, Productivity, and Cost requirements in order to exceed customer expectations (annual plant objectives and monthly scorecard).
* Reviews performance against operating plans and standards; requires interpretation of results from direct reports and approves changes in direction of plans.
* Resolves priority conflicts across lines and ensures lines are balanced and performing according to planning system rules.

**Continuous Improvement & Growth**

* Drives volume growth and productivity improvement by implementing Lean and continuous improvement methodologies across coating, curing, digital print, and material handling operations.
* Develops short- and long-term plans and programs for plant growth, including capacity, staffing, and capital investment roadmaps.

role.title: Wastewater Treatment Plant Manager - Brightwater
role.description:
**Summary**
-----------

**This posting is open to all qualified candidates.**

 
 
 
 
Are you looking for an opportunity to lead a highly trained team of Operations and Maintenance (O&M) staff and be a part of creating the strategic direction for a complex wastewater system? The Wastewater Treatment Division (WTD) in King County (KC) is hiring a leader for the Brightwater Treatment Plant. This position will lead a team of 40 Operations, maintenance and Facilities staff, oversee the planning and processes for facilities maintenance of the Brightwater system, and be an active member of the O&M Leadership team.
 
 
Working for KC WTD provides you with a work-life balance and benefits to support you and your family. You will also gain opportunities for growth through training, conferences hosted by leaders in the industry, and working across functional groups within the Division.
 
 
We are looking for creative and innovative thinking that drives us to continuously improve public service. Tap into your desire to serve the public and discover new and better ways to make a meaningful impact by joining the WTD O&M Leadership team.
 
 
**About the Role:**
 
This is a leadership position and will serve on the Operations and Maintenance Section Leadership team. This team is responsible for the strategic planning of the section, developing leadership skills among our supervisors, providing growth opportunities for our staff, and implementing metrics to deliver key performance measures that contribute to the overall growth and success of WTD Operations and Maintenance.
 
 
In this role, the successful candidate will apply their skillset in the areas of planning, coordination, scope, budget, schedule management, monitoring and control, and reporting in the maintenance and development of the Brightwater Treatment System.
 
 
**About the Team:**
 
The Operations and Maintenance Section of the Wastewater Treatment Division is tasked with ensuring safe, environmentally protective wastewater treatment for King County, serving 34 wholesale customers and approximately 2.3 million residents. The Section includes five treatment facilities, 48 pump stations, 400 miles of conveyance piping and treats an average of 185MGD of wastewater. We are a clean water utility, recovering resources such as biosolids, recycled water and biogas, continually seeking new ways to capture beneficial uses of resources that would otherwise be lost.
 
 
WTD is committed to the principles of equity and social justice (ESJ). We value diverse perspectives and life experiences in our workforce and are committed to building a culturally diverse and inclusive environment. WTD strives to provide equitable services to residents and businesses across King County. Our department vision is to provide sustainable and livable communities and a clean and healthy natural environment that supports a prosperous and resilient economy. 
 
 

Join our team dedicated to ensuring clean water for generations to come! With over 1000 employees engaged in planning, designing, building, and operating treatment facilities, our agency is at the forefront of environmental stewardship. Success for us means upholding our legacy while promising future generations a pristine environment.

 
 

We partner with regulatory agencies to reduce harmful waste discharge and actively educate the public and businesses on water quality protection. We prioritize accountability to our ratepayers and operate a well-managed agency that services over 2.3 million King County residents. Our regional wastewater treatment system not only sustains a healthy environment but also fuels economic development, fostering prosperity in our region. If you're passionate about making a difference and thrive in a collaborative environment, join us in our mission to safeguard our precious water resources.

 
 

**Commitment to Equity, Racial and Social Justice:**

King County, named after Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr., is a diverse and vibrant community that represents cultures from around the world. We prioritize equity, racial and social justice, making it a foundational and daily expectation for all employees. As a Wastewater Treatment Plant Manager, you will actively apply these principles in all aspects of your work. Learn more about our commitment at http://www.kingcounty.gov/equity.

 
 

**Apply now for a rewarding career at the** **Wastewater Treatment Division** **of King County Department of Natural Resources & Parks (DNRP). Join our talented workforce in protecting and restoring the natural environment and promoting more resilient, sustainable, and equitable communities. Enjoy training,** **comprehensive benefits****, and growth opportunities.**

**Job Duties**
--------------

**What You Will Be Doing:**

* Lead Brightwater’s operations, maintenance, and facilities teams through supervisors and technical staff, establishing priorities, setting performance expectations, developing employees, and promoting a safe, inclusive, and accountable work environment.
* Oversee daily treatment operations and facilities maintenance to support reliable service, regulatory compliance, employee safety, and protection of public health and the environment.
* Direct maintenance planning and prioritize preventive and corrective work to improve equipment reliability, address operational risks, and preserve treatment plant assets.
* Participate in the Operations and Maintenance Section Leadership Team, developing and implementing strategic priorities, coordinating across teams, and using performance measures to evaluate results and guide improvements.
* Develop and monitor assigned operating budgets, evaluate staffing and resource needs, and recommend adjustments to support operational priorities and responsible stewardship of public funds.
* Coordinate with engineering, capital project, process, safety, and other support teams to ensure projects and facility changes address operating needs, maintainability, and readiness for service.
* Lead and coordinate the plant’s response to operational disruptions and emergencies in collaboration with section leadership and appropriate support teams.
* Manage employee and labor relations matters in coordination with Human Resources and Labor Relations, including interpreting and applying collective bargaining agreements, conducting fact-finding investigations, resolving conflicts, and recommending appropriate corrective action.

**Experience, Qualifications, Knowledge, Skills**
-------------------------------------------------

**Qualifications You Bring:**

* Experience in leading teams, including team building, building consensus, developing employees, and working effectively with a diverse team.
* Knowledge of the operation and maintenance of wastewater treatment and conveyance systems, including the regulations and requirements as they relate to operation and maintenance of these facilities.
* Knowledge of the principles and practices of engineering and systems operation.
* Knowledge of budget techniques and principles.
* Knowledge of project management principles and techniques.
* Knowledge of labor relations principles, practices, and techniques.
* Skill in writing and communicating technical and non-technical information; skill in reading and interpreting technical information and making presentations to non-technical and technical audiences.
* Knowledge of current and possible future policies, practices, trends, technology, and information affecting the wastewater treatment industry.

 
**Competencies You Bring:**

* **Manages Complexity**: Making sense of complex, high quantity, and sometimes contradictory information to effectively solve problems.
* **Decision Quality**: Making good and timely decisions that keep the organization moving forward.
* **Plans and Aligns**: Planning and prioritizing work to meet commitments aligned with organizational goals.
* **Collaborates**: Building partnerships and working collaboratively with others to meet shared objectives.
* **Values Differences**: Recognizing the value that different perspectives and cultures bring to an organization.
* **Builds Effective Teams**: Building strong-identity teams that apply their diverse skills and perspectives to achieve common goals.
* **Communicates Effectively**: Developing and delivering multi-mode communications that convey a clear understanding of the unique needs of different audiences.
* **Drives Engagement**: Creating a climate where people are motivated to do their best to help the organization achieve its objectives.
* **Racially Just**: Identify and replace racist systems and structures with anti-racists and pro-equity approaches.

 
**Required Licenses/Certifications:**

* Washington State Group IV Wastewater Operator’s license (or out-of-state equivalency) or ability to obtain within 6 months.
* Washington State Driver’s License or the ability to provide timely or emergency transportation to work locations with limited or no public transportation.
* Additional licenses, certifications and other requirements determined to be necessary to meet the business needs of the employing unit may be required.
 

 

**It Would Be Great If You Also Bring:**

* Proven ability to lead diverse teams, including union-represented employees.
* Experience aligning operations with organizational goals and environmental sustainability.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, including public presentations.
* Experience with performance management, coaching, and workforce development.
* Demonstrated experience with SCADA systems and process automation, preventive and predictive maintenance programs, Regulatory compliance (e.g., NPDES permits, EPA/State reporting, emergency response and disaster preparedness, budget development and capital improvement planning.

 
**Workplace Exposures:**

* The successful candidate will be working within a wastewater treatment plant and potentially exposed to biological hazards, high voltage, equipment that automatically starts and stops, chemicals, loud noise, and other environments typically found in an industrial setting.

**Supplemental Information**
----------------------------

**Working Conditions:**

* **Work Location****:** Brightwater Treatment Plant - 22505 State Route 9 SE, Woodinville, WA 98072.
* **Work Schedule:** This full-time position works a 40-hour work week. This position is exempt from the overtime provision of the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) and is not overtime eligible.
* **Union Representation****:** This position is represented by Teamsters 117 - WTD Section and Assistant Managers.

 
**Application Instructions:**
 
We welcome applications from all qualified applicants. We value diversity, diverse perspectives and life experience and encourage people of all backgrounds to apply.
 
 
Application materials will be screened for clarity, completeness and alignment with the experience, qualifications, knowledge, and skills essential for this role to determine which candidates may be invited to participate in a technical assessment and one or more panel interviews.
 
 
**Anticipated** **Timeline for this recruitment (dates subject to change):**

* Technical Assessment: **week of 12/7/26**
* Panel Interview: **week of 12/14/26**

 
To apply, submit a:
 

* **Complete Application**
* **Resume**
* **Cover Letter**
* **Responses to the supplemental questions**

Note: Additional documents won't be considered during minimum qualification screening.
 
 
**Discover More About the Wastewater Treatment Division**: Visit our **website**and check us out at **Facebook****,** **X (formerly Twitter)****,** **Instagram****,** **YouTube**, and the**WTD Blog****.**
 
 
**Discover More About DNRP: Visit our** **DNRP website****, explore an** **interactive map** **of our recent accomplishments and check us out at** **Facebook****,** **X (formerly Twitter)****,** **LinkedIn****,** **TikTok****,** **Instagram****,** **YouTube** **and** **Keeping King County Green News****.**
 
 
Sign up for Job Alerts to be notified of additional career opportunities with King County. Select the **Natural Resources** category for DNRP opportunities and explore other categories of interest. 
 

Are you ready to make a difference? Come join the team dedicated to serving one of the nation's best places to live, work and play.

**Application Process:**

If you are interested in pursuing this position and supporting King County’s vision for unified, equitable, and high-performing government, please follow the application instructions carefully. Provide us with your work history as applicable, ensuring that you provide details that highlight your ability to fulfill the requirements for this position.

If you need this announcement in an alternate language or format, or you would like to request accommodation or assistance in the application or assessment process, please contact Rodney Dungo at rdungo@kingcounty.gov.

**King County's Vision, Mission, and ACTIVATE Values unite us.**

King County serves residents with a relentless sense of urgency, delivering on commitments with transparency and accountability. We are action-oriented, creative problem solvers who collaborate across roles, engage directly with communities, and challenge the status quo to achieve meaningful impact. As a unified team, we uphold high ethical and stewardship standards, embrace change, stay curious, and continuously improve. Across all interactions, we listen first, act quickly, and stay aligned as a team to earn and sustain public trust. Learn more about our Vision, Mission, and ACTIVATE Values **here** and visit our Why work at King County page **here**.

**King County is an Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) Employer**

No person is unlawfully excluded from employment opportunities based on sex, race, color, national origin, ethnicity, religious affiliation, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age except by minimum age and retirement provisions, pregnancy, status as a family caregiver, parental status, marital status, military status or status as a veteran who was honorably discharged or who was discharged solely as a result of the person's sexual orientation or gender identity or expression, citizenship or immigration status, genetic information, or other protected class. However, to the extent that distinction or differential treatment on the basis of citizenship or immigration status is authorized by either federal or state law, regulation, or government contract, it is not an unfair practice.
