role.title: VP, Global Operations
role.description:
About Oshkosh AeroTech, an Oshkosh company 
 
 Oshkosh AeroTech is a leading provider of aviation ground support products, gate equipment and airport services to commercial airlines, airports, air-freight carriers, ground handling and military customers. Oshkosh AeroTech offers products that make a difference in people’s lives by supporting those in our communities who do some of the toughest work. They own many of the most trusted brands in the air transportation industry, including LEKTRO®, JetAire®, JetPower®, AmpTekÔ, Jetway®, and more. 
 
 
 The Oshkosh AeroTech Vice President, Operations will lead operational strategy, execution, and continuous improvement across the Ground Support Equipment (GSE) and Jetway businesses. With dual reporting to the VP of Global Operations & Supply Chain at the Vocational segment and the President of Oshkosh AeroTech, this role is a key member of the Oshkosh AeroTech leadership team, responsible for driving a safety culture, operational efficiency, increasing capacity, manufacturing excellence, and overall business performance.
 
 YOUR IMPACT 
 Safety & Operations Leadership 
 Develop, implement, and sustain a world-class safety program that prioritizes team member well-being
 Drive a proactive safety culture by embedding safety into all operational activities, ensuring every team member understands and takes ownership of safety responsibilities.
 In collaboration with VP, Operations & Supply Chain at Vocational segment, develop and implement a comprehensive operations strategy aligned with business objectives.
 Establish KPIs to measure and drive operational performance, efficiency, and cost optimization.
 Lead continuous improvement initiatives in production, workflow optimization, and resource allocation.
 Ensure world-class manufacturing capabilities, leveraging Lean, Six Sigma, and automation best practices.
 Develop and implement strategy to increase capacity across AeroTech manufacturing sites.
 Partner with Supply Chain organization to optimize supplier partnerships and inventory management.
 Drive cost reduction initiatives while maintaining high quality and regulatory compliance.
 
 Quality & Compliance
 Ensure all operational processes comply with industry standards, safety regulations, and quality control frameworks.
 Implement best-in-class operational processes to reduce defects, improve reliability, and enhance customer satisfaction.
 Drive adherence to ISO and other relevant regulatory requirements.
 
 Financial Management
 Manage budgets, operational expenditures, and capital investments to drive profitability.
 Conduct financial analyses to improve operational decision-making and efficiency.
 Optimize cost structures through strategic sourcing, automation, and process improvements.
 
 Leadership & Talent Development
 Build, mentor, and develop a high-performing operations team.
 Foster a culture of safety, continuous improvement, accountability, and cross-functional collaboration.
 Partner with Human Resources on workforce planning and development initiatives to align with business growth and expansion.
 
 MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS 
 Bachelor’s degree in Business, Operations Management, Engineering, or related field.
 12+ years of experience in operational leadership, with at least 3 years in a VP or Director-level role.
 Experienced people leader with cross-functional collaboration and stakeholder management skills.
 Strong experience in multi-site manufacturing, supply chain management, and logistics.
 Proven track record in driving operational excellence, lean manufacturing, and six sigma methodologies.
 Strong financial acumen, data-driven decision-making, and process optimization skills.
 Lives the Oshkosh Core Values of We put people first, We do the right thing, We persevere, We are better together
 Demonstrates the Oshkosh Leadership Traits of Inspires Vision and Purpose, Drives Results, Customer Focus, Cultivates Innovation, Fosters Engagement, and Instills Trust
 
 STANDOUT QUALIFICATIONS 
 Master’s degree in business administration, Engineering, or a related field.
 Experience working with government, military, or defense contracts.
 International or global business experience.
 #LI-TM1
 
 
 Pay Range: 
$189,800.00 - $370,200.00 
 
 The above pay range reflects the minimum and maximum target pay for the position across all U.S. locations. Within this range, individual pay is determined by various factors, including the scope and responsibilities of the role, the candidate's experience, education and skills, as well as the equity of pay among team members in similar positions. Beyond offering a competitive total rewards package, we prioritize a people-first culture and offer various opportunities to support team member growth and success. 
 
 
 Oshkosh is committed to working with and offering reasonable accommodation to job applicants with disabilities. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to disability for any part of the employment process, please contact us at corporatetalentacquisition@oshkoshcorp.com. 
 
 Oshkosh Corporation is a merit-based Equal Opportunity Employer. Job opportunities are open for application to all qualified individuals and selection decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or other protected characteristic. To the extent that information is provided or collected regarding categories as provided by law it will in no way affect the decision regarding an employment application. 
 
 Oshkosh Corporation will not discharge or in any manner discriminate against employees or applicants because they have inquired about, discussed, or disclosed their own pay or the pay of another employee or applicant. However, employees who have access to the compensation information of other employees or applicants as a part of their essential job functions cannot disclose the pay of other employees or applicants to individuals who do not otherwise have access to compensation information, unless the disclosure is (a) in response to a formal complaint or charge, (b) in furtherance of an investigation, proceeding, hearing, or action, including an investigation conducted by the employer, or (c) consistent with Oshkosh Corporation's legal duty to furnish information.
 
 Certain positions with Oshkosh Corporation require access to controlled goods and technologies subject to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations or the Export Administration Regulations. Applicants for these positions may need to be "U.S. Persons," as defined in these regulations. Generally, a "U.S. Person" is a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident, or an individual who has been admitted as a refugee or granted asylum.

role.title: Quality Assurance Director
role.description:
**Quality Assurance Director – Folding Carton Packaging**

Carton Service CSI, LLC | Shelby, OH | Full-time, salaried (exempt) | On-site with occasional travel

**About Us**

Our site runs a food safety management system built to the SQF Food Safety Code (Edition 9). To learn more about us, visit www.cartonservice.com.

**The Role**

Reporting to the President, the Quality Assurance Director leads quality assurance across all our carton production. You'll make sure our products meet customer specifications and expectations, keep our quality and food safety systems current, and drive cost-effective quality improvements as a key contributor to our strategic plans.

**What You'll Do**

* Lead and develop the QA team and oversee the plant quality system
* Review and approve customer specs, and make sure CSI procedures are followed
* Conduct and document internal, supplier and customer audits, manage our FSC and IMS certifications, and serve as backup SQF Practitioner
* Champion GMPs for food-contact packaging, from low-migration inks to hygiene
* Represent us with customers and suppliers, and partner with internal departments, including Sales and Production

**What You Bring**

* College education in a related field (bachelor's degree preferred)
* 5+ years experience working in a GFSI Certified production plant, preferably packaging
* Proven success leading teams, including cross-functional teams
* Strong communication skills with associates, customers, suppliers and regulators
* Organized and results-driven, able to manage multiple priorities and people

**Nice to Have**

* Experience with SQF, BRCGS or another GFSI food safety program
* FSC chain-of-custody or IMS program experience

role.title: IT Director of Quality Assurance
role.description:
**ABOUT ETHOS & THE OPPORTUNITY**

Ethos Risk Services is a leading insurance claims investigation and medical management company focused on delivering better data, technology, and insights that help our clients make better decisions. We are continuing to invest in our technology organization and are seeking an experienced engineering leader to help scale how software is built, tested, and delivered.

We are seeking a **full-time Director of Quality Assurance** to own software quality across Ethos, overseeing an outsourced QA team and the processes, tooling, environments, and metrics that prevent defects from reaching production. Our ideal candidate is an experienced, results-driven QA leader who will establish a consistent defect lifecycle, reduce defect aging, implement effective root cause analysis and preventive measures, and improve the reliability of test environments. Within their first year, they will standardize QA tools and processes, integrate AI-based solutions into daily QA operations and performance tracking, and establish a comprehensive KPI framework that drives measurable improvements in software quality, efficiency, and accountability.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* **Lead Outsourced QA Operations:** Direct the day-to-day activities of an outsourced QA team of 8 to10 resources, establishing priorities, performance expectations, and accountability for quality deliverables.
* **Manage Vendor Performance:** Oversee vendor agreements, SLAs, staffing, onboarding, and performance evaluations. Address performance gaps through corrective action and ensure effective knowledge transfer and documentation.
* **Drive Defect Management:** Establish and enforce standardized defect tracking, classification, prioritization, and resolution processes. Lead regular defect triage with engineering and product teams to manage backlogs and identify quality risks.
* **Prevent Production Issues:** Lead structured root cause analysis of production defects, identify recurring failure patterns, and implement preventive measures through improved test coverage, regression testing, and quality gates.
* **Oversee Test Environments:** Partner with DevOps to maintain stable, production-representative QA, staging, and UAT environments, including configuration standards, test data management, and environment availability.
* **Define QA Strategy & Standards:** Develop and continuously improve QA processes across manual, automated, regression, integration, performance, and user acceptance testing to strengthen quality and consistency.
* **Advance Test Automation:** Evaluate and implement QA tools and automation frameworks, integrating automated testing into CI/CD pipelines to improve testing efficiency, coverage, and release reliability.
* **Leverage AI-Enabled QA Tools:** Apply AI-based solutions to test generation, defect classification, failure analysis, workload management, and performance monitoring. Evaluate emerging tools and implement solutions that deliver measurable improvements while maintaining appropriate security and accuracy controls.
* **Establish Quality KPIs:** Define and monitor performance metrics, including defect escape rates, resolution times, automation coverage, recurring production incidents, test effectiveness, and vendor SLA adherence.
* **Deliver Executive Reporting:** Produce monthly quality reports and quarterly reviews for the VP of Engineering and CTO, translating performance data into actionable insights, risks, trends, and recommendations.
* **Support Release Readiness:** Collaborate with engineering, DevOps, IT Delivery Leads, and Technical Product Owners to integrate QA into sprint and release planning, assess release quality, and recommend readiness for deployment.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

**Education:** Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience (required).

**Required Experience:**

* 8 to 10 years of progressively greater responsibility in software quality assurance.
* 3 to 4 years in a QA management role leading teams and managers.
* Proven expertise in defect lifecycle management, root cause analysis, and preventive quality practices.
* Hands-on experience establishing and maintaining test environments and test data management practices.
* Strong working knowledge of QA tooling, such as test management (e.g., Xray, Zephyr, TestRail), defect tracking (e.g., Jira, Azure DevOps), and automation frameworks (e.g., Selenium, Playwright, Cypress).
* Practical experience using AI-based tools in QA or team management, and enthusiasm for expanding their use.
* Experience defining QA KPIs and producing executive-level monthly and quarterly reporting.
* Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines and integrating automated testing into delivery workflows.

**Preferred Experience:**

* Performance, security, or API testing, and a regulated-industry background.
* Certifications: ISTQB Advanced or Test Manager, CSQE, or similar.
* Experience with data visualization or dashboard tools (e.g., Power BI, Tableau)

**WORKING AT ETHOS**

This is a 100% remote U.S.-based role, offering the flexibility to work from home while remaining closely connected to a collaborative leadership team. Our ideal candidate is available during EST standard business hours. Occasional travel may be required for quarterly or annual leadership meetings and company events.

**Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States and must not require current or future employment sponsorship.**

**Benefits include:** Paid Time Off and Sick Time **|** Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance **|** Short-Term + Long-Term Disability Insurance + Life Insurance **|** 401(k) Matching **|** Employee Referral Bonus Program

At Ethos, you'll have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact, shape the future of our engineering organization, and help build the systems and processes that support our next stage of growth. **To learn more about Ethos, visit our website:** https://ethosrisk.com/about-us/

*Ethos Risk Services is an equal opportunity employer and considers qualified applicants without regard to any characteristic protected by applicable law.*

role.title: Quality Director
role.description:
**Quality Director**

**Brunswick Hospital Center (Inpatient Behavioral Healthcare)**

**Amityville, NY**

**Position Summary**

The Quality Director provides strategic leadership for Brunswick Hospital Center’s quality management and performance improvement program. This role is responsible for analyzing trends, identifying systems issues, and driving organization-wide improvement using data provided by the Incident Management / Clinical Risk team.

The position maintains a clear separation of duties so that special investigations and Justice Center case management remain the responsibility of the Incident Management team. The Quality Director ensures alignment with OMH, Joint Commission, CMS, and Justice Center expectations at the systems level.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

**Quality and Performance Improvement**

* Develop and lead the hospital’s annual Quality and Performance Improvement Plan.
* Design and oversee systems for collecting, analyzing, and reporting quality and incident trend data.
* Chair the Performance Improvement Committee and ensure follow-through on improvement projects.
* Partner with department leaders to establish measurable quality goals and monitor progress.
* Track the implementation and effectiveness of Corrective Action Plans (CAPs) across the organization.
* Support organizational review of sentinel events and high-risk events through systems analysis and monitoring of resulting improvements.

**Collaboration with Incident Management**

* Receive completed investigation findings and case-specific data from the Clinical Risk / Incident Management team.
* Use this information for systems-level analysis and improvement without conducting or duplicating investigations.
* Ensure special investigations and Justice Center case management remain the responsibility of the Incident Management team.

**Compliance and Reporting**

* Prepare and submit required quality and performance improvement reports to internal leadership, the Board, and external agencies (OMH, CMS, Joint Commission) as applicable.
* Ensure timely and accurate reporting of quality indicators, trend data, and improvement outcomes.
* Monitor compliance with regulatory reporting timelines and documentation standards related to quality and performance improvement.
* Maintain documentation demonstrating the effectiveness of the quality program for surveys and audits.
* Coordinate the hospital’s response to quality-related findings from external reviews, ensuring corrective actions are tracked to completion.

**Survey Readiness and Regulatory Compliance**

* Coordinate survey readiness activities and maintain ongoing compliance with Joint Commission, CMS, OMH, and related standards.
* Serve as a liaison with OMH on quality and performance improvement matters (distinct from day-to-day incident reporting and Justice Center investigations).
* Oversee systems-level tracking and trending of patient complaints and grievances.

**Leadership and Communication**

* Facilitate communication of quality data and improvement initiatives to medical staff, leadership, and the Board.
* Identify and recommend resources, training, and process changes needed to sustain a culture of safety and continuous improvement.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in nursing or a related field required; Master’s degree preferred.
* Current RN or NP licensure in New York preferred; other advanced clinical or quality credentials (e.g., CPHQ) considered.
* Minimum of 5 years of progressive quality, performance improvement, or risk management experience in a behavioral health or hospital setting.
* Demonstrated experience with Joint Commission or CMS survey readiness.
* Strong data analysis, presentation, and facilitation skills.
* Experience working with OMH or Justice Center expectations at a systems/compliance level preferred.
* Prior supervisory or leadership experience preferred.

* Benefits offered. Salary commensurate with experience.

role.title: Vice President of Quality
role.description:
**Overview**

The Vice President of Quality provides strategic leadership and oversight of all quality functions, ensuring products and manufacturing processes meet customer requirements, applicable quality standards, and company expectations. This position is responsible for developing and executing the company's quality strategy, maintaining an effective quality management system, driving continuous improvement, and ensuring customer satisfaction.

The VP of Quality partners with executive leadership and cross-functional teams to improve manufacturing performance, reduce quality-related costs, resolve complex quality issues, and establish a culture of accountability and operational excellence.

Direct semiconductor manufacturing experience is required. The successful candidate must have 10–15 years of progressive quality experience, including experience in semiconductor equipment manufacturing, with a demonstrated ability to lead quality initiatives and deliver measurable improvements in product quality, process performance, and customer satisfaction.

**Duties**

- Develop and implement the company's quality strategy, objectives, and improvement initiatives in alignment with business goals.

- Provide executive leadership and oversight for all Quality department functions, personnel, systems, and processes.

- Establish, implement, and maintain an effective quality management system in accordance with applicable ISO standards, customer requirements, and industry standards.

- Ensure products and manufacturing processes meet established specifications, customer expectations, and applicable quality requirements.

- Serve as a senior point of contact for customer quality concerns, escalations, audits, corrective actions, and quality performance reviews.

- Manage root cause analysis, corrective and preventive actions, and continuous improvement initiatives to prevent recurring quality issues.

- Establish and monitor key quality performance indicators, identify trends, and implement improvement plans to reduce defects, scrap, rework, and quality-related costs.

- Partner with Operations, Engineering, Production, and other departments to resolve manufacturing issues and improve process consistency.

- Oversee internal and external quality audits, supplier quality performance, nonconformance management, and compliance activities.

- Ensure appropriate quality resources, inspection equipment, measurement systems, work instructions, and technical documentation are available and maintained.

- Build, lead, and develop a high-performing Quality organization with clear performance expectations, accountability, and development plans.

- Promote a culture of quality, teamwork, continuous improvement, and shared responsibility across the organization.

- Report quality performance, significant risks, customer concerns, and improvement initiatives to executive leadership.

- Evaluate quality risks and make sound decisions using technical analysis, available data, customer impact, and business priorities.

- Identify opportunities to improve process efficiency, reduce waste, and optimize the use of company resources.

- Maintain effective communication and coordination among Quality, Manufacturing, customers, and suppliers.

- Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

Required Knowledge and Skills

- Extensive knowledge of quality assurance, quality engineering, quality management systems, and manufacturing process controls.

- Direct knowledge and experience with semiconductor manufacturing quality requirements and production processes.

- Strong understanding of statistical process control (SPC), process capability studies, metrology, statistical analysis, root cause analysis, and corrective and preventive action methodologies.

- Experience implementing quality systems, managing audits, and driving continuous improvement.

- Ability to interpret technical specifications, engineering drawings, inspection requirements, and manufacturing documentation.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to evaluate complex issues and implement effective solutions.

- Proven ability to lead cross-functional teams, influence stakeholders, and establish accountability throughout an organization.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present technical findings and quality performance to executive leadership, customers, and employees.

- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and quality reporting and data analysis tools.

- Ability to balance customer expectations, product quality, operational efficiency, and business objectives.

Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, or a related technical field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

- 7–10 years of progressive quality engineering and quality leadership experience, including direct experience in semiconductor equipment manufacturing.

-Black belt or Green belt certification.

- Semiconductor manufacturing experience is mandatory. General manufacturing quality experience alone does not meet this requirement.

- Demonstrated experience leading quality functions or significant quality initiatives within a semiconductor manufacturing environment.

- Experience with manufacturing process controls, defect reduction, root cause analysis, corrective and preventive actions, and continuous improvement.

- Experience managing customer quality requirements, customer and supplier audits, nonconformances, and corrective action programs.

- Proven ability to lead and develop teams, establish strategic priorities, and deliver measurable improvements in product quality and customer satisfaction.

- Strong leadership, organizational, communication, and decision-making skills.

**Responsibility for Work of Others**

Provides executive leadership and oversight for the Quality department, including Quality managers, supervisors, engineers, inspectors, and other quality personnel, as applicable. Establishes departmental objectives, assigns responsibilities, evaluates performance, and ensures adequate staffing, training, and resources to meet company and customer requirements.

**Additional Information**

This job description is intended to describe the general nature and level of work performed in this position. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, or qualifications. Additional responsibilities may be assigned as business needs require.

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* Dental insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Health insurance
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

**Job Title** 
Plant Manager (Angleton, TX)

**Collaborate with Innovative 3Mers Around the World**

Choosing where to start and grow your career has a major impact on your professional and personal life, so it’s equally important you know that the company that you choose to work at, and its leaders, will support and guide you. With a diversity of people, global locations, technologies and products, 3M is a place where you can collaborate with other curious, creative 3Mers.

**The Impact You’ll Make in this Role** 
As a Plant Senior Manager you will have the opportunity to tap into your curiosity and collaborate with some of the most innovative and diverse people around the world. Here, you will make an impact by:

 

* EHS stewardship and compliance to ensure operational Environmental, Health, and Safety compliance and accountability. EHS active visible leadership, ownership, and involvement within all operations.
* Driving strategic planning and budgeting to drive sustainable improvements in factory cost through application of continuous improvement, entitlement thinking, yield improvement, and plant productivity.
* Managing supply chain execution and inventory management to ensure appropriate customer value stream performance through responsiveness, delivery performance, LTA, capacity management, supplier management, and appropriate inventory management including working and non-working inventory.
* Accelerating value creation for our customers through responsive end-to-end supply chain performance and prompt resolution to customer inquiries
* Developing manufacturing strategies for a high-performance workforce, capital equipment planning, technology advancement, and employee and leadership development.
* Championing inclusive programs that create a great place to work for all our employees

**Your Skills and Expertise**

* Bachelor's degree or higher (completed and verified prior to start) from an accredited institution
* Four (4) years of supervisory and/or management experience in a private, public, government or military environment
* Five (5) years of manufacturing experience in a private, public, government or military environment

* Experience managing and/or supervising direct reports
* Demonstrated strong leadership ability and history of leading high-performance teams

role.description:
Linde Advanced Material Technologies Inc.

**Plant Manager**

Ellisville, MS, United States | req34514

**What you will enjoy doing\***

* Lead the Ellisville manufacturing operation with full accountability for Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost (SQDC), while ensuring customer commitments and business objectives are consistently achieved
* Build and develop a high-performing leadership team by setting clear expectations, coaching managers and supervisors, strengthening accountability, and developing organizational capability and succession
* You will drive the PGT Lean Operating System through daily management, leader standard work, visual management, structured problem solving, standard work, and continuous improvement
* Be a visible leader on the shop floor, working with teams at the source to identify problems, remove barriers, strengthen process discipline, and ensure corrective actions address root causes and are sustained
* Improve operational performance and reliability by strengthening equipment performance, first-pass yield, flow, WIP, productivity, capacity, and on-time delivery while maintaining uncompromising safety and quality standards
* Develop and execute the site strategy, aligning workforce, training, equipment, materials, capital, and capacity with customer demand, growth priorities, and long-term business requirements
* Own the financial performance of the facility, including budgets, labor efficiency, overtime, productivity, cost improvement, operational spending, and capital priorities
* Also, you will lead cross-functionally and create a strong site culture, partnering with Operations, Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Maintenance, EHS, Human Resources, and Finance while fostering respect, transparency, employee engagement, urgency, and continuous improvement

**What makes you great**

role.title: Manufacturing Plant Manager - CT
role.description:
**Job Summary:**

The Plant Manager is responsible for leading all day-to-day manufacturing operations at the site, ensuring safe, efficient, and high-quality production. This role owns execution of production, cost, delivery, and safety performance, while aligning with corporate standards across quality, engineering, supply chain, and HR. The Plant Manager drives operational discipline, team performance, and continuous improvement to deliver consistent, predictable results.

 

**Company Overview:**

PTA Plastics, an employee-owned and innovative leader in the plastic injection molding, contract manufacturing and tool-building industry, is looking for a Plant Manager to join our dynamic team.

At PTA Plastics, we’re more than just a manufacturer; we partner with Fortune 500 OEMs in the medical device, defense, homeland security, and technology sectors, constantly pushing the boundaries of product development and manufacturing excellence. As an employee-owned company, every team member has a stake in our success, creating a collaborative and entrepreneurial environment where innovation thrives.

**Pay:** $150,000 - $190,000 annually

 

**Essential Duties/Responsibilities:**

**Site P&L Performance**

* Own site-level financial performance

* Deliver budgeted profitability, labor efficiency, and cost targets

* Control overtime, scrap, and operating expenses

 

**Production & Operational Execution**

* Lead all day-to-day plant operations

* Ensure schedule attainment and on-time delivery

* Drive production efficiency, uptime, and throughput

* Remove operational roadblocks quickly

* Lead and resolve customer escalations at the plant level

 

**Safety & Compliance**

* Own plant safety performance

* Ensure compliance with OSHA, environmental, and company standards

* Drive a proactive, behavior-based safety culture

 

**People Leadership & Culture**

* Lead and develop plant leadership team and floor personnel

* Drive accountability, performance management, and clear expectations

* Build a high-performance, no-excuses culture

 

**Execution of Corporate Quality Standards**

* Ensure adherence to corporate Quality Management System (QMS)

* Support and enforce corrective actions

* Hold production teams accountable for quality at the source

 

**Execution of Corporate Engineering Standards**

* Maintain schedule discipline and production alignment with planning

* Resolve plant-level material and supply issues

* Support inventory control and flow

 

**Cross Functional Alignment**

* Corporate Quality

* Corporate Engineering

* Corporate Supply Chain

* Corporate HR

 

**Continuous Improvement**

* Lead Lean and continuous improvement initiatives

* Reduce scrap, downtime, and inefficiencies

* Improve labor utilization and Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE)

 

**Qualifications & Requirements:**

#### **Education & Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in Manufacturing, Engineering, Operations Management, Business, or a related field required (or equivalent combination of education and experience)
* 7–10+ years of manufacturing experience, preferably in injection molding or a similar high-volume, process-driven environment
* 3–5+ years of leadership experience managing production teams and plant operations
* Proven track record of delivering results in:
 + Production output and schedule attainment
 + Cost control and labor efficiency
 + Safety and quality performance
* Experience leading in a metrics-driven environment (OEE, scrap, uptime, etc.)
* Hands-on experience with Lean manufacturing, continuous improvement, and waste reduction initiatives
* Experience working within structured corporate environments with cross-functional support (Quality, Engineering, Supply Chain, HR)
* Familiarity with ERP/MRP systems and production planning processes

#### **Technical & Industry Knowledge**

* Strong understanding of manufacturing operations, including production processes, workflow optimization, and plant performance metrics (OEE, uptime, scrap, labor efficiency)

* Working knowledge of injection molding processes, materials, tooling, and secondary operations (or similar high-volume manufacturing processes)

* Understanding of maintenance and reliability principles, including preventive maintenance and equipment uptime optimization

* Experience with Lean manufacturing, continuous improvement, and waste reduction methodologies (5S, Kaizen, standard work, etc.)

* Knowledge of quality systems and practices, including root cause analysis, corrective actions, and adherence to QMS standards (ISO or similar)

* Familiarity with production scheduling, capacity planning, and inventory flow within an ERP/MRP environment

* Understanding of workplace safety standards and regulatory compliance (OSHA, environmental requirements)

* Ability to interpret and act on operational data to drive performance improvements

 

**Physical Requirements:**

* Ability to stand, walk, and move around the production floor for extended periods.
* Capable of lifting and carrying heavy objects weighing up to 50 pounds.
* Manual dexterity and hand-eye coordination for handling small tools, machine components, and molds.
* Ability to work in a fast-paced environment and adapt to changing priorities.
* Comfortable wearing personal protective equipment (PPE) such as safety glasses, gloves, and ear protection.
* Occasional bending, kneeling, and reaching to access equipment and perform maintenance tasks.
* Good vision and color perception for inspecting parts and identifying any defects or abnormalities.
* Ability to work in temperature-controlled environments and withstand exposure to noise levels associated with manufacturing machinery.
* Ability to receive, comprehend and utilize required training from OSHA and Company including but not limited to the following:
* Hazard Communication
* Lock Out/Tag Out

 

**ITAR Requirements:** To conform to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), 8 U.S.C. § 1324b(a)(3), applicants for employment at PTA Plastics must be a U.S. citizen or national, lawfully admitted for permanent residence into the U.S. (i.e., current green card holder), or lawfully admitted as a refugee or granted asylum under 8 U.S.C. § 1157-1158.

 

**Equal Employment Opportunity & ADA Compliance Statement****:**

PTA Plastics is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all individuals, including those with disabilities. As part of this commitment, PTA Plastics complies with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA)andConnecticut’s Fair Employment Practices Act (CFEPA)**,** which prohibit discrimination against individuals with disabilities in hiring, job assignments, promotions, compensation, benefits, training, and other aspects of employment.

 

If you require a reasonable accommodation to participate in the application or interview process or to perform the essential functions of this position, please contact HR@ptaplastics.com. Reasonable accommodations will be provided in accordance with applicable laws to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential job duties.

 

This job description is intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. It is not an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required. Employees may be required to perform other duties as assigned.

role.title: SR. Manager Human Resources, Manufacturing (People & Culture)
role.description:
**Job Description Summary:**

At The Coca-Cola Company, our people and culture are essential to how we create value, grow our business, and make a difference every day. We are looking for a **Senior Manager, Human Resources-People & Culture (Manufacturing)** who will bring strong business partnership, sound judgment, and hands-on People & Culture leadership to two manufacturing locations supporting both union and non-union associates.

 

This role is the Primary **People & Culture Leader and** visible face of **Human Resources at the plant** , serving as a trusted partner to plant leadership and an accessible resource for associates. The Senior Manager will report directly to the Plant Manager, with a dotted-line relationship to the Director, People & Culture, helping ensure strong alignment between plant priorities and broader People & Culture strategies, standards, and practices.

 

Success requires someone who can move comfortably between the plant floor and leadership discussions. You will listen to associates, coach leaders, navigate complex employee and labor relations matters, use workforce insights to inform decisions, develop talent, and translate business priorities into practical people solutions. The ideal candidate brings manufacturing Human Resources experience, labor relations capability, strong business acumen, a commitment to inclusion, and the ability to build credibility and trusted relationships at every level of the organization.

 

**Key Responsibilities and Position-Related Functions**
-------------------------------------------------------

* Serve as the senior on-site People & Culture partner for two manufacturing locations, providing hands-on leadership and support across union and non-union associate populations.
* Partner directly with the Plant Manager and plant leadership teams to translate operational and business priorities into actionable workforce, talent, culture, and organizational initiatives.
* Serve as the primary, visible People & Culture resource for associates, creating an approachable and trusted presence across shifts and levels of the organization.
* Coach and advise plant leaders on organizational effectiveness, leadership capability, performance management, accountability, employee development, workforce decisions, and people-related business challenges.
* Lead and support employee relations matters with objectivity, consistency, confidentiality, sound judgment, and appropriate partnership with the Director, People & Culture and other subject-matter experts.
* Support labor relations within the unionized location, including interpretation and consistent application of the collective bargaining agreement, issue resolution, grievance processes, and development of productive labor-management relationships.
* Partner with leaders to promote a positive, inclusive, safe, and respectful workplace where associates can contribute, grow, and thrive.
* Lead workforce planning discussions, using workforce data and operational insights to identify talent needs, retention risks, organizational opportunities, and appropriate actions.
* Strengthen leader capability in performance management, associate engagement, development conversations, conflict resolution, and consistent application of People & Culture practices.
* Partner with leaders on talent reviews, succession planning, career development, critical-role planning, and development opportunities that build plant capability.
* Support recruiting and selection activities in partnership with Talent Acquisition and plant leaders, including workforce requirements, candidate assessment, pre-employment activities, and an effective transition from candidate to associate.
* Lead and continuously improve new-hire onboarding and integration, helping new associates understand performance expectations, workplace culture, policies, resources, and ways of working.
* Provide guidance to associates and leaders on pay, benefits, leave, workplace policies, Human Resources programs, systems, and processes, engaging appropriate partners when specialized expertise is required.
* Analyze turnover, attendance, staffing, engagement, workforce demographics, and other people data to identify trends and translate insights into practical recommendations for plant leadership.
* Apply digital tools, automation, and artificial intelligence responsibly to improve People & Culture insights, efficiency, associate experience, and decision-making while maintaining appropriate confidentiality and data stewardship.
* Ensure People & Culture practices and documentation are consistent with company policies, applicable collective bargaining agreements, and employment and labor requirements.
* Maintain accurate and appropriate associate records, documentation, systems, and reporting, with a strong focus on data integrity and confidentiality.
* Partner closely with the Director, People & Culture, keeping them informed of material plant activities, emerging workforce risks, labor and employee relations matters, and issues requiring escalation or broader functional support.
* Lead or support People & Culture programs, change initiatives, communications, events, and projects that strengthen organizational effectiveness and the associate experience across both locations.
Build effective partnerships across the broader People & Culture network and plant functions to solve problems, implement change, and deliver sustainable business and people outcomes. 

 

**Education and Qualifications**
--------------------------------

* Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Industrial or Labor Relations, Organizational Development, or a related field.
* 7+ years of progressive Human Resources experience, with meaningful experience supporting manufacturing, supply chain, distribution, or another complex operational environment.
* Demonstrated experience supporting both **union and non-union employee populations** , including practical knowledge of labor relations, collective bargaining agreements, grievance management, and consistent contract administration.
* Experience serving as a trusted Human Resources partner to senior operational leaders and translating business priorities into effective people solutions.
* Strong employee relations capability, including experience evaluating complex workplace situations, conducting or supporting investigations, resolving conflict, managing risk, and determining when escalation or specialist partnership is appropriate.
* Strong working knowledge of employment practices, labor relations principles, performance management, leave practices, and Human Resources policy interpretation.
* Experience supporting hourly and salaried populations and building credibility with associates and leaders across multiple organizational levels and work schedules.
* Demonstrated capability in workforce planning, talent management, succession planning, associate engagement, organizational effectiveness, and leader development.
* Strong data literacy with the ability to interpret workforce metrics, identify meaningful trends, develop insights, and use evidence to influence business decisions.
* Digital fluency across Human Resources information systems and productivity platforms; experience with UKG/Kronos or comparable workforce management technology is preferred.
* Practical understanding of responsible artificial intelligence use and an ability to identify opportunities to apply digital and AI-enabled solutions to People & Culture work while protecting confidential associate information.
* Strong communication, coaching, influencing, facilitation, conflict-resolution, and relationship-building skills.
* Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities, exercise sound judgment, maintain confidentiality, and make timely decisions in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
* Ability to lead through change, navigate ambiguity, and build alignment among stakeholders with different perspectives and priorities.
* Demonstrated commitment to fostering an inclusive workplace in which associates are treated with dignity and respect and have opportunities to contribute and develop.
* Ability to build productive partnerships across two locations while maintaining a strong, visible presence with plant leadership and associates.
Human Resources professional certification, such as SHRM-CP, SHRM-SCP, PHR, or SPHR, is valued but not required. 

The Coca-Cola Company will not offer sponsorship for employment status (including, but not limited to, H1-B visa status and other employment-based nonimmigrant visas) for this position. Accordingly, all applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis and must not require The Coca-Cola Company's sponsorship to continue to work legally in the United States.

**Skills:**

Analytics Insights, Human Resources Policies, Human Resources Training, Leadership, Strategic Human Resources Leadership, Waterfall Model

**Pay Range:**

United States: 130,000 - 147,000 USD


*Base pay offered may vary depending on geography, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. A full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits, dependent on the position, is offered.*

**Location(s):**

United States of America

**City/Cities:**

Ontario

**Travel Required:**

00% - 25%

**Relocation Provided:**

No

**Job Posting End Date:**

November 27, 2026

**Our Purpose and Growth Culture:**

We are taking deliberate action to nurture an inclusive culture that is grounded in our company purpose, to refresh the world and make a difference. We act with a growth mindset, take an expansive approach to what’s possible and believe in continuous learning to improve our business and ourselves. We focus on four key behaviors – curious, empowered, inclusive and agile – and value how we work as much as what we achieve. We believe that our culture is one of the reasons our company continues to thrive after 130+ years. Visit Our Purpose and Vision to learn more about these behaviors and how you can bring them to life in your next role at Coca-Cola.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and do not discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment because of race, color, sex, age, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, status as a veteran, and basis of disability or any other federal, state or local protected class. When we collect your personal information as part of a job application or offer of employment, we do so in accordance with industry standards and best practices and in compliance with applicable privacy laws.

role.title: Senior Manager Quality and Safety
role.description:
Site: Newton-Wellesley Hospital

Mass General Brigham relies on a wide range of professionals, including doctors, nurses, business people, tech experts, researchers, and systems analysts to advance our mission. As a not-for-profit, we support patient care, research, teaching, and community service, striving to provide exceptional care. We believe that high-performing teams drive groundbreaking medical discoveries and invite all applicants to join us and experience what it means to be part of Mass General Brigham.

**Job Summary**

The Sr. Manager in this role will oversee the execution of MGB strategy, processes, and infrastructure for the domains of safety, risk and PFR. This role oversees a team of safety, risk, and PFR specialists to support the implementation of standardization of best practices and a system strategy. This role will collaborate with site leadership to execute long and short-term goals for Risk Management, Patient Safety programs, and Patient and Family Relations. 
 
Does this position require Patient Care? 
No 
 
Essential Functions 

* Support the build out of safety/risk/PFR infrastructure, ensuring standardization in training, processes, and safety responses that are in line with MGB.

 

* Executes the MGB safety plans including those around event analysis, safety event reporting/management/mitigation.

 

* Implement the standardized risk management strategy, policies, and procedures, ensuring that risk management activities both align to and augment our approach to patient safety.

 

* Implement the system-wide safety event reporting system.

 

* Support as needed for system wide safety events such as recalls, shortages, and other events that impact safety.

 

* Understand data provided by the system team and use knowledge of local practices to identify areas of opportunity for improvement of patient safety as well as communicate to the system areas that are at risk.

 

* Execute the MGB quality and clinical compliance strategy within local site ensuring adherence to MGB standardized processes around quality measurement, strategy, prioritized areas, and performance improvement while also providing critical feedback about issues and needs that are arising within local site.

 

* Liase as needed with local site Risk/Safety/PFR leader to create prospective solutions and performance improvement as a result of safety events. Partner with safety team as needed prospectively to create performance improvement in pursuit of harm avoidance.

 

* Senior local site manager responsible for Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement QAPI planning and documentation, and updates as needed for board quality committee/patient care assessment committee.

 

* Serve as the senior local site administrative manager covering compliance activities at local site, ensuring adherence to local site standardized processes around tracer activity, site level preparedness activities, and measuring/monitoring compliance.

 

* Understand data provided by the system team and use knowledge of local practices and culture to identify areas of opportunity for improvement as well as communicate to the system areas which are at risk.

 

* Provides strong bi-directional communication between the system and the site, with accountability for distribution of organization communication (including pertinent data and analytics) from MGB to local site and vice versa.

**Qualifications**

Education Bachelor's Degree Related Field of Study required or Bachelor's Degree Patient Safety Leadership required and Master's Degree Nursing preferred Can this role accept experience in lieu of a degree? No Licenses and Credentials Experience Safety, Risk Management, and patient family relations. 3-5 years required and Leading process improvement and initiatives and managing teams. 3-5 years required Knowledge, Skills and Abilities - Support the build out of safety/risk/PFR infrastructure, ensuring standardization in training, processes, and safety responses that are in line with MGB. - Executes the MGB safety plans including those around event analysis, safety event reporting/management/mitigation. - Implement the standardized risk management strategy, policies, and procedures, ensuring that risk management activities both align to and augment our approach to patient safety. - Implement the system-wide safety event reporting system. - Support as needed for system wide safety events such as recalls, shortages, and other events that impact safety. - Understand data provided by the system team and use knowledge of local practices to identify areas of opportunity for improvement of patient safety as well as communicate to the system areas that are at risk.

**Additional Job Details (if applicable)**

**Remote Type**

Hybrid

**Work Location**

2014 Washington Street

**Scheduled Weekly Hours**

40

**Employee Type**

Regular

**Work Shift**

Day (United States of America)

**Pay Range**

$99,465.60 - $144,643.20/Annual

**Grade**

8 
At Mass General Brigham, we believe in recognizing and rewarding the unique value each team member brings to our organization. Our approach to determining base pay is comprehensive, and any offer extended will take into account your skills, relevant experience if applicable, education, certifications and other essential factors. The base pay information provided offers an estimate based on the minimum job qualifications; however, it does not encompass all elements contributing to your total compensation package. In addition to competitive base pay, we offer comprehensive benefits, career advancement opportunities, differentials, premiums and bonuses as applicable and recognition programs designed to celebrate your contributions and support your professional growth. We invite you to apply, and our Talent Acquisition team will provide an overview of your potential compensation and benefits package.

**EEO Statement:**

4100 Newton-Wellesley Hospital is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religious creed, national origin, sex, age, gender identity, disability, sexual orientation, military service, genetic information, and/or other status protected under law. We will ensure that all individuals with a disability are provided a reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. To ensure reasonable accommodation for individuals protected by Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, the Vietnam Veteran’s Readjustment Act of 1974, and Title I of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, applicants who require accommodation in the job application process may contact Human Resources at (857)-282-7642.

**Mass General Brigham Competency Framework**
---------------------------------------------

At Mass General Brigham, our competency framework defines what effective leadership “looks like” by specifying which behaviors are most critical for successful performance at each job level. The framework is comprised of ten competencies (half People-Focused, half Performance-Focused) and are defined by observable and measurable skills and behaviors that contribute to workplace effectiveness and career success. These competencies are used to evaluate performance, make hiring decisions, identify development needs, mobilize employees across our system, and establish a strong talent pipeline.

role.title: Sr. Manager Operations
role.description:
**Job Description**

**Ingram Content Group (ICG)**is hiring a **Sr. Manager Operations** to support our **Distribution** team in **Jackson, TN**. The Sr. Manager, Operations manages the daily operations of an assigned area within the Distribution Center and serves as a key partner to the Director, Operations. This role collaborates with the Director on hiring, safety and security, maintenance and repairs, non-product purchasing, and strategic planning to ensure customer service levels and commitments are achieved, while maintaining a zero-error environment.

Want to join a key team that helps the world read?

At Ingram, the Operations team serves a key role within the organization. We ensure that our distribution centers and manufacturing facilities function at maximum efficiency. Safety is a core value in our operations environment. We emphasize this through training, education, and accident prevention programs. Process Improvement is another core value, and through innovations such as voice and Radio Frequency (RF) technologies, as well as feedback from our associates, we work toward constant improvement.

The world is reading, and it is our goal to connect as many people as possible to the content they want in the simplest ways. If you want to be part of a customer-centric team that strives for excellence, collaboration, innovation, we can’t wait to meet you!

**Schedule:**

* Monday-Friday, first shift, with flexibility to work weekends, additional hours, and provide on-call support as business needs require.

**What You’ll Need:**

* College degree OR HS diploma or GED with directly related year-for-year experience
* 6 years’ experience in a high-volume distribution center OR production/manufacturing facility with a clear track record of success
* 5 years’ experience supervising at least 25 or more employees

**What You’ll Do:**

* Achieve and maintain full working knowledge of all aspects of the assigned operation
* Implement a fast-paced, lean distribution system; drive the delivery of products and orders on time.
* Oversee KPIs, goals, and objectives for the management team; set clear goals and expectations for Managers and Area Managers, measure performance, provide feedback, and hold leaders accountable.
* Build a passionate team with a positive, inclusive, results-oriented culture; mentor and develop leaders and staff; manage staff selection and development, ensuring associates are fully trained and cross-trained on systems and procedures.
* Develop, manage, and lead continuous process improvement strategies and initiatives; leverage Lean, Six Sigma, and Performance Improvement tools to enhance productivity.
* Provide strategic-level/long-term planning (3, 6, and 12 months out), including labor planning, rate forecasting, and peak season planning.
* Work closely with support functions (HR, Maintenance/Engineering, Safety, IT, and other leaders) to build and secure support and resources for projects and initiatives.
* Ensure customer service levels exceed requirements and standards; works with management to improve cost-per-unit (CPU)/cost-per-line (CPL) while providing outstanding customer service.
* Collaborate with Senior Management in the planning, development, and launch of processes and strategies for the site; review competitive information and visit other companies to bring in new ideas on operations.
* Oversee the supervision of the operations area, ensuring the timely and accurate movement of materials into and out of the facility.
* Monitor and execute company policies and procedures for HR-related issues, including associate attendance, timekeeping, and performance reviews.
* Control and manage budget costs for all assigned departments/areas.

**Essential Physical Demands:**

* Ability to walk and stand as needed
* Ability to grip/grasp as needed
* Ability to lift/carry in full range of motion up to 60lbs as needed
* Ability to push/pull in a warehouse environment up to 70lbs force to push as needed
* Ability to bend, squat/kneel, twist/turn, climb, crawl, reach above shoulder, and type/keyboard frequently
* Ability to work a flexible which could include nights and weekends
* Ability to travel as needed
* Exposure to wide range of temperatures

*Hiring Salary Range: $113,201k - $143,945k. This range represents the anticipated low and high end of the salary for this position. It will be determined by factors including but not limited to: the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, geographic location, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.*

 **Additional Information**

**Perks/Benefits:**

* A highly competitive compensation package with generous benefits beginning first day of employment for Medical/Prescription Drug plans, HSA, Vision, Dental and Health Care FSA.
 + 15 vacation days & 12 sick days accrued annually and 3 personal days
 + 401K match, Life and AD&D, Employee Assistant programs, Group Legal, & more
* Encouraged continued education with our tuition reimbursement program
* Financial and in-kind opportunities to engage with non-profits in your community
 + Company match program for United Way donations
 + Volunteer opportunities and in-kind drives for non-profits throughout the year
* Casual Dress Code

The world is reading, and Ingram Content Group (“Ingram”) connects people with content in all forms. Providing comprehensive services for publishers, retailers, libraries and educators, Ingram makes these services seamless and accessible through technology, innovation and creativity. With an expansive global network of offices and facilities, Ingram’s services include digital and physical book distribution, print-on-demand, and digital learning. Ingram Content Group is a part of Ingram Industries Inc. and includes Ingram Book Group LLC, Ingram Publisher Services LLC, Lightning Source LLC, Ingram Library Services LLC, Tennessee Book Company LLC, Ingram Content Group UK Ltd. and Ingram Content Group Australia Pty Ltd.

*All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, work related mental or physical disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or genetic information.*

* *EOE-Race/Gender/Veterans/Disabled*
* *We participate in EVerify.*
* *EEO Poster in English*
* *EEO Poster in Spanish*

role.title: Regional Director of Operations
role.description:
Circle of Life is growing, and we have an opening for a Regional Director of Operations to join our team. This position will oversee and manage our New Mexico branches; Albuquerque, Gallup, Kirtland, Shiprock, and Zuni.

**Good for employees**

Circle of Life’s focus is creating a workplace where respect, appreciation and teamwork are the shared experiences of our team. We do good for our employees by collaborating on scheduling, a focus on wellbeing, a client-first directive, respecting and valuing every team member, having fun along with top industry compensation and benefits.

**Good deeds**

We also do good in our work. Our team of office and field staff care about each other and the clients we serve. We help one another. We care and provide for a wide range of patients with a focus on serving the underserved.

**Position duties include**

* Participate in the hiring and training of managers
* Organize and oversee the work and schedules of managers
* Conduct performance evaluations
* Handle discipline of employees as needed following company policy
* Establish quantitative and qualitative metrics, guidelines, and standards by which the company's efficiency and effectiveness can be evaluated (identify opportunities for improvement)
* Implement policies and procedures that will improve day-to-day operations
* Oversee office operations, ensuring each branch is reaching goals set by departmental and company leadership
* Monitors budget and revenue in each office to achieve financial objectives
* Communicates and explains new directives, policies/procedures to manager for change and meets with staff to explain changes, answer questions, and maintain morale
* Improve customer service and satisfaction
* Market current products to potential clients, families, case workers and potential referral sources
* Leads coordination and integration of efforts among homecare teams to produce smoother workflow and more cost-effective business processes
* Traveling is required

**Qualifications**

Qualified applicants will have 3 years of management experience, excellent verbal and written communication skills and interpersonal and customer service skills. Healthcare and/or home care experience preferred. The Regional Director of Operations oversees the day-to-day activities for their assigned branches, ensuring the organization is managed and performing efficiently and effectively. While carrying out the responsibilities of the position, ensure the values of servant-leadership, empathy, altruism, and integrity are evident in all actions and encounters.

**How good?**

* Positively change the lives of individuals and families in our communities
* Serve the underserved providing access to care for those who have been traditionally overlooked by the health care system
* Support a talented team of administrative and clinical professionals and be a part of a team that supports each other

**Full Benefits include**

* Medical, Dental, 401K, Paid Holidays, Top PTO Plan, Mileage, Flexible Schedules, Vision, Year-End Bonus

role.title: Head of Quality Assurance Operations
role.description:
About David AI
David AI is the first audio data research company. We bring an R&D approach to data–developing datasets with the same rigor AI labs bring to models. Our mission is to bring AI into the real world, and we believe audio is the gateway. Speech is versatile, accessible, and human—it fits naturally into everyday life. As audio AI advances and new use cases emerge, high-quality training data is the bottleneck. This is where David AI comes in.

David AI was founded in 2024 by a team of former Scale AI engineers and operators. In less than a year, we’ve brought on most FAANG companies and AI labs as customers. We recently raised a $50M Series B from Meritech, NVIDIA, Jack Altman (Alt Capital), Amplify Partners, First Round Capital and other Tier 1 investors.

Our team is sharp, humble, ambitious, and tight-knit. We’re looking for the best research, engineering, product, and operations minds to join us on our mission to push the frontier of audio AI.


About our Data Operations team
Our Data Operations team powers David AI's Data Factory, transforming raw audio into high-quality training datasets for leading AI labs. Our mandate is to spin up new data pipelines and run them at a massive scale. This means starting from a model capability we want a model to unlock, experimenting with different shapes of data and collection strategies, and validating them with researchers. Once an approach works, we industrialize it, building pipelines that can process audio with reliability, quality, and efficiency. We are relentless operators who thrive in ambiguity, equally comfortable prototyping novel workflows as we are managing large-scale production systems.


About this role
As Head of Quality Assurance Operations, you'll own quality for every dataset David AI ships including but not limited to conversational, TTS, and transcription data, and manage David AI’s relationships with the global contingent workforce, comprising independent contractors and vendor-supplied contributors. You'll report to the Head of Operations and be located in the US.


In this role, you will

 - Own the quality bar across all data ops, including quality standards, calibration, consistency and on-time delivery of datasets

 - Design the quality review structure, organized by language and region, so every dataset gets consistent quality coverage

 - Audit and review the quality of delivered work product across languages, keeping quality benchmarks consistent globally

 - Run quality in languages you don't speak through deliverables from native-speaker and cross-language gold sets

 - Plan capacity against production ramps and own contingent workforce sourcing across many countries, ensuring each engagement is structured and classified correctly under local law

 - Build and own dashboards for quality, throughput, and cost efficiency

 - Manage David AI’s relationships with staffing vendors, service providers, and employer-of-record partners
 

Your background looks like

 - 7 to 10+ years in operations, including 3+ in senior leadership roles

 - You've run quality operations for large contingent workforce networks across multiple countries

 - You've owned quality at scale, across calibration, capacity planning, and spend efficiency

 - You built the system yourself, from tooling to contingent workforce sourcing at scale

 - Speech, audio, or linguistic data experience is a strong plus


VISAS

We sponsor international candidates across several visa types, including H-1B transfers, H-1B1, O-1, E-3, and TN. We also hire candidates on STEM OPT. If you’re on OPT, we’ll want to confirm you have a path to one of the visas listed above before your OPT ends. While we can’t guarantee any individual outcome, we’ve successfully sponsored teammates from all over the world.

role.title: Sr. Manager, Advanced Manufacturing Engineering
role.description:
MicroAire Surgical Instruments LLC 
 
 As a part of the global industrial organization Marmon Holdings—which is backed by Berkshire Hathaway— you’ll be doing things that matter, leading at every level, and winning a better way. We’re committed to making a positive impact on the world, providing you with diverse learning and working opportunities, and fostering a culture where everyone’s empowered to be their best. 
 
 
Leads Advanced Manufacturing initiatives across supply chain, sustaining engineering, manufacturing engineering, and process development for existing and new mechanical and electromechanical products. Serves as a technical advisor in researching and implementing manufacturing technology and is responsible for assigned elements of new product development under MicroAire Design Controls Procedures. Manages the technical and personnel aspects of facilities maintenance and provides technical leadership in areas critical to MicroAire’s success. 
 
 + Essential Duties and Responsibilities 

 • Drives the planning and execution of critical Advanced Manufacturing projects for insourcing, automation, and continuous improvement, including cost savings, delivery, and quality.
 • Leads or coaches critical continuous improvement, Lean, kaizen, and Blue Belt projects. Coordinates corporate CI tracking and planning, drives the site CI calendar, and tracks and reports savings.
 • Supports Supply Chain in the technical aspects of insourcing, alternative sourcing, supplier quality, and supplier continuous improvement. Supports business initiatives such as repairs and service programs.
 • Participates and makes recommendations regarding departmental quarterly plans and performs all essential duties and responsibilities within the company’s mission, vision and values.
 • Develops career paths for direct reports.
 • Provides guidance to manufacturing engineering for new highly critical products and oversees facilities maintenance activities within cross-functional teams consistent with departmental goals and objectives.
 • Oversees Engineering activity around investigation and root cause analysis for failures observed in the field that needs Engineering support.
 • Serves as the specialized technical expert resource for all project teams for manufacturing engineering projects.
 • Provides leadership by taking initiative for existing product modifications.
 • Provides guidance on Design For Manufacturing during New Product Development process.
 • Interfaces with all departments within the company as well as consultants, vendors, surgeons, and others as required to ensure quality, efficacy, and timely completion of directed projects.
 • Proactively works with team members to achieve established goals, budgets and timelines.
 • Monitors department budgets closely and takes all necessary actions to ensure budget alignment.  Identifies capital needs for production and facilities to provide CapEx recommendations.
 • Collaborates with department heads to develop and update engineering standard operating procedures.
 • Ensures project compliance with all applicable laws and regulations, especially U.S. FDA regulations and EU Medical Device Regulation supporting Regulatory group.
 • Researches and analyzes facility requirements and manufacturing capabilities / capacities around potential acquisition opportunities.
 • Provides technical training for engineering and operations personnel. Provides systems training to other functional areas as necessary.
 • Identifies Advanced Manufacturing Engineering needs and communicates these needs to Senior Management.
 • Manages facilities maintenance activities through prioritization of safety, health and production needs.
 • Identifies safety issues in the immediate work environment and other work areas and recommends solutions for improvement.
 • Ensures engineering and facilities maintenance activities are in compliance with Quality System requirements.
 • Ensures facility maintenance activities are also in compliance with OSHA and other applicable health and safety standards.
 • Performs other related duties as required.
 Authority and supervision: Directly manages Facility Maintenance and mentors junior engineers. Reviews and approves project team work and exercises sound business judgment, recognizing that errors may significantly affect the company.

 + Education and Experience 

 Education Requirements: Bachelor’s in Mechanical Engineering or applicable degree.
 Experience Requirements:  8-10 years of Engineering (Manufacturing & Design) experience supporting products in post market phases of product lifecycle.  3- 5 years of leadership experience.  Five years in medical device industry desirable.

 Job knowledge skills and abilities 

 • Proficiency in 2D drafting and 3D modeling, preferably AutoCAD and SolidWorks.
 • Knowledge of ANSI Y14.5 drafting standards.
 • Expertise in properties of various materials, such as stainless steel, aluminum and plastics.
 • Expertise in part fabrication techniques, such as machining and injection molding.
 • Expertise in the factors that affect the life of re-usable surgical instruments, such as corrosion, wear and thermal cycling.
 • Thorough understanding of part tolerancing and tolerance stack-up analysis.
 • Thorough understanding of mechanical stress analysis.
 • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, Project and other job associated software.
 • In depth understanding of regulatory requirements for medical device design control and manufacturing.
 • In depth understanding of various surgical techniques as related to surgical instruments.
 • Ability to apply scientific reasoning and to develop test methodologies to resolve complex technical problems.

 + Competencies 

 Advanced Manufacturing and Technical Leadership 
 Skills: Automation, insourcing, manufacturing processes, design for manufacturing, mechanical analysis, and root cause investigation. 
 Behaviors: Leads manufacturing initiatives from planning through implementation; guides technical decisions and resolves complex product and process issues using evidence. 

 Program Execution and Business Acumen 
 Skills: Project planning, risk and milestone management, budget control, CapEx evaluation, and cost savings analysis. 
 Behaviors: Sets priorities, coordinates resources, anticipates risks, and delivers projects within agreed budgets and timelines; connects investment decisions to business results. 

 People Leadership and Cross Functional Collaboration
